findings.title: A 'skipped' run_boot_stage result is rendered as a successful migration (page D) — 'ลองใหม่' after a rollback and the disk-space gate both show fake success with the plan's counts
findings.scenario: First-time migration fails validate → rollback → `_save_state({'rolled_back_for_version': app_version})`. User clicks 'ลองใหม่' (boot_flow_window.py:2108) → run_migration → run_boot_stage hits auto_migrate_boot.py:633 `if st.get('rolled_back_for_version') == app_version: return _done('skipped', 'previously-rolled-back')` → `_outcome_from_result`: reports=[] so failing is None and `ok=True` → page D 'ตรวจสอบครบ 0 ขั้น — ไม่มีข้อมูลหาย', 'ย้ายขึ้นโครงใหม่ N รายการ (…)', 'ลบไฟล์ขยะ N รายการ' — nothing was migrated, data is still v1, and the wizard comes back next boot. Same for `skipped/disk-space` (auto_migrate_boot.py:635) on a nearly-full disk: the user is told the migration finished. The retry button therefore can never actually retry within the same app version.
findings.evidence: boot_flow.py:901 `ok = result.action in ("applied", "pending_applied", "skipped") and failing is None`; 949-951 `promoted=list(plan.promote_items) if plan else []` … `junk_deleted=len(plan.junk_items) if (plan is not None and ok) else 0`; terminal renderer (boot_flow_terminal.py:110-122) prints the same success block.
findings.fix: Treat `action == 'skipped'` with a non-None plan as `ok=False` (error=result.reason, data_intact=True, promoted/archived/junk_deleted empty) or add a distinct 'skipped' outcome the window renders as 'ไม่ได้ย้าย: <reason>'; on the failed page hide/disable 'ลองใหม่' when `load_state().get('rolled_back_for_version') == __version__` and point to `takkub migrate apply`.

findings.title: GUI boot never runs auto_migrate_boot.run_boot_stage() on a fully-migrated (v2) install → version-marker never re-pinned, new ladder steps and drift-repair never applied (prod proof: marker stuck at 2.1.0 while venv is 2.1.31)
findings.scenario: Every normal boot of an installed cockpit: wizard → _proceed_to_migration_check → plan_migration() returns None because layout_state()=='v2' (boot_flow.py:345) → `_on_plan_ready(None)` just `accept()`s. `run_migration()` (the only wizard-side path into run_boot_stage → apply_pending) is reachable solely from page B's start button (_start_migration), which never shows on a v2 machine. auto_migrate_boot.run_boot_stage's own contract (lines 610-622) says apply_pending() MUST run on 'v2' every boot to re-pin `version-marker` after each upgrade and pick up ladder steps added later; only the TAKKUB_BOOT_UPDATE=0 path (app.py:1046) still does that. Consequences: VersionMarkerStep.validate() (core/migration/steps.py:76-84, `existing.get('app') == APP_VERSION`) is false forever → `takkub migrate validate`/`doctor --storage-layout` report a mismatch after every release; any step added after the first migration never applies; the wizard's 'previous_version' text (`_read_previous_app_version`, `_previous_app_version`) shows 2.1.0 instead of the real previous build.
findings.evidence: boot_flow_window.py:2221-2223 `if isinstance(plan, _WorkerError) or plan is None:` → `self._proceed = True` / `self.accept()`; grep shows run_migration( is called only at boot_flow_window.py:169 (_MigrationWorker) and boot_flow_terminal.py:347. Prod (read-only): C:/Users/monch/.agent-takkub/system/version.json has `"component": "app", "version": "2.1.0"` (mtime 2026-09-11 21:33) while venv/Lib/site-packages holds agent_takkub-2.1.31.dist-info; no projects.json/custom-roles.json/.takkub_issues.json/v2 at the prod root → layout_state()=='v2'; events.log line 1431 (2026-09-22T19:53:56) `boot_phase gate_start wizard: true`.
findings.fix: In `_proceed_to_migration_check`'s worker (or in `_on_plan_ready` when plan is None) call `auto_migrate_boot.run_boot_stage()` (via `flow.run_migration(None)`) before `accept()`, mirroring app._run_auto_migrate_headless; log its BootMigrationResult.action/reason to boot.log. `takkub migrate run` (CLI) already does this and would repair prod's marker today.

findings.title: Boot wizard's worker QThreads are parented to a QDialog that run_boot_flow_gate drops on return → 0xC0000409 abort whenever the gate exits with a worker still running (X/Esc during provider check, #640 deadline, Ctrl+C)
findings.scenario: User launches the cockpit, sees 'กำลังตรวจสอบอัพเดต provider…' and clicks the X (or presses Esc): closeEvent/reject only guard PAGE_MIGRATING (lines 2236, 2249), so done() emits flowFinished(True), loop.exec() returns, MainWindow is built (2412) and the local `wizard` is garbage-collected while `_CallWorker` (check_provider_updates: up to 5 `--version` + 3 `npm view`, 15/30 s caps) is still running → Qt qFatal 'QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running' → process dies right after the main window appears. Same abort for the #640 deadline (2362-2379): it fires on ANY page, including page C mid-migration (footer itself says 2–5 min vs 180 s default), builds MainWindow while `_MigrationWorker` is still copying (panes then write into RUNTIME_DIR mid-ladder) and aborts at frame exit. Same for Ctrl+C via _poll_quit → sys.exit(0) unwinding the frame. tests/test_boot_flow_window.py:1565 stubs start() so no worker ever exists — the 'wedged stage still opens the cockpit' test never exercises a live worker.
findings.evidence: Workers parented to the dialog: line 2148 `worker = _CallWorker(lambda: flow.check_provider_updates(30.0), self)`, 2162, 2207, 2215, and 1540 `worker = _MigrationWorker(self._flow, signals, self)`; gate holds no ref after `return main_window_factory()` (2412). Reproduced with this venv's PyQt6: a Python-owned QObject parent with a running child QThread dropped at function return → exit code -1073740791 (0xC0000409) before the next print. events.log on prod confirms boots go through the wizard (`"phase": "gate_start", "wizard": true`).
findings.fix: Keep the wizard alive past the gate (module-level ref or parent it to the QApplication) and `wait()`/`quit()` every entry in `_workers` before returning; give workers no parent (hold them in `_workers`) so dialog teardown can't delete them; never fire the deadline while `_stack.currentIndex() == PAGE_MIGRATING` (re-arm it on each progress event instead); on _poll_quit, stop workers before sys.exit.

findings.title: Claude Auth override (base_url/api_key/extra_env) silently ignored: pane reads it from the curated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, Settings saves it to the base profile dir
findings.scenario: User opens Settings → Claude Auth, sets a base URL + API key (or extra env) for a profile, respawns panes of any real project (project != 'default', TAKKUB_SKILL_GATE unset/1 = default). spawn_engine.py:3342-3343 sets env['CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR'] to the curated dir (pane_env.py:544-545 → user_profile.curated_config_dir_for), then spawn_engine.py:3413 apply_claude_auth_overrides(env) does `config_dir = env.get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")` → load_claude_auth(<curated>/takkub-claude-auth.json) → file absent → blank ClaudeAuthConfig → pane keeps OAuth login; nothing in the UI says why.
findings.evidence: claude_auth_config.py:177-178 `config_dir = env.get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR") or None` / `env.update(load_claude_auth(config_dir).active_env())`; settings_window.py:3797 saves via `self._users_auth_dir(profile_name)` = the profile's base config_dir; user_profile.py:853-860 ensure_curated_claude_config_dir mirrors only `.credentials.json, settings.json, settings.local.json, keybindings.json, CLAUDE.md` — grep for `takkub-claude-auth|_AUTH_FILENAME` finds no mirror anywhere in src.
findings.fix: Either add `_AUTH_FILENAME` to the mirror list in ensure_curated_claude_config_dir (user_profile.py:853), or make apply_claude_auth_overrides resolve the BASE profile dir (user_profile.config_dir_for(project)) instead of the pane's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; add a test that spawns with the curated dir active and asserts ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL lands in env.

findings.title: load_projects() fail-open to an empty registry is persisted by the next writer (set_open_tabs/clear_active_project) → every project wiped from the V2 registry
findings.scenario: Post-#504 the V1 projects.json is archived, so the V2 registry is the only copy. If one read of registry.json fails transiently (OSError/PermissionError from an AV/backup tool holding the file, or a UnicodeDecodeError), load_projects logs a warning and returns `empty` ({"active": None, "projects": {}}). The user then closes/opens/reorders a tab → main_window.py:1358 set_open_tabs → `data = load_projects()` (empty) → known=set() → cleaned=[] → save_projects_json writes `registry["data"] = {"active": None, "projects": {}, "open_tabs": []}` over the real registry. Next boot: zero projects, no V1 fallback. clear_active_project (config.py:834-836) has the same shape. Rare trigger, unrecoverable outcome.
findings.evidence: config.py:642-644 `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:` / `_log.warning(...)` / `return empty`; config.py:862-874 `data = load_projects()` … `data["open_tabs"] = cleaned` / `save_projects_json(data)`; config.py:666-667 `registry["data"] = data` / `return _write_json_atomic(registry_path, registry)`
findings.fix: Make load_projects distinguish 'file exists but unreadable' from 'no file' (raise or return a sentinel), and have save_projects_json/set_open_tabs/clear_active_project refuse to persist when the read did not succeed (or when the new document has zero projects while the on-disk one had some).

findings.title: V2 account override clobbers the curated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (#563 skill gate) on every claude spawn
findings.scenario: User opens any real project with the claude provider (V2 router is default-ON, TAKKUB_SKILL_GATE unset). spawn_engine.py:3343 `inject_curated_claude_config_dir` sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to DATA_HOME/providers/claude/<profile>-<slug> (curated skills + filtered enabledPlugins), then spawn_engine.py:3349 `_apply_v2_account_env_override` calls `resolve_account_for('claude', ...)`; no V2 pool exists so the legacy fallback (facade.py:71-77) returns the raw profile and `account_env_overrides` (providers/plan.py:51-60) writes CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR back to the profile's base dir. Result: the curated dir is built on every spawn (disk work) but never used; every pane (Lead + teammates) loads the full user-level skills/plugins again, so the #563/#580 skill gate is silently off.
findings.evidence: This Lead pane: env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=C:/Users/monch/.claude-work while DATA_HOME/providers/claude/office-agent-takkub exists on disk. `resolve_account_for('claude','agent-takkub','lead')` -> ('legacy-claude-office','C:/Users/monch/.claude-work'); `account_env_overrides` -> {'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR': 'C:/Users/monch/.claude-work'}. spawn_engine.py:3342-3349 order: `inject_user_profile_env(env, project_ns)` / `inject_curated_claude_config_dir(env, project_ns)` / ... / `_apply_v2_account_env_override(env, CLAUDE, project_ns, role_name)`. facade.py docstring line 11-12 claims 'wiring this in changes nothing observable until a pool is actually registered' — false since #563 (38cc80cd, 2026-09-12) inserted the curated injector between the two; tests/test_skill_gate_563.py:135-155 only test the injector in isolation, tests/test_spawn_v2_account_env.py:193-202 only covers codex on a dev checkout.
findings.fix: Either (a) in spawn_engine.py move `_apply_v2_account_env_override` BEFORE `inject_curated_claude_config_dir` and pass the resolved `account.config_dir` as `base_dir` to `ensure_curated_claude_config_dir`, or (b) make `resolve_account_for` return None on the legacy fallback (only a real V2 pool should override env — legacy profile env is already applied by `inject_user_profile_env`). Add a spawn-level test asserting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR contains 'providers/claude' with a non-default profile and V2 router on.

findings.title: _SHARED_DIR_LEGACY_GLOBS 'agents/*.md' archives the live custom-role .md files spawn reads from
findings.scenario: User creates a custom role in Role Manager after migration. custom_roles.create_role() writes CUSTOM_AGENTS_DIR/<name>.md (custom_roles.py:211-223) where CUSTOM_AGENTS_DIR = SETTINGS_HOME / "agents" (config.py:515) = DATA_HOME/agents/<name>.md on prod, and spawn reads that exact path (config.py:1011-1013 `custom_src = CUSTOM_AGENTS_DIR / f"{role}.md"`). Next archive pass: `_shared_dir_legacy_candidates()` (2455-2479) matches agents/<name>.md, copy-verifies it into backups/v1-archive-<ts>/agents/ and prunes it. RoleAgentMigrationStep._role_md_pairs() (steps_v1.py:234-248) only re-copies roles listed in the V1 custom-roles.json, which is already archived, so nothing lands in agents/custom/. The role stays in the V2 registry (agents/custom/registry.json) but spawns with no instructions; `_scan_orphan_custom_role_docs` no longer sees it.
findings.evidence: promote_v1.py:247-250 `_SHARED_DIR_LEGACY_GLOBS: tuple[str, ...] = ("agents/*.md", "projects/*/role-providers.json",)`; custom_roles.py:8-13 docstring: '<config.CUSTOM_AGENTS_DIR>/<name>.md ... stays V1 (this is what spawn actually reads)'.
findings.fix: Remove 'agents/*.md' from _SHARED_DIR_LEGACY_GLOBS, or only archive an agents/<role>.md when the V1 custom-roles.json source still exists and the role is not present in the V2 registry; never archive a file the running app still reads.

findings.title: A late-write-kept entry leaves the archive WAL forever: resume never rescans, re-created live files are re-deleted or clobber the archived V1 snapshot, validate() stays red every boot
findings.scenario: After the 11/9 archive, `_prune_phase` kept a live-rewritten file (late_write_kept non-empty) so `ledger.clear()` at 1220-1221 never ran. On every later apply_pending pass: apply_copy_only() sees ledger.exists() and rebuilds entries ONLY from the WAL (2675-2678, T6 'never a fresh scan'), so bin/, provider-quota.json, context/ etc. are never enumerated; then prune() baseline hits the 11/9 entry for e.g. remote.json whose src was re-created by the app: `_remove_entry_source` -> hash differs -> `_remove_verified_file(src, dest, None)` -> `copy_only(src, dest)` OVERWRITES the archived 11/9 remote.json (the snapshot restore-v1 would put back) with post-migration content; if the hash happens to match the recorded one, `_remove(entry.src)` (969-971) deletes the live file again. late_write_kept stays non-empty -> WAL never cleared -> ArchiveV1LegacyStep.validate() red forever -> v1_retired False -> the 5 _ARCHIVED_SOURCE_STEP_IDS steps re-apply + take a new BackupManager slot every boot.
findings.evidence: promote_v1.py:1220-1221 `if not late_write_kept:\n            ledger.clear()`; 2675-2678 `if ledger.exists(): ... new_entries = [_entry_from_wal(rec) for rec in ledger.read().values()]`; 901-903 `copy_only(src, dest)\n        return False, _sha256(dest)`. Prod: backups/archive-v1-legacy-wal.json mtime 11/9 23:13:24 still present; remote.json/theme-settings.json re-created at top level after being archived.
findings.fix: When every WAL entry is SOURCE_PRUNED at resume time, clear the WAL and take a fresh candidate scan; treat a source that reappears AFTER its entry was PRUNED as a new file (never refresh dest / never delete it under the old entry); clear the WAL after a prune whose only leftovers are late-write-kept files and re-enumerate them as fresh candidates next pass.

findings.title: ArchiveV1LegacyStep sweeps LIVE top-level state (remote.json, theme, graft store, cloudflared bin) into the archive on every apply pass
findings.scenario: Installed build: SETTINGS_HOME == DATA_HOME (config.py:228-230). Live writers keep state at DATA_HOME top level: remote/config.py:22 `_PATH = SETTINGS_HOME / "remote.json"` (remote token/secret/public_url/password hash), theme_settings.py:33, performance_settings.py:69, plan_tier.py:50, provider_state.py:129 (provider-quota.json), response_language.py:39, auto_resume.py:120, graft_store.py:149 (`return DATA_HOME` -> DATA_HOME/graft-graphs, graft-staging), trace_store.py:41 (context/), circuit_breaker.py:229 (resilience/), cloudflared_install.py:51 (bin/cloudflared.exe, #710). None are in _ARCHIVE_SKIP_NAMES (175-193) or _V2_TOP_LEVEL_NAMES (140-156), so `_archive_candidates()` = every unlisted top-level entry; `_pending_real_data()` turns validate() red, apply_pending re-applies the step, `_copy_phase` copies then `_prune_phase` DELETES the source. User sees: remote pairing gone (must re-pair phone), theme/perf reset, cloudflared re-downloaded, graft code-graph store rebuilt from scratch, new `v1-archive-<ts>` per boot.
findings.evidence: promote_v1.py:2449-2453 `return [p for p in sorted(self.data_home.iterdir()) if p.name not in protected and p.name not in delete_names]`. Prod store ~/.agent-takkub/backups/v1-archive-1789137187.587171/ (11/9) contains remote.json, theme-settings.json, performance-settings.json, pane-tools.json, context/, graft-graphs/ (63,138 files), graft-staging/ (128,108 files) - all moved out from under the running app; today's top-level graft-graphs (33,676 files, newest 22/9 19:54) and graft-staging (68,869) are the rebuilt live store, remote.json re-created 22/9 19:58. The very same class was already hit for auto-migrate-state.json (auto_migrate_boot.py:105-121 '#504 H8 fresh_two_boots') and fixed only for that one file.
findings.fix: Default-deny: archive only names known to be V1 (LEGACY_MAPPING sources + _SHARED_DIR_LEGACY_GLOBS + an explicit allowlist), never 'everything not in a skip list'. At minimum add every live SETTINGS_HOME/*.json writer (remote.json, theme-settings.json, performance-settings.json, plan.json, provider-quota.json, response-language.json, park-fallback.json, claude-auth.json), bin, context, resilience, graft-graphs, graft-staging to _ARCHIVE_SKIP_NAMES, and make _pending_real_data() ignore unknown names instead of treating them as V1 leftovers.

findings.title: write_json_atomic never invalidates the read cache -> post-apply validate() reads pre-write data for 3 s
findings.scenario: apply_pending() re-applies an already-applied domain step (readonly-registries/capability/state/role-agent/project) whose validate() went red: engine.py:598 `s.validate()` reads the target via legacy_reader.read_json -> cached_read (target mtime old => cached with recent=False); apply() then write_json_atomic()s the target without invalidate(); engine.py:624 `_validate_one` runs milliseconds later -> read_cached returns the cached pre-write parse via the 3 s stat-free TTL (cached_read.py:82-83) -> data != source -> false 'mismatch'. In apply_pending the false failure is fed to on_validate_step/last_validate_reports (wizard shows step failed) and, when promote/archive ran this pass, _downgrade_on_health (line 671) downgrades the apply report to ok=False so _finish_deferred_prune skips every prune and auto_migrate_boot records the step in stale_applied_steps (doctor WARN) — repeating next boot. v2_target.write_data (v2_target.py:199-200) does call invalidate(); the migration writer does not.
findings.evidence: registry_copy_step.py:47-51 `tmp.write_text(...)` / `os.replace(tmp, path)` (no invalidate); cached_read.py:82-83 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S:` / `return hit[1]`; engine.py:598 `_validated = s.validate()` then 605 `_copy_only_apply(s)` then 624 `_validate_one(s, ...)`; RegistryCopyStep.validate() 188 `read_json(m.target).get("data") != read_json(m.source)`.
findings.fix: Call agent_takkub.cached_read.invalidate(path) at the end of write_json_atomic (same rule the memory note already mandates for every cached_read writer), or have each step's validate() read targets with json.loads(path.read_text()) like _domain_target_problems does.

findings.title: RAM-derived max_panes_global is sampled once at cockpit boot and never refreshed; Settings/cache invalidation never reaches the live governor
findings.scenario: `effective_slot_policy()` is called exactly once — `ResourceGovernor.__init__` (resource_governor.py:329) from `Orchestrator.__init__` (orchestrator.py:1806) — while the cockpit is still booting (WebEngine + boot sweep eating RAM). `_ram_derived_max_panes_global()` = floor((available - total*min_available_ram_percent) / 650MB), floored at 1. On a 16GB laptop in balanced mode (reserve 20% = 3.2GB) with ~5GB free at boot the cap is 2; the third concurrent `takkub assign` is denied `global_panes_limit` ('queued — machine-wide pane cap reached (RAM free 45%)', orchestrator.py:1217-1223) and stays queued until another role releases its token, even after the user closes Chrome and RAM is plentiful. Only a cockpit restart re-samples. `invalidate_policy_cache()` (called by core_v2_settings.save) only clears the module cache — the governor's `self.slot_policy` snapshot is never re-read, so no runtime knob can lift the cap.
findings.evidence: facade.py:74-80 docstring: 'Sampled fresh on every call ... this number needs to track current headroom' — but the only caller is resource_governor.py:329 `self.slot_policy = slot_policy or scheduling_facade.effective_slot_policy()`; `_live_limits` (resource_governor.py:389-418) refreshes env caps only, never `slot_policy`. Measured here: total 39.6GB, avail 17.7GB, maximum mode (12%) -> cap 20; formula gives 2 for 16GB/balanced/5GB-free. `_active_counts` (resource_governor.py:525-546) counts tokens (one per assigned role) as panes.
findings.fix: Re-evaluate the RAM cap at request time: in `_denial_reason` (or a cheap throttled helper) recompute `max_panes_global` when the policy leaves it None instead of freezing it in `__init__`; keep the parsed settings policy cached but layer the psutil sample on each check (it is microseconds). Alternatively re-read `effective_slot_policy()` on `_capacity_epoch` bumps and after `core_v2_settings.save()`.

findings.title: read_data serves a 3s-TTL cached object to read-modify-write callers → cross-process lost update / duplicate issue numbers on state/issues/local.json
findings.scenario: Cockpit process reads local.json at T0 (issues._load_local_issues → read_data → read_cached, entry cached with recent=False). A pane runs `takkub issue "..."` (CLI process, cli.py:6649 → issues.cmd_issue_new) which writes local.json at T0+1s. At T0+2s the cockpit's auto_issue_capture.py:353 / auto_issue_signals.py:340 / update_worker.py:218 call issues.new_issue → _load_local_issues is served from cache WITHOUT a stat (cached_read.py:82, `mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S`) → stale list → `number = max(...)+1` (issues.py:536) collides with the CLI's number → issues.append + _save_local_issues → write_data overwrites the file: the pane's issue is gone and the new one reuses its number. write_data's invalidate() (v2_target.py:200) only fixes the SAME process's later reads, not the stale read that preceded this write.
findings.evidence: issues.py:378 `return data if isinstance(data, list) else []` (returns the cached object itself); issues.py:535-536 `issues = _load_local_issues(local_cwd)` / `number = max([iss.get("number", 0) for iss in issues] or [0]) + 1`; cached_read.py:82 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]`
findings.fix: Read-modify-write stores must bypass the TTL: have _load_local_issues (and any writer path) call cached_read.invalidate(target) before read_data, or add a `fresh=True` parameter to read_data/read_json that forces a stat, and copy the parsed object before returning it so callers never mutate the cache entry in place.

findings.title: save_custom_roles never invalidates cached_read → every read within 3s is stale (registry lost-update, delete no-op, create not registered)
findings.scenario: Registry read via legacy_reader.read_json → cached_read (3s stat-skip TTL); writer uses registry_copy_step.write_json_atomic which does NOT call cached_read.invalidate(). Reproduced with venv python + temp file: load → save {a,b} → load returns ['a'] only; delete_role('b') returns True while b stays on disk; correct after 3.1s. Real flows (2nd-ever custom role, file already exists so boot read cached it with recent=False): (1) legacy Settings 'New Role' (settings_window.py:3546→3555) — load_custom_roles().get(name) is None → roles.register_role skipped → status says 'spawn ได้ทันที' but takkub assign --role <name> fails until restart, and _apply_new_role_tools_policy → pane_tools_policy.set_role_items:287 rejects the role (known_roles() reads list_role_names() stale) → '! แต่บันทึก MCP/Plugins default ไม่สำเร็จ'. (2) new UI roles_repo.create → relationships._apply_access → pane_tools_policy.reset_role:382 False → RuntimeError 'เขียน MCP/plugin policy ไม่สำเร็จ' → FileTransaction rollback → create fails. (3) cleanup.role_delete_plan:76 shows 'Built-in role ลบไม่ได้' for a role created <3s ago. (4) two saves <3s apart (create A then create/update B) → A's registry entry dropped.
findings.evidence: custom_roles.py:117 `data = read_json(path())` (cached) · :158-160 `from .core.migration.registry_copy_step import write_json_atomic` / `write_json_atomic(path(), payload)` (no invalidate) · cached_read.py:82 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]` · repro output: `read-back : ['a']` after `on disk : ['a','b']`; `delete_role(b) : True | still on disk: True`
findings.fix: In save_custom_roles call `from .cached_read import invalidate; invalidate(path())` right after write_json_atomic (same contract v2_target.write_data already follows), or route the write through v2_target-style wrapper that invalidates. Add a test that primes the cache with an old-mtime file, saves, and asserts the immediate read-back sees the new role.

findings.title: UTF-8 BOM file gains one extra BOM on every Ctrl+S (data corruption)
findings.scenario: Open any BOM-prefixed file (PowerShell .ps1, .csproj, files saved by Notepad/VS on Windows) in the Monaco editor and press Ctrl+S. The file on disk now starts with EF BB BF EF BB BF; each further save appends another BOM and Monaco shows a growing run of invisible U+FEFF chars at line 1.
findings.evidence: editor_widget.py:153 `text = resolved.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (codec keeps U+FEFF; only utf-8-sig strips it) -> static/editor/index.html:512 `monaco.editor.createModel(text, ...)` / :322 `tab.model.getValue()` round-trips it -> editor_service.py:181-183 `data = text.encode("utf-8")` then `if expected.bom: data = _UTF8_BOM + data` prepends a second BOM.
findings.fix: In read_file_for_editor use `encoding="utf-8-sig"` (or `text.lstrip("﻿")`), and in editor_service._encode_for_write strip a leading U+FEFF from `text` before prepending _UTF8_BOM.

findings.title: Re-opening an already-open file silently discards unsaved edits
findings.scenario: User edits a file in the editor (dirty), then double-clicks the same file in the Explorer or clicks its row in the CHANGES panel (main_window.py:542 -> open_file(show_diff=True)). EditorHost.open_file has no already-open short-circuit: it re-reads disk and calls editorOpenFile, and the JS side replaces the model and clears dirty — the edits are gone with no prompt.
findings.evidence: editor_widget.py:628-644 open_file never checks `abs_path in self._open_paths`; static/editor/index.html:519-524 `} else { tab.text = text; // reopen with fresh content\n tab.dirty = false; ... tab.model.setValue(text); }`
findings.fix: In open_file, if the resolved path is already in _open_paths: skip the worker, run_js to activate the tab (and dispatch _on_diff_requested when show_diff) instead of editorOpenFile; alternatively make JS editorOpenFile refuse setValue when tab.dirty.

findings.title: Feedback-prompt auto-skip in _send_when_ready._check has no cooldown/attempt cap → '0\r' written every 150 ms poll; delivery stays prompt-blocked
findings.scenario: A gemini/agy teammate shows the CLI survey ('How's the CLI experience so far? … [0] Skip') while a task is being delivered. `_prompt_block_reason` (line 223-227) calls `is_at_feedback_prompt()` with NO provider → generic regex over the FULL screen (pty_session.py:2805,2818). `_check` runs every 150 ms and writes the skip key unconditionally each poll while the survey text is still on screen; each extra '0\r' after the prompt closes is submitted to the composer as a user message '0'. Meanwhile `_reason` stays truthy → `can_accept_input(prompt_blocked=True)` keeps ready_streak at 0; at timeout `_deliver(unconfirmed=True)` sees reason 'feedback' → 30 s defer → `_warn_lead_delivery_blocked_ceiling` → task never pasted. The two other auto-skip sites gate on `feedback_prompt_dismiss_ts` (3 s cooldown, max 3 attempts: orchestrator.py:13583-13586, spawn_engine.py:4460) — this one does not.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:1761 `if _reason == "feedback":` … 1770-1771 `_skip_key = feedback_prompt_skip_key_for(_prov) or "0\r"` / `pane.session.write(_skip_key)` (no latch, no PaneState cooldown); pty_session.py:2805 `text = "\n".join(self.display_lines()).lower()`
findings.fix: Reuse PaneState.feedback_prompt_dismiss_ts/attempts here (skip if now-ts<3.0 or attempts>=3), and do not count 'feedback' as prompt_blocked once a skip has been sent within the last few seconds. Also add 'feedback' to the kind map at lines 2614-2618.

findings.title: Weekly-window quota hit is declared a false positive: deny verdict checks only five_hour / codex primary
findings.scenario: Max user's claude pane hits the 7-day cap (seven_day=100%, five_hour=30%) and shows the quota banner. Watchdog -> _maybe_auto_resume_park -> confirm thread -> confirm_verdict_for_provider('claude') -> _usage_confirms_limit False (five_hour<95) -> _usage_denies_limit returns (True, 30.0) -> 'denied' -> _on_limit_usage_denied clears rate_limited_until, arms quota_false_positive_armed, tells Lead the pane did NOT hit quota. No reroute to codex/gemini, idle 'forgot takkub done' reminders resume into a pane that cannot answer for days; orchestrator._rate_limit_suppressed (15043-15049) ignores the banner while it stays on screen. Same for codex weekly (secondary) limit: line 144 reads only p_usage.utilization (primary).
findings.evidence: L109-111: `if window.name == "five_hour" and isinstance(window.utilization, (int, float)):` / `return pct < threshold, pct`   L144-149: `util = getattr(p_usage, "utilization", None)` ... `return "denied", float(util)` (provider_usage.py:412 sets utilization from `primary` only; secondary is in `windows` L431-433 but never consulted)
findings.fix: Only return 'denied' when EVERY known window (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet; codex primary AND secondary via p_usage.windows) is below threshold; treat any window >= threshold as 'confirmed'. Mirror in _usage_confirms_limit and quota_reprobe_verdict.

findings.title: Preset roles spawn into whichever project is active 15 s after boot, and boot-restored tabs steal focus/active
findings.scenario: projects.json has A active with presets=[frontend] and open_tabs=[A,B]. Boot: A's tab is built, then at 2.5 s `_open_project_tab('B')` sets B active + current. At 15 s `orch.spawn('frontend')` (no project) resolves the active project = B, so the preset pane opens in B's cwd. Also every boot with 2+ tabs lands on the LAST restored tab, not the one the user was on, and `active` flips each boot.
findings.evidence: main_window.py:968 `presets = preset_roles_for_active()` computed at boot; :975 `QTimer.singleShot(15_000 + i * 3_000, lambda r=role: self.orch.spawn(r))` passes no project; :991 restores tabs via `_open_project_tab` which unconditionally :1498 `set_active_project(project_name)` and :1508 `self.tabs.setCurrentIndex(idx)`. orchestrator.py:2202-2210 `_resolve_project(None)` -> active project.
findings.fix: Capture `initial_project` and pass `project=initial_project` to the preset spawn lambdas; give `_open_project_tab` a `make_current: bool` parameter and pass False from the boot restore loop (then re-select the initial tab / restore `active`).

findings.title: Lead never spawns while the cockpit is not the foreground app, and the gate poll floods events.log at 20 lines/s
findings.scenario: User launches the cockpit (or `takkub restart` from the phone) and alt-tabs away / locks the screen before the window becomes active. `_spawn_lead_when_quiet` requires ApplicationActive, so the Lead pane stays empty until the user clicks the window; meanwhile a `boot_lead_gate_blocked` line is written every 50 ms (2 MiB rotation of events.log in ~11 min, wiping history the auto-issue watcher reads).
findings.evidence: main_window.py:1062 `app_active = QApplication.applicationState() == Qt.ApplicationState.ApplicationActive`; :1068-1078 logs + reschedules every `_BOOT_LEAD_POLL_MS`=50 (:90). runtime/events.log.old: 680 `boot_lead_gate_blocked` lines, 20 per second at 2026-09-20T09:33:15..20, all `"app_active": false`. orchestrator_text.py:54 `_EVENTS_LOG_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024`.
findings.fix: Drop `app_active` from the gate (or accept ApplicationInactive after N turns / a timeout), and log `boot_lead_gate_blocked` once per reason change instead of every poll tick.

findings.title: Lead-spawn failure on the only/new tab destroys the shared usage corner; status ticks raise forever and later tab switches abort before set_active_project
findings.scenario: All tabs closed (empty state), user opens a project via + whose Lead spawn returns not-ok (provider binary missing, role/preset gate, PTY error). The failed tab is removed and deleteLater'd while it still hosts `_usage_corner` (meter + performance chip). From then on `_update_status` raises RuntimeError every 2 s, and the next successful `_open_project_tab` raises inside `_on_tab_switched` before `set_active_project`, so `active` stays None, the task dock/preview never sync, and Restart Lead / provider switch / Shell button act on no project until restart.
findings.evidence: main_window.py:1506-1508 addTab -> `_on_tab_switched` mounts the corner (:1671-1672); :1524 `self.tabs.removeTab(failed_index)` -> `_on_tab_switched(-1)` (:1648-1654) never detaches; :1525 `tab.deleteLater()`. Compare the explicit detach that `_close_project_tab` does at :1606-1609. status_header.py:800 `self._chip_performance.setText(` has no sip.isdeleted guard; main_window.py:1669-1670 `self._limit_label_host.pane_tabs.setCornerWidget(None, ...)` runs on the deleted tab. Also :1516-1525 never calls `unregister_workspace_diag_sources` for the failed tab.
findings.fix: Factor the corner detach (`setCornerWidget(None)`, `_usage_corner.setParent(None)`, `_limit_label_host = None`) into a helper and call it in the `_open_project_tab` failure branch (and in `_on_tab_switched(-1)`); also unregister the failed tab's diag sources.

findings.title: Closing a project tab leaves its teammate panes registered in the orchestrator; reopening the project can never spawn those roles again
findings.scenario: User closes project A's tab while it has a qa pane, later reopens A (+ picker) and Lead runs `takkub assign --role qa`. spawn() finds the dead qa AgentPane in the registry, never emits paneRequested, launches the provider process, then attach_session raises RuntimeError on the deleted terminal -> 'failed to spawn qa: wrapped C/C++ object ... has been deleted'. Every later assign of qa in A fails the same way until the cockpit restarts; `takkub list` in A still shows qa as 'empty'.
findings.evidence: main_window.py:1588 `tab.teammate_panes.clear()` runs BEFORE :1589 `close_all_teammates`, so the deferred `_teardown` (:826-828) returns before :839 `unregister_pane`. orchestrator.close() (:6047-6392) never pops the registry; the only pop is spawn_engine.py:1570. spawn_engine.py:2228 `pane = project_panes.get(role_name)` -> stale pane, :2027 launches session, :2034 `pane.attach_session` -> agent_pane.py:655 `self._terminal.resized.connect` on a deleted widget -> caught at spawn_engine.py:2185.
findings.fix: In `_close_project_tab`, after `close_all_teammates`, call `self.orch.unregister_pane(role, project=tab.project_name)` for every pane in the saved `teammate_panes` list (or pop the whole `_panes_by_project[project]` entry); alternatively make `_teardown` unregister even when the tab dict is already empty.

findings.title: Stuck-recover respawn reads last_spawn_resumed before a deferred/queued spawn has run → full task re-pasted into a --resume'd conversation (Bug-5 duplicate work)
findings.scenario: Machine is overloaded (exactly when panes wedge). `_check_stuck_panes` → `_auto_recover_stuck` → close() → 2 s later `_do_respawn` restores session_uuid + `_recent_exits` (14552-14581) then calls spawn(). spawn() hits the resource-governor gate or the FIFO arbiter and returns `(True, '… spawn deferred (gate blocked)')` / `'… spawn queued (arbiter busy)'` (spawn_engine.py:2401, 2428) WITHOUT creating a session. `_ps_after.last_spawn_resumed` is the fresh PaneState default False (spawn_engine.py:928), so line 14630-14631 sends the FULL original task via `_send_when_ready`, which keeps polling until the session is alive. When `_retry_deferred_spawn`/`_drain_spawn_queue` finally spawns, can_resume finds the restored uuid → `--resume` → claude reloads the conversation that already contains the task, then receives it again → reruns migrations/commits. Same latent shape in `_auto_respawn` (spawn_engine.py:4400-4417).
findings.evidence:
orchestrator.py:14627-14633 `_ps_after = self._pane_state.get(key)` / `spawn_resumed = _ps_after.last_spawn_resumed if _ps_after is not None else False` / `if not spawn_resumed: self._send_when_ready(role, snap_task, project=project)`
spawn_engine.py:2428 `return True, f"{role_name} spawn queued (arbiter busy)"`
findings.fix: Decide replay-vs-nudge after the session actually attaches: move the `snap_task`/`_STUCK_RESUME_NUDGE` choice into a callback keyed on the spawn completing (e.g. check `msg` for 'deferred'/'queued' and defer the decision via the existing `_preserve_pending_spawn_initial_task` / `_recent_exits` machinery), or pass `resume_uuid=snap_uuid` explicitly and always send only the nudge when a uuid exists.

findings.title: Quota banner still on screen after reset is re-detected and rolled +24h (or re-added duration) → phantom new quota episode, Lead notice, park/reroute
findings.scenario: claude teammate hits its quota at 10:00 with banner '<quota-marker> … resets 3pm'. At 15:00 the QTimer fires `_emit_rate_limit_reset` (or the next tick clears via line 15033-15037), `rate_limited_until` becomes 0. The banner text is still in the visible screen (claude does not clear it; display_lines() is the whole screen), so the very next 5 s tick calls `rate_limit_reset_at()` again: `_parse_rate_limit_reset` sees 'resets 3pm', 15:00 today is already past, so pty_session.py:1338-1339 returns tomorrow 15:00. Result: `ps.rate_limited_until` = +24h, a second '[system] … hit quota — resets in 23h59m' notice to Lead, idle reminders suppressed for a day, and `_maybe_auto_resume_park` starts a fresh confirm loop whose claude probe uses `fetch_usage_shared(max_age_s=300)` (limit_autoresume.py:129) — cached telemetry from before the reset says exhausted → `_reroute_or_park`. Same for gemini/agy duration form ('resets in 2h' is static text → re-parked 2h every cycle). Nothing arms `quota_false_positive_armed` on this path (only the usage-denied slot does).
findings.evidence:
orchestrator.py:15050-15059 `if reset_at is None: return False` … `ps.rate_limited_until = reset_at` (no latch after a reset)
pty_session.py:1338-1339 `if epoch <= now:  # clock time already passed today → it means tomorrow` / `epoch += 24 * 60 * 60`
orchestrator.py:15181 `_ps_rr.rate_limited_until = 0.0` (reset clears state but leaves banner text detectable)
findings.fix: After a reset (both in `_emit_rate_limit_reset` and the `now >= existing` branch of `_rate_limit_suppressed`) set `ps.quota_false_positive_armed = True` (or a dedicated `quota_reset_seen_marker`) so the same on-screen banner is ignored until it scrolls off; additionally have `_parse_rate_limit_reset` refuse to roll a clock-time forward when the caller passes the previous episode's reset_at (treat 'already passed today' within N minutes as 'expired', return None).

findings.title: strip_takkub_text_payload splits on newline BEFORE blanking quotes — multi-line assign/done text is classified as commands (#649 regression)
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub assign --role backend "<spec>"` where the spec has a line starting with `npm run build` / `pytest` / `tsc` while any other pane is 'working' (machine-state.json fresh). classify() line 4015-4029 returns busy_machine:pm_build and Lead cannot hand out the task — the exact #649 symptom. Same for a multi-line `takkub done` note.
findings.evidence:
line 827: `for segment in re.split(r"(&&|\|\||[;|]|
)", cmd):` — the `
` split happens before `_QUOTED_RUN` (which is `(?s)` and could span lines), so line 2+ of the quoted payload becomes its own segment with no `takkub` in it and is never blanked. Probe (venv python): `_is_heavy_build_or_suite('takkub assign --role backend "do this
npm run build
then done"')` → `(True, 'pm_build')`; `strip_takkub_text_payload(...)` returned the text unchanged.
findings.fix: Split with the quote-aware `_split_chain_segments` (line 2207) or apply `_QUOTED_RUN.sub('""', ...)` to the whole command when `_TAKKUB_TEXT_CMD` matches at a segment start; then strip once at the top of classify() so every rule sees the stripped text.

findings.title: full_suite / scope_tiny / browser / git rules run on the raw command — a `takkub done` note quoting a runner or git verb is denied
findings.scenario: A backend pane reports `takkub done "ran:\npytest\nall green"` (or a note with a fenced block whose line starts with `jest`, `vitest run`, `git push ...`). The hook denies the done call with full_suite:pytest / git_lead_only:push; the pane retries (#399 loop) and Lead must recover the pane by hand.
findings.evidence: Only `_is_heavy_build_or_suite` (line 838) calls `strip_takkub_text_payload`; line 4135 `full_suite = _full_suite_rule(cmd)`, line 4046 `_TAKKUB_QA_GATE.search(cmd)`, line 4084 `_BROWSER_PATTERNS`, line 4195+ git patterns all use unstripped `cmd` with `^` under re.M. Probe: `classify('takkub done "ran:\npytest\nall green"', 'backend')` → `allowed=False, rule='full_suite:pytest'`.
findings.fix: Compute `code = strip_takkub_text_payload(cmd)` once after `_unwrap_shell_wrappers` (line 3980) and evaluate every rule against `code` (keep `raw_cmd` only for the GIT_* env scans).

findings.title: save_policy never invalidates cached_read: regen + CLI verify read stale policy, `takkub mcp allow/deny` reports 'this is a bug' and variant file keeps the old MCP set
findings.scenario: User runs `takkub mcp deny --role qa playwright` (policy file last written >2s ago, i.e. always in practice). deny_item() calls load_policy() (populates cache with hit[3]=False), save_policy() writes via registry_copy_step.write_json_atomic (no invalidate), then _regen_role_variants_best_effort() -> regen_role_variants_checked() -> load_policy()/effective_mcps() hit cached_read's fast path (cached_read.py:82 returns hit[1] with NO stat for 3s) -> shared-mcp-qa.json is regenerated from the OLD policy (still contains playwright). cli.py:5233 then re-reads effective_mcps (stale) and returns {"ok": False, "msg": "deny 'playwright' for qa did not change the effective allowlist ... this is a bug, not a config issue."}. Variants are only regenerated again at cockpit boot (orchestrator.py:1607/1647) or a later Settings/CLI regen, so the next qa spawn still loads playwright (Chromium tree). Same for the empty-policy branch (L198 unlink, no invalidate) used by reset_role, and for the Settings Role Manager path (settings_management/repositories/mcps.py:232 save_policy -> relationships.py:101 regen_role_variants_checked) in the cockpit process. tests/test_cli_pane_tools.py monkeypatches load_policy/effective_mcps/allow_item so the real cache is never exercised.
findings.evidence: pane_tools_policy.py:234-235 `write_json_atomic(path(), payload)` / `_regen_role_variants_best_effort()`; cached_read.py:82 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]`; cli.py:5233-5240 `effective = ptp.effective_mcps(...)` -> `"msg": (... did not change the effective allowlist ... this is a bug ...)`; contrast provider_config.py:128 `invalidate(target)` after the same write_json_atomic.
findings.fix: In save_policy call `from .cached_read import invalidate; invalidate(path())` immediately after write_json_atomic (L234) and after `path().unlink(missing_ok=True)` (L198), before _regen_role_variants_best_effort(). Mirror provider_config._write_routing.

findings.title: Node auto-targeted tier: `vitest related` without --passWithNoTests fails the gate when a changed file has no related spec
findings.scenario: Specialist edits a component/util in a vitest project that has no spec importing it, runs `takkub qa-gate --auto`. classify_diff → 'targeted' → step `test:vitest-related` runs `npx --no-install vitest related --run <files>`; vitest finds no test files and exits 1 ('No test files found, exiting with code 1') → step FAIL → GATE: FAIL on a healthy diff. The jest branch (l.1460) explicitly passes `--passWithNoTests`; the vitest branch does not.
findings.evidence: l.1459-1461 `if runner == "jest":\n    return pm_exec(pm, "jest", "--ci", "--passWithNoTests", "--findRelatedTests", *files)\nreturn pm_exec(pm, "vitest", "related", "--run", *files)`
findings.fix: `pm_exec(pm, "vitest", "related", "--run", "--passWithNoTests", *files)`.

findings.title: release rollback leaves the annotated tag behind → every retry refused with 'tag already exists'
findings.scenario: `takkub release` commits (l.387) and tags (l.391), then `build_wheel` (l.398) fails (no `build` module, stale build/ dir, 300s timeout). The except block resets the commit and restores the 4 files but never runs `git tag -d`, so `vX.Y.Z` now points at an orphaned commit. Re-running `takkub release` hits `_tag_exists` (l.331) → ValueError 'git tag vX.Y.Z already exists — pick a different version'; the user must hand-delete the tag.
findings.evidence: l.391 `_git(repo_root, "tag", "-a", tag, "-m", tag)` runs before l.398 `wheel_path = build_wheel(repo_root)`; the except at l.401-427 only does `_git(repo_root, "reset", "--mixed", original_head)` + file writes — no tag deletion anywhere in the module.
findings.fix: Track `tag_created = True` after l.391 and in the except block run `_git(repo_root, "tag", "-d", tag)` (best-effort) before the reset; or build the wheel before tagging.

findings.title: Boot-time remote start builds the Qt bridge on a worker thread: every bridged /api/* route answers 504 after each cockpit boot
findings.scenario: remote.json enabled=true (the user's prod config). Cockpit boots -> main_window._start_remote_off_thread runs RemoteControl.prepare() via cli.run_off_thread (a plain daemon threading.Thread, cli_server.py:309). prepare() -> _start_blocking() -> http_server.start_server() -> RemoteHttpServer.__init__ -> `self.bridge = _Bridge(orch)` (http_server.py:1130): the QObject's thread affinity is the now-dead worker thread. Every handler-thread `bridge.request.emit(pending)` is queued to that thread, which has no event loop, so `_Bridge._handle` never runs and `_bridge_call` times out: 504 {"msg":"orchestrator did not respond"} after 8 s for /api/projects, /api/activity, /api/lead/history, /api/lead/sessions, /api/sse-ticket, /api/open, /api/close, /api/lead/say, /api/lead/upload, /api/lead/answer-picker, /api/usage, /api/image, /api/lead/resume. Phone shows 'โหลด projects ไม่สำเร็จ', never gets an SSE ticket, chat stays blank. Only recovery is Settings -> Disable -> Enable (maybe_start on the Qt thread, user_actions.py:854) every boot. Introduced by #640 (commit 265bb2cb, v2.1.13).
findings.evidence: __init__.py:97-105 docstring claims prepare() 'touches no Qt object', but _start_blocking() line 172 `self._server = http_server.start_server(self.config, self._orch)` -> http_server.py:1130 `self.bridge = _Bridge(orch)` (QObject, `self.request.connect(self._handle)` at :221). Reproduced with the venv PyQt6: a QObject created in a threading.Thread never receives a queued signal emitted from another thread even while the main event loop runs ('slot NEVER ran'). tests/test_remote_scaffold.py:685 stubs run_off_thread to call work() on the test thread, so the suite cannot see this.
findings.fix: Create `_Bridge` on the Qt thread: give RemoteHttpServer a `bridge=None` slot, construct/attach it in RemoteControl._start_qt() (or call `self._server.bridge.moveToThread(QCoreApplication.instance().thread())` in finish_start()), and make _bridge_call answer 503 while bridge is None. Add a test that runs prepare() on a real thread and asserts a bridged request completes.

findings.title: Quick-tunnel / ngrok-random URL is only ever harvested by the Settings-dialog 6-second poll; after a cockpit restart the pairing URL is the previous run's dead hostname (or blank)
findings.scenario: tunnel.type = quick (or ngrok url_mode=random). (a) Restart the cockpit: _start_blocking() builds `Tunnel(self.config.tunnel, self.config.public_url, port)` with the *.trycloudflare.com hostname saved last session; Tunnel.__init__ sets `captured_url = public_url or None`, so _scan_for_url (line 638 `if self.captured_url is None`) never records the new random hostname cloudflared just printed, nothing at boot reads captured_url, and RemoteSettingsDialog / reports.build_url keep showing the dead URL. Phone link and every report link 530/404. (b) First Enable: user_actions._poll_remote_public_url gives up silently after _QUICK_TUNNEL_WAIT_S=6.0 s (line 756 `elif attempts >= max_attempts: timer.stop()`); cloudflared quick tunnels routinely take >6 s to print the URL, so captured_url lands later but config.public_url stays "" and the dialog shows 'Disable & revoke pairing' with no URL and no message. Quick mode also never checks `proc.poll()`/is_alive (only _start_named calls _verify_named_started), so a cloudflared that exits at once looks identical.
findings.evidence: tunnel.py:461 `self.captured_url: str | None = public_url or None`; tunnel.py:638-641 only sets it when None; __init__.py:225-228 passes the stale `self.config.public_url`; the only readers of captured_url are user_actions.py:748 and :894 (Enable path). user_actions.py:132-133 `_QUICK_TUNNEL_WAIT_S = 6.0`.
findings.fix: For quick/ngrok-random, always start with captured_url=None (ignore the stale public_url) and have RemoteControl expose a 'tunnel_url_ready' callback/timer used by both boot (main_window) and Enable paths that keeps polling until the reader thread ends; save + repaint chip/dialog when it lands; treat proc.poll() is not None as tunnel_error in _start_quick/_start_ngrok.

findings.title: _write_all never invalidates cached_read → lost `takkub send` records and mark_delivered silently no-ops (→ spurious replays)
findings.scenario: `_reap_role_messages` (orchestrator.py:5628) reads messages/<ns>.jsonl every 5s tick, warming the cache with recent=False. Lead runs two `takkub send` within 3s (or one send followed by its own `_confirm_role_message` ~1-2s later, orchestrator.py:5606): the second `read()` hits `read_cached` line 82-83 (`not hit[3] and mono-hit[2] < 3.0`) and returns the pre-write parse. `_append_record` then rewrites the file WITHOUT the first send (lost from audit log); `mark_delivered` finds no id → returns False silently → record stays 'sent' forever → after the next respawn `undelivered_in` replays it into the fresh pane (up to MAX_REPLAYS=3 duplicate instructions).
findings.evidence: role_messages.py:112 `path.write_text(...)` with no `invalidate(path)`; cached_read.py:82 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]`; cached_read.py:49 docstring: 'in-process writers call invalidate() so their own saves are visible immediately'. No `invalidate` import anywhere in role_messages.py (grep).
findings.fix: In `_write_all`, after write_text call `from .cached_read import invalidate; invalidate(path)` (same pattern as backlog.py:130 / provider_config.py:128). Optionally write via tmp+os.replace.

findings.title: service-stop / service-list trust a bare PID: PID reuse kills an unrelated process tree
findings.scenario: A registered service (e.g. cloudflared) dies; Windows recycles its PID for a pane's node.exe/claude process. `takkub service-list` keeps showing the service alive (never pruned), and `takkub service-stop <name>` runs psutil.Process(pid).kill() plus all children on that unrelated process — e.g. a live pane's tree. started_ts is stored but never compared.
findings.evidence: service_spawner.py:96-102 `_pid_alive` = `psutil.pid_exists(pid)` only; :246-252 `p = psutil.Process(pid); for child in p.children(recursive=True): child.kill() ... p.kill()` with no create_time/name check.
findings.fix: Record `psutil.Process(proc.pid).create_time()` in ServiceRecord at spawn; in _pid_alive/stop treat the row as dead unless `abs(Process(pid).create_time() - rec.create_time) < 1.0`.

findings.title: Second click on Knowledge Refresh / Design Tools Refresh / Test raises RuntimeError (deleted _CallableThread) — button does nothing and an auto-issue is filed
findings.scenario: Knowledge tab → Refresh → wait for result → Refresh again: `_cleanup` (148) already ran `deleteLater()` on the thread, so `self._kd_knowledge_thread.isRunning()` raises 'wrapped C/C++ object of type _CallableThread has been deleted' inside the slot → nothing happens on screen; app.py's excepthook routes it to `capture_cockpit_crash` (a spurious cockpit crash report). Same at 422 (Design Refresh) and 473 (Test).
findings.evidence: 295: `if self._kd_knowledge_thread is not None and self._kd_knowledge_thread.isRunning():` — no try/except. 146-148: `_cleanup` → `_ACTIVE_THREADS.discard(self); self.deleteLater()`. Probe in this venv (PyQt 6.8.1): `isRunning()` after deleteLater → RuntimeError. settings_usage.py:591-597 wraps the identical check in `except RuntimeError: self._usage_import_thread = None` — this file's three callers were never given that guard.
findings.fix: Wrap the three `isRunning()` checks in try/except RuntimeError that sets the attribute to None (copy settings_usage.py:591-597), or have `_cleanup` also clear the owner's reference.

findings.title: Save & Apply under solo-lead/pair persists rolesEnabled=False for every position; later switching to full/auto shows all positions OFF, flips the project to 'custom' or leaves assign rejected
findings.scenario: Project on 'ทำเอง' (solo-lead) or 'คู่' (pair) → open Roles page → change anything (e.g. a provider) → Save & Apply. Every position toggle was rendered OFF (2549: `enabled=_row_enabled_now(...)` → `_can_spawn_from_cfg` returns False for positions under those presets, team_preset.py:99-112 roles all False) and 1641-1643 writes ALL toggles → pipelines.json rolesEnabled = {frontend:false, backend:false, mobile:false, devops:false}. Caller then broadcasts '[system] role X DISABLED' ×4 to Lead (user_actions.py:389-396) though no toggle was touched. Later pick 'ทีมเต็ม' → rows render OFF (`_row_enabled_now` ANDs `pipeline_config.is_role_enabled` = disk False, 2383) → Save → `note_manual_roles_change` sees drift vs full (team_preset.py:404-406) → project silently becomes 'custom' with no positions. Pick 'อัตโนมัติ' instead → no flip, but `is_role_enabled` stays False → `takkub assign --role frontend` rejected at orchestrator.py:2757 / cli_server.py:736 while the chip says auto.
findings.evidence: 1641-1643: `for role, toggle in role_toggles.items(): roles_enabled[role] = toggle.isChecked()`; 2383: `return can_spawn_ok and pipeline_config.is_role_enabled(role, self._project)`; team_preset.py:486: `allowed = bool(cfg["roles"].get(base, False))`.
findings.fix: Only persist rolesEnabled for toggles the user actually changed (diff against the values rendered at build time), or render the toggle from `is_role_enabled` alone and show preset exclusion as a separate dimmed state instead of writing it back to disk.

findings.title: Autoskills scan/install QThreads are parented to the WA_DeleteOnClose SettingsWindow (#688 pattern) — closing Settings mid-scan kills the whole cockpit
findings.scenario: Skills page → click 'ดึง skill ตาม stack' (autoskills CLI, up to ~60s) → press Cancel/Esc/X on Settings while it runs → SettingsWindow deleteLater destroys its child QThread while running → Qt qFatal 'QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running' → fail-fast 0xc0000409, no Python traceback. Same for the install step at line 4420.
findings.evidence: 4376: `self._as_preview_thread = _AutoskillsPreviewThread(roots[0], self)`; 4420: `self._as_install_thread = _AutoskillsInstallThread(roots[0], selected, self)`; both classes do `super().__init__(parent)` (792, 808). SettingsWindow sets WA_DeleteOnClose at 956. The #688 fix at 835-841/1069 (`_ModelCatalogRefreshThread()` unparented + `_CATALOG_THREADS` keep-alive) was applied only to the catalog thread.
findings.fix: Construct both autoskills threads unparented, keep them alive in a module-level set (mirror `_CATALOG_THREADS` at 841/1071-1073), connect `finished` → discard + `deleteLater`; PyQt auto-drops the `resultReady` connection when the dialog dies.

findings.title: autoskills QThreads parented to WA_DeleteOnClose SettingsWindow — close mid-run = Qt fatal abort (#688 class)
findings.scenario: Settings → SKILL → click 'ดึง skill ตาม stack' (preview via `npx --yes autoskills@latest`, up to 60s) or confirm an install (up to 120s), then press Esc/Cancel/X on Settings while it runs. SettingsWindow is WA_DeleteOnClose (line 956) so the QThread parented to it is destroyed while still running → 'QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running' → process aborts (0xc0000409 on Windows, not catchable by faulthandler/excepthook per #688). No closeEvent/wait()/isRunning guard exists in settings_window.py.
findings.evidence:
settings_window.py:4376 `self._as_preview_thread = _AutoskillsPreviewThread(roots[0], self)`
settings_window.py:4420 `self._as_install_thread = _AutoskillsInstallThread(roots[0], selected, self)`
settings_window.py:956 `self.setAttribute(Qt.WidgetAttribute.WA_DeleteOnClose)`
findings.fix: Parent both threads to None (or the main window), keep the reference on self, and in SettingsWindow.closeEvent either wait() on a running thread or disconnect resultReady and let it finish detached; same pattern already applied for #688.

findings.title: ensure_user_mcps() deletes MCPs the user added via `takkub mcp add` / Tools dialog on next boot (prunes everything not in ~/.claude.json)
findings.scenario: User adds an MCP with `takkub mcp add context7 npx ...` (cli.py:5267 → add_mcp_server, writes ONLY runtime/shared-mcp.json). At the next cockpit boot orchestrator.py:1647 calls ensure_user_mcps(): if ~/.claude.json has at least one credential-free mcpServers entry (to_merge non-empty) the prune loop deletes every non-managed name not present in ~/.claude.json — context7 is gone from master + all role variants, only a log.info line. Panes silently lose the server; the Tools dialog shows it missing. On this machine dev runtime/shared-mcp.json holds user-added `context7`,`notebooklm`; ~/.claude.json has `pms` (http + Authorization header → skipped), so today to_merge is empty and the early return at :1310 masks it — the first credential-free entry added to ~/.claude.json (e.g. `claude mcp add ...`) triggers the wipe.
findings.evidence: shared_dev_tools.py:1325-1331 `for name in list(servers.keys()):` / `if name in MANAGED_MCP_NAMES: continue` / `if name not in to_merge: del servers[name]`; add_mcp_server (:887-926) never touches ~/.claude.json; _USER_MCP_DEFAULT_ALLOW is empty (:745).
findings.fix: Track provenance: only prune entries that were themselves merged from ~/.claude.json (e.g. tag merged entries with `"_source": "claude.json"` or keep a runtime/user-mcps-merged.json list) and leave add_mcp_server entries alone; add a regression test: add_mcp_server('x') + ~/.claude.json with one clean entry → ensure_user_mcps keeps 'x'.

findings.title: Crash auto-respawn replays the task even when spawn() only deferred/queued, so a later --resume gets the task twice
findings.scenario: A teammate crashes (or the user types /exit) while a modal is open (Settings dialog -> _spawn_gate_pred True) or while another pane's ConPTY spawn is in progress (fan-out). 2.5 s later _auto_respawn calls spawn(), which returns (True, 'spawn deferred (gate blocked)' / 'spawn queued (arbiter busy)') WITHOUT spawning. _auto_respawn treats ok=True as spawned, reads the STALE last_spawn_resumed from the previous session (False for a first spawn) and calls _send_when_ready(cached_task). _send_when_ready is sticky for gate-deferred roles (lead_inbox.py:1705-1735) and waits for the session. When the deferred spawn finally runs it is inside RESUME_WINDOW_SEC, so it uses --resume: the conversation already contains the task and the pane then receives it pasted a second time -> duplicate/non-idempotent work (the exact Bug-5 the comment says it avoids).
findings.fix: Only replay when the spawn actually attached a session in this call (e.g. return a structured result / check pane.session.is_alive and that last_spawn_resumed was stamped by THIS spawn), or defer the replay decision into the deferred/queued retry path after the real spawn completes.

findings.title: Ledger state saved without invalidating cached_read → second assign within ~3s overwrites the first (row + open pointer lost)
findings.scenario: Lead fires two assigns in one burst (e.g. `takkub assign --role frontend … && takkub assign --role backend …`, a `--shards N` / `--plan` fan-out whose shards are staggered 400 ms apart by `_fire_qa_plan_fanout`, or `_drain_fanout_queue`). Assign #1: `_load_state` stats the file (mtime old → cached with recent=False), appends its row, `_save_state` writes. Assign #2 <3 s later: `read_cached` takes the no-stat fast path and returns the PRE-write parse; it appends its own row and saves → frontend's row and `open['frontend']` are gone from `.ledger-state.json` and INDEX.md. Frontend's later `takkub done` → `mark_done` finds no open pointer → silent no-op; Task dock / pending list / `get_open_scope` (cli.py:4891 guard) all see nothing. Same mechanism reverts boot `reconcile_orphaned` closures if an auto-respawn assign lands within 3 s.
findings.evidence: task_ledger.py:155-156 `def _save_state(project, state): _atomic_write(_state_path(project), json.dumps(...))` (no invalidate); task_ledger.py:124 `read_cached(_state_path(project), json.loads, ...)`; cached_read.py:82-83 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]`. backlog.py:128-130 does the invalidate this module lacks; memory note: same bug class already hit backlog (#684 lost update).
findings.fix: In `_save_state` after `_atomic_write(...)` add `from .cached_read import invalidate; invalidate(_state_path(project))` (mirror backlog.py:128-130). Optionally also invalidate in `_atomic_write` callers for detail files.

findings.title: attach_session steals keyboard focus to every newly spawned pane, including input-locked teammates
findings.scenario: User is typing into Lead. Lead runs `takkub assign` (or auto-respawn / limit_autoresume fires) -> spawn_engine._launch_session -> pane.attach_session() on the main thread -> `self._terminal.setFocus()` -> QWebEngineView of the new teammate pane takes focus. Teammate panes are input-locked by default (agent_pane.py:276-277), so the user's next keystrokes land in TerminalWidget._on_input_data and are silently dropped (terminal_widget.py:756-757) until they click back on Lead.
findings.evidence: agent_pane.py:664 `self._terminal.setFocus()` is unconditional; terminal_widget.py:978-979 `def setFocus(self): self._view.setFocus()`. No refocus-to-Lead anywhere (grep setFocus: only user_actions.py:434-444, which focuses the *shell* pane explicitly — the one case where focusing is wanted). Spawns run on the Qt main thread via cli_server `_mainThreadCall` (cli_server.py:112/307) while the user can be mid-draft.
findings.fix: Only call `self._terminal.setFocus()` when `not self._lockable` (user-driven Lead/Shell), or drop it entirely and rely on user_actions' explicit shell focus.

findings.title: Restart-successor boot path never starts auto_issue_signals.start_watch()
findings.scenario: After any `takkub restart` / status-bar restart / auto-update relaunch (TAKKUB_RESTART_SUCCESSOR=1), the cockpit boots through the early-return branch, so the #297 events.log pattern watcher (freeze / lost-delivery / watchdog auto-issues) is silently off until the next cold start.
findings.evidence: app.py:1176-1186 successor branch: `_boot_main_window`, `_install_signal_handlers`, `_start_deadman_watchdog`, `w.show()`, `return app.exec()` — no `start_watch()`. Normal path app.py:1345-1350 calls `from .auto_issue_signals import start_watch; start_watch()`. Only caller in the tree: app.py:1348.
findings.fix: Extract the post-window setup (signal handlers, deadman, start_watch, show, exec) into one helper used by both branches.

findings.title: Signal rule listens for event `no_content_pane_recover` that nothing emits → rule can never fire
findings.scenario: The watchdog's no-content recovery repeats 3+ times in 6 h (the #569 class of defect this rule was written for) but the emitted event names are `no_content_pane_warned` (lead_inbox.py:3246) / `no_content_pane_respawned` (maintenance.py:50 label), so `scan_for_signals` counts 0 and no auto-issue is ever filed; the operator gets no report for exactly the failure the rule documents.
findings.evidence: auto_issue_signals.py:157-158 `key="no_content_pane_recover", event="no_content_pane_recover"`; grep of src for `"no_content_pane_recover"` finds only this rule, maintenance.py's label dict and a comment in pty_session.py:2145; lead_inbox.py:3246 emits `"no_content_pane_warned"`.
findings.fix: Point the rule's `event` at the real emitted name (e.g. `no_content_pane_respawned`, or a rule per emitted event) and add a test that every `RULES[*].event` string appears in a `_log_event(` call in src.

findings.title: [caller of subsystem] Steady-state apply_pending() path walks the entire runtime/ tree every boot and silently skips when free disk < 4x runtime size
findings.scenario: _run_apply_pending calls `_disk_has_room(config.DATA_HOME)` every boot on 'v2'/'mixed'; `_estimate_copy_bytes` (170-239) does `_dir_size(data_home / "runtime")` (full os.walk of runtime/, 100k+ files on prod: browser-profiles 1.76 GB, exports 2.07 GB, core 1.16 GB) then doubles it, and the gate requires 2x that free. Nothing in runtime/ is copied on this path any more (runtime-triage already applied), so on a laptop with e.g. 6 GB runtime and < 25 GB free every boot reports 'skipped disk-space' only via progress_cb and apply_pending never runs (no version-marker re-pin, no self-heal), with no doctor finding. Also adds seconds of blocking I/O to every boot for nothing.
findings.evidence: auto_migrate_boot.py:193 `total = _dir_size(data_home / "runtime") if (data_home / "runtime").is_dir() else 0`; 238 `total = total * 2 + extra_backup_only`; 448-450 `if not _disk_has_room(config.DATA_HOME): ... return BootMigrationResult("skipped", "disk-space", messages)`. Prod runtime/ ~6.3 GB (measured).
findings.fix: Size the steady-state gate from what apply_pending would actually copy (promote candidates + archive candidates + pre-migrate entries), not runtime/ wholesale; log/doctor-surface a disk-space skip.

findings.title: _build_staging_mirror hardlinks the ENTIRE project tree (node_modules/.venv/dist included) into the repo root; a crash strands it there
findings.scenario: Settings → 'ดึง skill ตาม stack' → confirm install on a Node/Python project. The walk excludes only `.git` and `.claude/skills` (lines 584-587), not node_modules/.venv/dist/.next, so tens of thousands of hardlinks are created under `<project_root>/.autoskills-staging-<tok>/` (inside the repo, untracked, not gitignored): `next dev`/`tsc --watch`/WebStorm re-index the whole tree, `git status` shows the staging dir during the run, and if the cockpit is killed mid-install (or aborts via the SettingsWindow QThread bug above) the `finally: shutil.rmtree(staging)` at line 862 never runs and the full mirror stays in the user's repo permanently. On Windows `os.walk(followlinks=False)` still descends NTFS junctions (pnpm's node_modules/.pnpm layouts).
findings.evidence:
autoskills_installer.py:572 `staging = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=_STAGING_PREFIX, dir=str(project_root)))`
autoskills_installer.py:585 `dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != ".git" and d != staging.name]`
autoskills_installer.py:606 `os.link(src, dest)`
findings.fix: Prune the same ignore set the Explorer uses (IGNORED_NAMES: node_modules, .venv, venv, dist, build, .next, coverage, __pycache__) and git-ignored dirs; put the staging dir under RUNTIME_DIR/tmp (use copy for manifests only) or at minimum add `.autoskills-staging-*` to .git/info/exclude and sweep stale staging dirs on the next install.

findings.title: `backlog import` raises ValueError on any status cell not in STATUSES → partial import, duplicates on retry
findings.scenario: Owner runs `takkub backlog import` on an audit-report markdown table that has a สถานะ/status column ("ยังไม่แก้", "open", "✅ done"). `parse_markdown_table` copies the raw cell into `fields['status']` (line 361); `add_item(status=...)` raises `ValueError('invalid status: ...')` (line 166-167). `backlog_command` returns the error (orchestrator.py:11061), but every row before the bad one was already persisted by its own `_save` → half-imported list; re-running the import duplicates those rows.
findings.evidence: backlog.py:361 `fields[field] = val.strip(" `")` (status passes through raw); backlog.py:376 `created.append(add_item(project, title, **fields))`; backlog.py:166-167 `if status not in STATUSES: raise ValueError(...)`.
findings.fix: Normalise status like severity/impact: add a `_STATUS_WORDS` map (Thai labels + open/todo/done/blocked…) with fallback `"todo"` in `parse_markdown_table`; and/or validate all parsed rows before the first `add_item`.

findings.title: Phase-3 'ตรวจสอบ' events are re-labelled phase 4 on a first-time migration (max-phase clamp vs engine.validate() firing after archive) → verify row never active, archive row count overwritten, failed heading names the wrong phase
findings.scenario: First-time v1 apply: run_boot_stage runs `engine.apply()` (backup → promote → domain steps → archive copy → deferred prune, all firing on_entry for phases 1/2/4) and only THEN `engine.validate()` (auto_migrate_boot.py:652), which is where `on_validate_step` fires (engine.py:903). By then state['max_phase'] is 4, so every `emit(3, …)` from on_validate_step becomes phase 4: the 'ตรวจสอบ' row was already flipped to done when archive started, and the 'เก็บของเก่าเข้า archive' row's counter is overwritten with '5 / 12 ขั้น … 12 / 12 ขั้น' instead of its own 'k / N รายการ'. If validate fails at step 7, `_outcome_from_result` (930) sets `failed_phase=_phase_of_step(step)` = 2, so page E reads 'ขั้นที่ 2 คัดลอกขึ้นโครงใหม่ (7/12) ไม่ผ่าน' for a validation failure.
findings.evidence: boot_flow.py:615-616 `phase = max(phase, state["max_phase"])` / `state["max_phase"] = phase`; 829-837 `emit(3, done=position, total=verify_total, …)`; engine.py:880-907 validate() is a separate pass after apply(); boot_flow.py:930 `failed_phase = _phase_of_step(failed_step)` returns 1/2/4 never 3.
findings.fix: Exempt phase 3 from the clamp (track validate events with their own phase/clock; only clamp late phase-1/2 prune notifies to the current phase), and for a validate-report failure set `failed_phase=3`.

findings.title: Provider-update results are discarded and worker exceptions are swallowed unlogged → a failed update looks like 'nothing happened'
findings.scenario: User ticks claude on page A and clicks 'อัพเดตที่เลือก (1)'. `run_provider_updates` runs `provider_update.update_provider` which can return STATUS_FAILED (npm lock held by another instance, placeholder-binary check, npm error — provider_update.py:362-373). The window connects `resultReady` to `lambda _result: self._proceed_to_migration_check()` and `_progress_cb` is a no-op, so the header just flips to 'กำลังตรวจสอบโครงสร้างข้อมูล…' and the cockpit opens with the old CLI; the same update is offered again next boot with no explanation. Likewise `_on_provider_check_done` (2183), `_apply_remembered_choice._on_items` (2165) and `_on_plan_ready` (2221) receive `_WorkerError` and silently proceed — the exception text is never written to any log.
findings.evidence: 2204-2208 `def _progress_cb(*_args, **_kwargs): pass` … `worker.resultReady.connect(lambda _result: self._proceed_to_migration_check())`; 2221 `if isinstance(plan, _WorkerError) or plan is None:` with no `_LOG`/`_log_event` call.
findings.fix: After run_provider_updates, re-populate page A rows with the returned statuses and pause on any FAILED row (chip 'อัพเดตไม่สำเร็จ' + message) before proceeding; in every `_WorkerError` branch call `_LOG.exception`-equivalent (`_LOG.error('…', exc_info=err.exc)`) and `_log_event('boot_flow_worker_failed', stage=…)`.

findings.title: NativeChromeManager.ensure_started busy-waits up to 8 s (+5 s taskkill on failure) on the Qt main thread inside spawn()
findings.scenario: Windows, first spawn of qa/critic/designer after boot, or any spawn after the #406 idle-release killed the cockpit Chrome: spawn_engine.py:2445 calls manager.ensure_started() synchronously on the GUI thread; it Popen()s chrome.exe then loops `_cdp_ready()` (urlopen timeout 0.2 s) + `time.sleep(0.05)` until CDP answers (typically 1-4 s, up to _START_TIMEOUT_SEC=8) and on failure calls self.close() → `taskkill ... timeout=5` + `wait(3)`. Lead pane input lags/drops for the whole window — the same main_thread_stall class #406 moved the close() path off-thread for (orchestrator.py:2134-2138) but the start path was left synchronous.
findings.evidence: browser_chrome.py:183-192 `deadline = time.monotonic() + _START_TIMEOUT_SEC` / `while ...: if self._cdp_ready(): return ...` / `time.sleep(0.05)` then `self.close()`; spawn_engine.py:2445 `chrome_ok, chrome_msg = manager.ensure_started()` with no thread/timer.
findings.fix: Launch Chrome from spawn() but poll CDP readiness from a QTimer (or daemon thread + signal) and only log/notify when ready; never call close()/taskkill synchronously from the spawn path.

findings.title: takkub wait heartbeat/progress lines are block-buffered under a pipe — background wait looks hung until it exits
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub wait --role backend` as a background shell (the documented use, comments at lines 172-176 and 94-98). stdout is a pipe/file, Python block-buffers it (no PYTHONUNBUFFERED anywhere in the repo, no flush=True), so '[wait] watching…', '[wait] still waiting on…', '[wait] resolved: …' and the #431 '[wait] orchestrator ไม่ตอบ… retry' line all sit in the 8 KiB buffer and only appear when the process exits (up to 1800 s later). The #249 heartbeat that exists to tell 'still waiting' from 'hung' never shows.
findings.evidence: Verified live: `python -c "print('[wait] watching'); sleep(3); print('[wait] done')" | read -t 1.5` → NOTHING arrived within 1.5s. Code: `print(f"[wait] still waiting on {len(pending_keys)}: "` (3087) / `print(f"[wait] resolved: …"` (3081) / `print(f"[wait] orchestrator ไม่ตอบใน …"` (162) — all plain print(), and `_ensure_utf8_stdio` (3641-3646) only reconfigures encoding, not line_buffering.
findings.fix: In `_ensure_utf8_stdio` call `stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", line_buffering=True)` (or `write_through=True`), or add `flush=True` to every `[wait]` print in cmd_wait/_request_with_retry.

findings.title: _utf8_print writes to sys.stdout.buffer behind the TextIOWrapper — output order inverts vs print() when stdout is a pipe (tail/task show/worktree clean)
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub tail --role codex` from a pane (Bash tool → pipe). cmd_tail does `print(f"[{args.role}] {path}")` (2921, buffered in TextIOWrapper) then `_utf8_print(line)` per line (2926, written straight to .buffer and flushed) → the transcript lines print FIRST and the `[codex] <path>` header LAST. Same for `takkub task show` (2625 print header, 2626 _utf8_print body) and `worktree clean` (1378 print '(nothing to clean)' vs 1390-1393 _utf8_print orphan rows).
findings.evidence: Verified live: `print('A'); sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'B\n'); buffer.flush(); print('C')` piped → prints `B`, `A`, `C`. Code at 3651-3653: `if hasattr(sys.stdout, "buffer"): sys.stdout.buffer.write((text + "\n").encode("utf-8")); sys.stdout.buffer.flush()`.
findings.fix: Make `_utf8_print` call `sys.stdout.flush()` before the raw write, or simply `print(text)` — `_ensure_utf8_stdio()` already reconfigured stdout to UTF-8 in main(), so the raw-buffer path is unnecessary.

findings.title: assign --effort rejects xhigh/max at argparse although the flag's own help and provider_spec advertise them for claude
findings.scenario: Lead reads `takkub assign --help` ('claude alone also takes xhigh/max'), runs `takkub assign --role backend --effort xhigh "…"` → argparse: invalid choice: 'xhigh' (choose from 'low','medium','high'). The provider-aware validator that was meant to do this check (`assign_effort_override_error`, provider_config.py:864 `if spec.effort_levels and normalized not in spec.effort_levels`) is never reached.
findings.evidence: cli.py:5474 `choices=("low", "medium", "high"),` while cli.py:5483 help says `claude alone also takes xhigh/max` and provider_spec.py:714 `effort_levels=("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max")`.
findings.fix: Drop `choices=` on `--effort` (keep the help text) and let `assign_effort_override_error` validate per effective provider; or extend choices to include xhigh/max.

findings.title: assign dedup fingerprint is stamped before the synchronous subagent assign() result and refreshed on every hit — a corrected retry within 8 s is falsely acked as 'deduped'
findings.scenario: `takkub assign --role backend --mode subagent --model opus "task"` → orchestrator.assign returns `(False, "model override is not supported in subagent mode")` (orchestrator.py:2976). Lead drops `--model` and reruns the same task within 8 s → same (project, role, task_hash, 'subagent') key → reply `ok=True "task already queued for backend moments ago (deduped)"` while nothing was dispatched. Same for the async path when the deferred assign rejects and Lead retries; each retry refreshes the timestamp so the window slides.
findings.evidence: line 926-929: `fp = self._assign_fingerprint(project_ns_fp, role, req.get("task", ""), mode)` … `self._recent_assign_fingerprints[fp] = now_fp` (unconditional, before the check at 930 and before `assign()` at 941). `_assign_fingerprint` (line 407-413) excludes model/provider/effort/isolation/cwd.
findings.fix: Stamp the fingerprint only after a successful dispatch (`ok` True on the sync path, after `_fire_staggered` on the async path) and do not refresh it on a dedup hit; include model/provider/effort/isolation/cwd in the key.

findings.title: ensure_cli_shims is never idempotent for takkub.cmd on Windows (CRLF read as LF) — rewrites + os.replace on every spawn, racing panes executing the shim
findings.scenario: Installed (prod) cockpit on Windows: `_pane_cli_bin_dir` (spawn_engine.py:235) calls `ensure_cli_shims` on every pane spawn. `_cmd_shim` content is joined with `\r\n` (line 47) but `target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (140) applies universal newlines and returns `\n`, so `current != content` is always True → tmp write + `os.replace` of `<DATA_HOME>/bin/takkub.cmd` on EVERY spawn and every `takkub doctor`.
