A pane that is executing `takkub.cmd` (hooks fire `takkub _guard` on every Bash call) at that instant makes `os.replace` raise PermissionError/sharing violation → spawn_engine.py:236-240 silently falls back to `CLI_BIN_DIR` (venv Scripts on PATH) — exactly the #341/#696 exposure the shim was added to remove, with only a `cli_shim_write_failed` event as breadcrumb.
findings.evidence:
Verified: `io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO(b'@echo off
REM x
'), encoding='utf-8').read()` → `'@echo off
REM x
'`. Code: `return "
".join(` (47) vs `current = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (140) and docstring claim `Idempotent: rewrites only when content differs` (130).
findings.fix: Compare bytes: `current = target.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")` (or `target.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="")`) so CRLF survives the comparison; optionally use a per-process tmp name to avoid two writers sharing `.takkub.cmd.tmp`.

findings.title: load_projects() reads the V2 project registry/projects.json uncached on every 2s status tick from the Qt main thread
findings.scenario: status_header._status_timer fires every 2s (status_header.py:650-653 → _update_status) and calls _refresh_overage_chip (line 994), _refresh_plan_badge (line 1014) and _update_provider_chip (line 667), each doing config.active_project() → load_projects() → `registry_path.exists()` + `read_text()` + json.loads — 3-4 full file reads per tick on the main thread. On the wedged-disk condition cached_read.py was written for (#386: 'the SAME reads sat in pathlib.open / read_text for 1-10s each'), every tick blocks the UI; cached_read.py:5-8 explicitly claims 'the projects registry (config.active_project)' is served through the stat cache, but config.py never calls read_cached — the invalidate at config.py:139 for this file is a no-op.
findings.evidence: config.py:624-626 `if registry_path.exists():` / `registry = json.loads(registry_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`; config.py:641 `data = json.loads(PROJECTS_JSON.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`; status_header.py:651-652 `self._status_timer.setInterval(2_000)` / `timeout.connect(self._update_status)`
findings.fix: Route both reads in load_projects through cached_read.read_cached(path, json.loads, missing=None) (it already has the invalidate hook in _write_json_atomic), keeping the same fallback/warning behaviour on parse errors.

findings.title: BrainStore appends via whole-file read-modify-replace with no lock -> concurrent done() threads silently drop memory records
findings.scenario: BrainStore builds JsonlStore(path) with the default true_append=False, so every append_event reads the whole project .jsonl, writes a tmp and os.replace()s it (jsonl_store.py:56-62). orchestrator.done()/subagent_done() start a NEW daemon thread per done for brain.facade.on_pane_done (orchestrator.py:8140-8150, 2600-2605), and each on_pane_done does 2-4 appends. When two panes of the same project finish close together (shard fan-out, qa + reviewer, pipeline hops) thread B's `existing = read_bytes()` predates thread A's os.replace, so B's replace overwrites A's line — A's record is gone with no error. On Windows, os.replace while the other thread's load_active()/read_text() has the file open raises PermissionError, which facade.submit swallows (facade.py:95-101) -> record lost, one log line.
findings.evidence: store.py:77 `self._jsonl = JsonlStore(brain_store_path(project))`; jsonl_store.py:56 `existing = self._path.read_bytes() if self._path.exists() else b""` ... :62 `os.replace(tmp, self._path)`; the docstring (jsonl_store.py:5-8) only anticipates frequency, not concurrency.
findings.fix: Construct BrainStore's JsonlStore with true_append=True (the brain log is append-only by design, store.py:5-12) or guard append_event/load with a module-level threading.Lock per path.

findings.title: Conversation JSON writers never invalidate the stat-TTL read cache -> stale summary/cursor reads for 3 s
findings.scenario: summary.load_summary, store.get_conversation and cursor_store.get_cursor/set_cursor all read through core.storage.legacy_reader.read_json -> cached_read.read_cached, which (cached_read.py:82) serves a cached entry for 3 s WITHOUT a stat when the file was not recently written. write_json_atomic (used by save_summary, get_or_create, set_cursor, checkpoint) never calls cached_read.invalidate(). Concrete path in facade._on_pane_done_impl: line 127 load_summary (caches the pre-done summary, last written minutes ago), line 129 save_summary, line 131 CheckpointManager.create -> checkpoint.py:87 load_summary again within milliseconds -> returns the pre-done summary, so every checkpoint's summary.json is one done() behind. Same window makes context_builder._recent_summary_lines (called from _inject_v2_context on an assign fired <3 s after that role's done, e.g. a fix-loop re-assign) inject the pre-done summary. This is the exact 'store using cached_read must invalidate on _save' trap the project memory records as already hit twice; other writers do it (backlog.py:130, provider_config.py:128, core/storage/v2_target.py:200).
findings.evidence: _json_io.py:16-17 `tmp.write_text(...)` / `os.replace(tmp, path)` — no invalidate. cached_read.py:82 `if hit is not None and not hit[3] and mono - hit[2] < _STAT_TTL_S: return hit[1]`. facade.py:127-131 load_summary -> save_summary -> CheckpointManager(cs).create (which calls load_summary at checkpoint.py:87).
findings.fix: Call `cached_read.invalidate(path)` right after os.replace in write_json_atomic (and in JsonlStore.append for true_append paths read via read_json, if any).

findings.title: Claude transcript ingest looks in the wrong project dir and falls back to an unrelated session
findings.scenario: Any claude teammate pane runs `takkub done`. orchestrator.done() (orchestrator.py:7936-7946) spawns conversation.facade.on_pane_done -> ingest_provider_transcript -> claude_adapter.resolve_source(cwd, session_id). It calls find_session_by_uuid(cwd, session_id, config_dir=None) with no project_ns/base_role/project_dir_name, so it only checks `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl`. Since #516 F1 every non-Lead pane writes to `takkub-project-<ns>-<role>/` (pane_env.claude_project_dir_name, pane_env.py:567-569), so the uuid is never found and the code falls back to find_latest_session(cwd) = newest file in the legacy encoded-cwd dir, i.e. a different, possibly the user's own hand-run, Claude session (exactly what token_meter.py:255-266 / #129 forbids). On an installed build CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is DATA_HOME/claude-config (config.py:262-264) but the adapter still reads ~/.claude, so either nothing or a foreign session is ingested. The role's conversation store, bindings and checkpoints then hold an unrelated transcript; the pane's real transcript is never ingested.
findings.evidence: claude_adapter.py:25-28: `path = find_session_by_uuid(cwd, session_id, config_dir) if session_id else None` / `if path is None: path = find_latest_session(cwd, config_dir=config_dir)`. On this machine runtime/core/conversation_ingest_cursors.json has 4 keys all under `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-monch-WebstormProjects-agent-takkub/`, while the backend pane sessions live in `~/.claude/projects/takkub-project-agent-takkub-backend/` (80 files, newest 2026-09-15) — none of the 4 ingested uuids exist in any takkub-project-* dir.
findings.fix: Thread the pane's `_claude_config_dir` and `_claude_project_dir_name` (already on PtySession, agent_pane.py:888-889) through facade.on_pane_done -> ingest_provider_transcript -> adapter.resolve_source, or reuse token_meter.resolve_pane_session(provider, cwd, session_uuid=, not_before=spawn_ts, config_dir=, project_dir_name=). Remove the find_latest_session fallback for claude (uuid-only, per #129).

findings.title: Non-claude ingest binds the newest session in cwd with no spawn-time bound -> sibling pane's transcript attached to this role
findings.scenario: codex/gemini/cursor/kimi panes never get a cockpit-minted session id (agent_pane.py:869-872, token_meter.py:470-476), so done() passes session_id=None and codex_adapter.resolve_source -> _scan_root_for_cwd picks the newest rollout whose cwd matches (102-120); gemini_adapter.resolve_source (74-78) and cursor/kimi do the same. Two panes of the same provider sharing a cwd (routine for a single-repo project, #129) -> the OTHER pane's newer rollout is ingested into and bound to this role's conversation (bindings.jsonl, messages.jsonl). token_meter.resolve_pane_session already bounds this with not_before=spawn_ts but the ingest adapters take no such argument.
findings.evidence: codex_adapter.py:106-108 `candidates = sorted(root.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True)`; :127 `wanted_id = str(session_id or "").strip()` then any cwd match wins when empty.
findings.fix: Plumb the pane's spawn timestamp (`pane._spawn_ts`) through facade.on_pane_done -> ingest_provider_transcript -> resolve_source(cwd, session_id, not_before=...) and skip candidates older than it, mirroring token_meter.resolve_pane_session.

findings.title: After one `done --fail`, stale `next: fix:` and `pending:` lines are injected into every later assign for that role
findings.scenario: qa runs `takkub done --fail "tests red"` -> apply_done_note sets next_action="fix: [qa] tests red" and prepends the entry to pending/warnings (lines 117-125). qa later fixes it and runs `takkub done "tests green"` (different headline). The success branch (126-134) only removes a pending entry equal to the NEW headline and never touches next_action, so the summary keeps next_action="fix: [qa] tests red" and pending=["[qa] tests red"] forever. context_builder._recent_summary_lines (context_builder.py:204-209) renders `- pending: [qa] tests red` and `- next: fix: [qa] tests red` into the "## Context (Takkub brain)" block of every subsequent qa assign (TAKKUB_V2_CONTEXT is default-on), telling the pane to fix a failure that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: summary.py:122 `next_action=f"fix: {entry}",` (failed branch); success branch 126-134 has no `next_action=` and `pending=[x for x in summary.pending if x != entry]` only drops an exact-headline match.
findings.fix: In the success branch set next_action="" and drop pending/warnings entries tagged `[{role}]` (or all entries older than this success); alternatively clear pending on any clean done for the same role.

findings.title: Every apply_pending()/validate() sha256-hashes the entire archive (191k files / 10.5 GB on prod) before MainWindow can open
findings.scenario: apply_pending() line 532 calls ArchiveV1LegacyStep.validate() up front; that walks every backups/v1-archive-* generation and _archive_entry_problems() re-hashes every recorded file (promote_v1.py:2986, 1455-1461). validate() (898) and validate_ok_steps() (958) do it again; a WAL resume in apply_copy_only additionally re-hashes each SOURCE_PRUNED entry's dest (_verified_target_intact). _run_apply_pending also calls _disk_has_room -> _estimate_copy_bytes which os.walks the whole runtime/ tree (auto_migrate_boot.py:193). The gate must finish before MainWindow is constructed, so on a real install this is a multi-minute boot stall every boot (worker thread, but boot is blocked on it). Hidden today only because the wizard never reaches apply_pending().
findings.evidence: engine.py:532 `v1_retired = archive_step is not None and archive_step.validate().ok`; promote_v1.py:2953 `for gen in _all_archive_generation_dirs(self.data_home):` ... 2986 `problems = _archive_entry_problems(gen, manifest)`; 1460 `if _sha256(target) != expected:`. Prod: backups/v1-archive-1789137187.587171 = 191,305 files / 10,544.6 MB; runtime/ = 244,050 files (PowerShell walk alone 21.3 s).
findings.fix: Validate archives by manifest presence/size (or a sampled subset) on the boot path and reserve full sha256 verification for `takkub migrate validate`/doctor; cache the disk estimate or skip _estimate_copy_bytes when no promote/archive candidates exist.

findings.title: One legacy-v2 marker rmdir failure leaves a generation PENDING forever: every later pass is blocked by _stale_generation_problems and restore-v1 hides that generation
findings.scenario: Windows: `_rmdir_tree(legacy_root)` (2840) fails once (Explorer/indexer handle on DATA_HOME/v2). Branch 2849-2867 writes the manifest with state PENDING and says 'retry apply to finish', but `_prune_phase` already cleared the WAL (1221), so prune() for that generation can never run again. Next pass: apply_copy_only() opens a NEW empty generation; `_downgrade_on_health` -> `_health_problems` -> `_stale_generation_problems` reports the old generation 'incomplete' (2587-2591) -> no step prunes -> v2/ never removed -> layout_state() stays 'mixed' -> migration wizard shows every boot, forever. `takkub migrate restore-v1` with no --archive: `_find_latest_manifest` skips PENDING (1425-1426) and rollback() reports 'no v1-archive found - nothing to restore' (3042-3045) although that generation holds every archived source (already pruned). validate() (2953-2994) meanwhile never checks the COMPLETE flag, so the two checks disagree.
findings.evidence: promote_v1.py:2587-2591 `if not _manifest_is_complete(manifest):\n                problems.append(f"archive generation {gen.name} is incomplete (crashed or in-progress)")`; 2854 `"state": "PENDING",  # legacy v2/ marker not archived yet`; 1425-1426 `if _manifest_is_complete(manifest):\n            return m`.
findings.fix: In the marker-failure branch keep the WAL (or write a marker-only WAL) so prune() can finish the SAME generation; in _stale_generation_problems treat a PENDING generation whose archived entries all verify and whose sources are gone as complete (or auto-promote it to COMPLETE); make _find_latest_manifest fall back to such a generation.

findings.title: Leftover archive WAL pins apply_copy_only to the old entry list; new candidates never archived, archive copy refreshed from live files
findings.scenario: _prune_phase leaves the ledger on disk when late_write_kept is non-empty (1220-1221) and the step never clears it afterwards. On the next apply, apply_copy_only() sees ledger.exists() and rebuilds new_entries from the WAL instead of rescanning (2675-2678), so the docstring promise at 816-818 ('kept file picked up by the NEXT candidate scan') never happens while the WAL exists; prune() then hits the kept, still-changing source again, _remove_entry_source refreshes the ARCHIVE copy with the file's current live content (987-988) and keeps it again — validate() stays red forever, freshly appeared top-level files are never archived, and the 'archive' silently tracks live edits.
findings.evidence: promote_v1.py:2675-2678 `if ledger.exists():` / `meta = ledger.read_meta()` / `new_entries = [_entry_from_wal(rec) for rec in ledger.read().values()]`; 1220-1221 `if not late_write_kept:` / `ledger.clear()`; 987-988 `copy_only(p, entry.dest / rel)` / `digests[rel] = _sha256(entry.dest / rel)`. Prod: backups/archive-v1-legacy-wal.json (47.7 MB, 29 entries all state PRUNED) still present 11 days after the journal recorded 'archived 29 item(s)' ok; `context/` and `graft-graphs/` from that WAL are still at DATA_HOME top level.
findings.fix: After a successful prune, clear the WAL even when late writes were kept (record kept names in the manifest instead), and have apply_copy_only merge a fresh candidate scan into resumed WAL entries rather than replacing it.

findings.title: core-internal-store re-apply clobbers live core_home() JSONL/brain stores with the frozen runtime/core copy
findings.scenario: After the flip, core_store_path() and brain/store.py write straight into system/ (accounts.jsonl, account_pools.jsonl, account_switches.jsonl, models.jsonl, model_profiles.jsonl, obsidian_dedup.jsonl, brain/<project>.jsonl, conversations/) while runtime/core/ keeps the frozen pre-migration copy. _REENTRY_EXCLUDED_NAMES only exempts version.json and conversation_ingest_cursors.json, so the first appended record to any other top-level jsonl makes validate() (1183 byte-compare) red every boot; apply_pending then re-applies: _copy_entry copies the frozen file over the live one (copy2) and copytree(dirs_exist_ok=True) overwrites same-named brain/*.jsonl and conversations/* — every record appended since migration is lost, every boot, and backups.backup(system/) (1119) copies the whole system/ tree into migration_backups each time (never rotated).
findings.evidence: steps_v1.py:1059-1061 `_REENTRY_EXCLUDED_NAMES: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(` / `{"version.json", "conversation_ingest_cursors.json"}`; 1131-1134 `for name in entries: if name in self._REENTRY_EXCLUDED_NAMES: continue` / `self._copy_entry(source / name, target / name)`; writers: core/accounts/registry.py:66,95, core/accounts/switch_log.py:34, core/model_catalog/registry.py:65,94, obsidian_dedup.py:26, core/brain/store.py:49 all resolve through core_home(). Prod runtime/core currently holds only brain/, conversations/ + the 4 excluded files, so not yet triggered there.
findings.fix: Exclude every core_home()-resolved store from re-apply (or skip re-apply entirely once target exists and only check existence, as the dir branch already does); never copytree-merge brain/ and conversations/ on re-apply.

findings.title: CoreInternalStoreStep.apply() copies the whole system/ store into a new BackupManager slot on every apply and nothing ever rotates slots (1.18 GB on prod)
findings.scenario: Every apply() unconditionally runs `self.backups.backup(self.step_id, target)` where target = system/ (conversations, brain, model catalog). BackupManager.backup (backup.py:31-45) always creates a new timestamped slot with a full copytree and has no retention. Pre-#486/#488 the step re-applied on ~every boot (journal shows 'core-internal-store ... 4 entrie(s)' after almost every version-marker line), and the same pattern is still in RegistryCopyStep/RoleAgent/Project apply() (a 'kept' target is backed up again each re-apply). runtime/core is also inside the disk-gate's `_dir_size(runtime)` estimate, so the churn inflates the very number that can make the gate skip.
findings.evidence: steps_v1.py:1119 `self.backups.backup(self.step_id, target)`; prod ~/.agent-takkub/runtime/core/migration_backups/core-internal-store = 48 slots, 1,180.8 MB; version-marker = 59 slots; runtime/core = 1.16 GB total.
findings.fix: Skip the backup when apply() is a no-op merge (target already validates), and add per-step slot retention in BackupManager (keep N newest, or one per app version).

findings.title: read_all decodes strictly (no errors='replace') so a torn/partial UTF-8 line raises UnicodeDecodeError instead of counting as corrupt — silently kills the V2 conversation done-hook thread
findings.scenario: V2 conversation is ON by default (conversation/flag.py:1). On every done(), orchestrator.py:2574-2579 runs facade.on_pane_done on a bare daemon thread (no try/except); it appends messages via JsonlStore(true_append=True) (conversation/store.py:148) and reads back bindings/messages via read_all (store.py:164, 215). A >8KB done-note / ingested transcript line is written as two syscalls (line bytes, then b'\n'); a concurrent reader (remote/notify.py:1814 phone poll, a second done() thread, a crash mid-write) can observe a partial multibyte sequence (Thai text is 3 bytes/char) → `read_text(encoding='utf-8')` raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is NOT JSONDecodeError → propagates. On the daemon thread it dies silently (pythonw has no stderr) so summary/checkpoint/binding for that done() are never written; notify.py:1826 swallows it and silently falls back to the scanner history.
findings.evidence: jsonl_store.py:69 `for raw_line in self._path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():`; jsonl_store.py:97 `raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` (read_from is tolerant, read_all is not); jsonl_store.py:2-3 docstring promises 'bad lines skipped and counted, never raised'
findings.fix: In read_all use `self._path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` (same as read_from) and have JsonlStore.append write `line + b"\n"` in one write() call; wrap facade.on_pane_done's thread body in try/except that logs `conversation_v2_hook_error`.

findings.title: write_data → registry_copy_step.write_json_atomic: unconditional fsync (file + dir) and no PermissionError retry on os.replace — every V2 settings save stalls the main thread and can fail unhandled on Windows
findings.scenario: User changes a role's model/provider in Settings → role_models.py:161/205 write_data (twice) + provider_config.py:124 _write_routing → each call does tmp.write_text + os.fsync(tmp) + os.replace + dir fsync on the Qt main thread. #658 measured FlushFileBuffers under an AV filter at ~1s and made fsync opt-in in config._write_json_atomic (config.py:118-122) for exactly these small main-thread settings files — but all post-#504 V2 writers use write_json_atomic which always fsyncs, so a Settings save freezes the UI 1-3s on such machines. Separately, os.replace at registry_copy_step.py:51 has no sharing-violation retry (config.py:130-140 exists because 'Windows can transiently reject replacement while an AV scanner or another reader still has the destination open'); the remote HTTP thread reading routing/role-models via read_cached while the main thread replaces → PermissionError propagates out of the save slot, the change is silently not persisted.
findings.evidence: registry_copy_step.py:49-51 `with open(tmp, "r+b") as f:` / `os.fsync(f.fileno())` / `os.replace(tmp, path)`; v2_target.py:199 `write_json_atomic(target, {"schema": 1, "updated_at": time.time(), "data": data})`; config.py:127-128 `if durable:` / `os.fsync(f.fileno())` (opt-in, #658)
findings.fix: Give write_json_atomic a `durable: bool` flag (default False for v2_target.write_data, provider_config._write_routing, pane_tools_policy, skill_policy, custom_roles, auto_issue_capture; True only for migration ledgers/WAL) and reuse config._write_json_atomic's bounded PermissionError retry loop around os.replace.

findings.title: create_role silently overwrites an existing custom role's registry entry and instructions .md
findings.scenario: User opens Settings → New Role and types the id of a custom role that already exists (typo / forgot it exists). validate_role_name only rejects built-in names; create_role does `previous = roles.get(name)` and proceeds, then `tmp_path.replace(role_file)` replaces the role's hand-written .md with the new text — or the default template when the instructions box is blank (legacy settings_window.py:3544 passes None). No confirm, no undo. Reachable from the default legacy window (settings_window.py:3532-3546 has no existence check) and the new UI (roles_page.py:369-377 / repositories/roles.py:117-141).
findings.evidence: custom_roles.py:232-234 `roles = load_custom_roles()` / `previous = roles.get(name)` / `roles[name] = Role(...)` · :240 `tmp_path.replace(role_file)` · settings_window.py:3546 `ok, err = custom_roles.create_role(name, label, self._nr_color, column, row, instructions)`
findings.fix: In create_role return (False, 'มี custom role นี้อยู่แล้ว — แก้ไขแทน') when name in load_custom_roles() or role_file.exists(); make the UI route an existing name to the edit path instead.

findings.title: DB preflight false-negatives (mongodb+srv, prod DATABASE_URL) make qa-gate fail-fast and skip the entire test tier
findings.scenario: Project .env has `DATABASE_URL=mongodb+srv://cluster0.x.mongodb.net/app` (Atlas): urlsplit gives port None → `_DEFAULT_PORTS['mongodb+srv']` = 27017 → socket.create_connection((srv-hostname, 27017)) fails (an SRV name has no A record / no listener) → ok=False → qa_gate.py:1843-1848 marks every remaining check `test-db-preflight failed — fail-fast` and qa_gate.py:2148-2154 skips pytest/ruff/lint-imports. Same outcome when DATABASE_URL points at a firewalled/remote prod DB while the test suite uses sqlite/testcontainers (no TEST_DATABASE_URL set): the gate reports a FAIL for a DB the tests never touch.
findings.evidence: db_preflight.py:38-39 `"mongodb": 27017,` / `"mongodb+srv": 27017,`; db_preflight.py:103 `with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S):`; qa_gate.py:1843-1844 `if not db_finding.ok:` / `for rest in checks[index:]:`
findings.fix: Treat `mongodb+srv` (and any scheme without a resolvable literal port) as skipped; only fail-fast when the URL var is TEST_DATABASE_URL or the host is loopback/docker-local, otherwise downgrade an unreachable generic DATABASE_URL to a WARN step instead of skipping the suite.

findings.title: detect_investigate_task falls back to the DONE NOTE headline → a note saying 'ready for review' mutes the #278 zero-files alarm on an implementation task
findings.scenario: backend is assigned 'implement X'. It reports `takkub done` with note 'Implemented X — ready for review' but touched 0 files (the #278 incident shape). orchestrator.py:8078 passes `raw_note`; the first line matches `\b(review)\b` → investigate_task=True → `_files_bit` renders 'ไฟล์ที่แตะ: 0 (งานตรวจสอบ/read-only — 0 คือผลลัพธ์ที่ถูกต้อง)' instead of the ⚠️ alarm. Contradicts #244's rule that identity/verdict never comes from the agent's own prose.
findings.evidence: digest_facts.py:153 `for text in (task_text or "", note or ""):` … 158-160 `first_line = text.strip().split("\n", 1)[0]` / `if _INVESTIGATE_HEADLINE_RE.search(first_line): return True`; orchestrator.py:8078 `investigate_task = detect_investigate_task(_assigned_task_text, raw_note)`
findings.fix: Only accept the weak headline words from the ASSIGNMENT text; for the note fallback require a strong marker (`_INVESTIGATE_STRONG_RE`) or drop the note fallback entirely.

findings.title: Default `takkub doctor` reads every transcript line of the last 14 days (measured 301 files / 410 MB / 10.6 s here) for the tools-drift check
findings.scenario: `check_claude_tools_drift` is in `run_all_checks()` (l.234 via check_claude) so every `takkub doctor`, `doctor --fix` (which runs it twice, cli.py:3661+3665) and the Doctor button walk `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (+ DATA_HOME/claude-config/projects on prod) and json-parse each tool_use line. Measured on this machine: 301 files, 410.6 MB, 10.6 s; grows with usage. The module docstring promises 'pure-logic checks' with only one network probe.
findings.evidence: l.299 `candidates = list(s_dir.glob("**/*.jsonl"))`; l.312-314 `with fpath.open(...) as fh:\n    for line in fh:\n        if "tool_use" not in line:` — no byte cap, no per-file cache, no newest-N limit.
findings.fix: Cap to the N most-recent files / a total byte budget, or cache the extracted tool set keyed by (path, mtime, size) under runtime/, and make the full scan opt-in (`--tools-drift`).

findings.title: Editor diff-vs-HEAD uses roots[0] as the git repo root -> wrong/empty diff for multi-root or sub-directory roots
findings.scenario: Project has two configured paths (web, api) or a single path that is a subdirectory of the repo. Diff on a file under the 2nd root: `relative_to(roots[0])` raises -> read_head_blob returns None -> whole file rendered as newly added. For a sub-dir root, `git show HEAD:<rel-to-subdir>` resolves from the repo top-level and misses -> same wrong 'all added' diff or 'Diff unavailable'.
findings.evidence: editor_widget.py:738 `worker = _DiffWorker(roots[0], roots, Path(path), MAX_EDITOR_FILE_BYTES)`; :180 `rel = _safe_resolve(abs_path).relative_to(_safe_resolve(Path(repo_root))).as_posix()`; git_changes_service.py:215 `resolve_repo_root` (rev-parse --show-toplevel) exists for exactly this (GAP-009) but is not used here.
findings.fix: Resolve the repo root with git_changes_service.resolve_repo_root(resolved.parent) (or the configured root that contains the file) and compute `rel` against it in build_diff_result/read_head_blob.

findings.title: agy workspace miss-cache keyed on the main .db (mtime,size) never invalidates under WAL — a session probed too early stays 'unknown workspace' for the cockpit's lifetime
findings.scenario: gemini pane spawns; the notifier's dir-signature check (conversations dir mtime bumps when the new .db/-wal/-shm appear) triggers an immediate rescan; _antigravity_workspace() opens the brand-new db before agy has committed the trajectory_metadata_blob row (or gets SQLITE_BUSY during -shm setup, timeout=0.2) → None → `_agy_ws_miss[key] = (mtime_ns, size)` of the MAIN file. agy's dbs are WAL (this machine: 500 .db, 498 -wal/-shm), so the blob commit lands in -wal and the main file's signature never changes → every later find_antigravity_sessions() skips the db → Remote mirror / history / token badge for that gemini pane stay blank until cockpit restart (session_uuid is None for gemini spawns, token_meter.py:470-476, so only this scan can find it).
findings.evidence: gemini_helper.py:366-367 `st = db_path.stat(); sig = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)`; :370-375 `if _agy_ws_miss.get(key) == sig: return None` ... `_agy_ws_miss[key] = sig`; :395 comment acknowledges `-wal/-shm siblings are ignored`.
findings.fix: Fold the `-wal` sibling's (mtime_ns,size) into `sig` (or stat both and take the max), and give miss entries a short TTL (e.g. 10 s) so a transient lock/early probe cannot pin a live session.

findings.title: First cold find_antigravity_sessions walk still runs synchronously on the caller — the Remote notifier QTimer (main thread) can be that caller (#701 residual)
findings.scenario: Boot with a live gemini Lead and Remote on: notify.py:2201 `_resolve_jsonl` → :924 resolve_antigravity_transcript → find_antigravity_sessions(cwd, limit=1) runs on the 200 ms QTimer; the single-flight only makes a SECOND concurrent caller return []. The first caller does the full 500-db sqlite walk (2-13 s measured in #701) on whichever thread it is on. The only off-thread warmer is the token-meter worker (agent_pane.py:897, 5 s tick) — it is a race which fires first, so roughly every other boot the GUI freezes once. Caches are process-lifetime (only tests call _reset_antigravity_caches), so it happens once per boot, and again whenever `limit` truncation keeps _agy_probed_all False.
findings.evidence: gemini_helper.py:426-434 `if not _agy_probed_all: if not _agy_scan_lock.acquire(blocking=False): return []` / `else: _agy_scan_lock.acquire()` then the walk at :439-450 runs inline; notify.py:2165-2168 documents this resolver path is on the Qt main thread.
findings.fix: Warm the cache from a daemon thread at boot / on gemini pane spawn, and have the main-thread resolver ALWAYS use the non-blocking path (return [] until warm) — e.g. pass `block=False` from notify's resolve_session.

findings.title: _read_current_text can raise OSError out of _DiffWorker.run → diffReady never fires, editor diff pane shows nothing
findings.scenario: User clicks a file in the Explorer CHANGES panel that another process holds open without share-read (Windows, e.g. a running app's db/log) or that a pane deletes/renames between the `exists()` check and `stat()`/`open()`. `resolved.stat()` / `resolved.open("rb")` raise PermissionError/FileNotFoundError; diff_sync only catches PathEscapesRootsError and ValueError, so the exception escapes the QRunnable. With app.py's custom excepthook (app.py:110) PyQt logs it instead of aborting, but `signals.finished` is never emitted, so editor_widget._on_diff_ready (:742) never gets a DiffResult or an `editorDiffFailed` call — the diff view just never loads.
findings.evidence: git_changes_service.py:310 `size = resolved.stat().st_size`, :313 `with resolved.open("rb") as fh:`, :317 `return resolved.read_text(...)`; diff_sync :337-344 catches only PathEscapesRootsError / ValueError; _DiffWorker.run :407-412 has no try/except.
findings.fix: Wrap the body of diff_sync (or _DiffWorker.run) in `except OSError as exc: return DiffResult(path=..., unified=None, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")` so the UI gets an error row.

findings.title: git subprocesses spawned on worker threads bypass project_file_index.SUBPROCESS_LOCK — the exact concurrent-CreateProcess pattern #375 documented as an interpreter crash
findings.scenario: Git tab visible (task_dock._GitStatusWorker on QThreadPool runs git_status.collect every 30 s) while the Explorer's _StatusWorker/_DiffWorker (lock-holding) and cli_server._run_off_thread's daemon thread (WorktreeManager()._default_runner for collect_done_git_facts on every `takkub done`) all call subprocess.run concurrently. git_changes_service.py:46-58 states concurrent subprocess.run from separate threads 'reproducibly crashed the interpreter with a Windows access violation inside CreateProcess' and that `_run_git` is 'the one locked entry point every git subprocess in this codebase should go through'; git_status._run_git and worktree_manager._default_runner do not take it.
findings.evidence: git_status.py:62 `proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], ...)` (no lock); worktree_manager.py:266 `proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], ...)` (no lock), invoked off-thread from cli_server.py:1159-1171 and task_dock.py:461.
findings.fix: Have git_status._run_git and worktree_manager._default_runner acquire `project_file_index.SUBPROCESS_LOCK` around subprocess.run (lazy import to keep the leaf contract), or route them through git_changes_service._run_git.

findings.title: Background `git status` polls take index.lock inside live panes' worktrees — pane `git commit`/`add` fails with 'index.lock: File exists'
findings.scenario: Git tab open in the Task dock: every 30 s _collect_worktrees runs `git status --porcelain` with cwd = each wt/* worktree (including ones a pane is actively working in); git_changes_service runs `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` on the shared root 1.5 s after every file change (a pane writing files triggers it continuously). Neither passes --no-optional-locks / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, so `git status` opportunistically writes the refreshed index under .git/index.lock (or .git/worktrees/<id>/index.lock). A pane's `git commit`/`git add -A` in the same window dies with "Unable to create '.../index.lock': File exists"; auto_commit_snapshot (worktree_manager.py:1604) returns False on that and the Lead gets the 'no commit kept' warning for work that is actually there.
findings.evidence: git_status.py:186 `dirty_out = _run_git(["status", "--porcelain"], wt_path, timeout_s)` (per worktree, every 30 s); git_changes_service.py:185 `["git", "status", "--porcelain=v2", "-z", "--untracked-files=normal"]`; git_status.py:231 `_run_git(["status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch"], top, timeout_s)`.
findings.fix: Set `env={**os.environ, "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"}` (or prepend `--no-optional-locks`) in git_status._run_git, git_changes_service._run_git and worktree_manager._default_runner for read-only probes (status/diff/rev-list), matching what VS Code and other IDEs do.

findings.title: Headless boot never runs the storage-migration ladder (run_boot_stage) before spawning panes
findings.scenario: `python -m agent_takkub.headless` (Docker/headless install) upgrades from 2.0.x or across releases: HeadlessWindow.boot() binds the CLI, starts remote control and spawns every Lead immediately. auto_migrate_boot's contract ('Callers MUST finish this stage before constructing MainWindow — a pane spawned mid-copy … would look like corruption to validate()') is never honoured: no first-time promote/archive, no per-boot apply_pending, version-marker never written; a headless machine stays on whatever layout it had forever and doctor --storage-layout reports v1/mixed.
findings.evidence: grep `run_boot_stage(` across src: only app.py:1046 (`_run_auto_migrate_headless`, TAKKUB_BOOT_UPDATE=0 path) and boot_flow.py:707/849; headless.py:85-99 `window = HeadlessWindow()` … `port = window.boot()` with no migration call; headless_window.py:78-109 likewise.
findings.fix: In headless.main(), before `HeadlessWindow()`, call `auto_migrate_boot.run_boot_stage(progress_cb=_log.info)` (same shape as app._run_auto_migrate_headless) and log the result; abort boot (return 1) on `rolled_back`/`error` so panes never write into a half-migrated tree.

findings.title: Non-claude Lead's AGENTS.md is written into the user's repo without the git-exclude that teammate AGENTS.md gets (and is overwritten by teammate cheatsheets in a shared cwd)
findings.scenario: Switch Lead to codex/gemini-agy/opencode (Settings or #698 menu). `render_lead_agents_md` writes ~20KB of cockpit policy to `<lead_cwd>/AGENTS.md` and returns; unlike `codex_agents_md.ensure_agents_md` (line 454 `_ensure_git_excluded(spawn_path, "AGENTS.md")`) it never adds the file to `.git/info/exclude`, so the user's repo shows an untracked AGENTS.md on every non-claude Lead session and `git add -A` commits cockpit policy into their project (same regression class #146 fixed for graft). Additionally, in a single-repo project where Lead and a codex/gemini teammate share the same cwd (#129 says this is routine), each spawn overwrites the marker-tagged file with the other role's content (ensure_agents_md:447-449 overwrites any marker file; render_lead_agents_md:908-913 likewise), so a Lead respawn/reroute (#699) can boot reading the specialist cheatsheet ('you are a specialist, do the task yourself').
findings.evidence:
lead_context.py:906-913 `target = pathlib.Path(spawn_cwd) / "AGENTS.md"` … `target.write_text(f"{TAKKUB_MARKER}\n\n{text}", encoding="utf-8")`
codex_agents_md.py:449-454 `target.write_text(CODEX_AGENTS_MD + extra, ...)` then `_ensure_git_excluded(spawn_path, "AGENTS.md")`
findings.fix: Call `codex_agents_md._ensure_git_excluded(spawn_path, "AGENTS.md")` after the write in render_lead_agents_md; for the shared-cwd case tag the marker with the role and refuse/merge instead of silently overwriting the other role's file.

findings.title: No-content watchdog measures from raw elapsed[0] (includes pre-session spawn-gate wait) → premature kill/respawn, second time degrades to claude
findings.scenario: A modal/dialog (Settings, QMenu) blocks ConPTY construction so spawn() defers (spawn_engine.py:2392-2401, retry every 50 ms with no ceiling; the 2026-07-11 dogfooding case was ~70 s). `_check` keeps polling with session None and `elapsed[0] += 150` (line 1718). When the pane finally spawns, `elapsed[0]` is already ≥ 60 s; the first polls with the session alive have `first_content_ts() is None` (normal for a codex/agy cold boot) and `elapsed[0] >= 75 000` → `_recover_no_content_pane` closes and respawns a pane that had been alive only seconds. The #356 fix added `elapsed_at_session_alive` for the boot ceiling (line 2217) but this check still uses the raw clock.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:2072 `if _no_content and elapsed[0] >= no_content_ceiling_ms:`; compare 2217 `boot_marker_elapsed_ms = elapsed[0] - (elapsed_at_session_alive[0] or 0)`
findings.fix: Use `elapsed[0] - (elapsed_at_session_alive[0] or 0) >= no_content_ceiling_ms`.

findings.title: _warn_lead_* helpers drop task-loss notices when the Lead pane is momentarily absent instead of letting _notify_lead queue them durably
findings.scenario: User restarts Lead (or switches Lead provider) while teammates are being assigned. During the few seconds Lead is down a spawn fails / a delivery hits the single-flight block (#339) / the 30 s prompt-block ceiling gives up without pasting (#484) / auth-failure or account-pending recovery fires. Every one of these helpers returns before `_notify_lead`, so nothing is written to `_pending_done_notices`; the new Lead never learns the task was never delivered. `_notify_lead` itself (4376-4389) already handles Lead-absent by queuing durably — the early return defeats it.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:2612-2613 `if not (lead and lead.session and lead.session.is_alive): return` — identical guard in _warn_lead_delivery_blocked (2699), _warn_lead_delivery_uncertain (2669), _warn_lead_spawn_failed (3616), _warn_lead_auth_failure (3104), _warn_lead_account_pending (3184), _warn_lead_pane_exited (3731).
findings.fix: Remove the Lead-alive guard from the 'task was NOT delivered' helpers (blocked, blocked_ceiling, spawn_failed, boot-timeout, auth/account) and rely on `_notify_lead`'s durable fallback; keep it only where the docstring justifies it (respawn-capped).

findings.title: Durable notice stores (_save_pending_done_notices / _save_pending_cc) are written non-atomically → a crash mid-write silently loses every queued notice
findings.scenario: The store exists precisely for crash/restart durability (#13). `write_text` truncates then writes; a cockpit crash/kill during the write leaves a partial JSON, `_load_pending_done_notices` (3815-3828) swallows the parse error and drops the whole project's queue — done reports spilled while Lead was busy vanish with no log line. `NoticeDeduper._persist` (task_delivery.py:583-586) already uses tmp+os.replace for the same reason.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:3802 `path.write_text(json.dumps(queue, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")`; same at 3766 for CC; 3767/3803 `except Exception: pass`
findings.fix: Write to `path.with_suffix('.tmp')` then `os.replace`, mirroring NoticeDeduper._persist; log the exception instead of `pass`.

findings.title: _force_deliver_done_notices never calls _mark_done_notices_delivered → `takkub inbox` later reports a delivered report as 'missing (#678)'
findings.scenario: Done notices spill to the durable queue (Lead on a prompt >30 s, draft-hold expired, Lead died mid-queue, or writer rejected) and the reaper force-delivers them after 60 s not-ready (`done_notice_force_flush`). The text lands in Lead's pane but `_done_unread[(ns, role)]` (set in done(), orchestrator.py:8236) is never cleared; 120 s later `inbox_report` (orchestrator.py:9429-9443) appends a 'missing … แจ้ง Lead เอง' item, and `takkub status` shows 'done (unread)' — the pane is told to re-report a report Lead already read.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:4647 `self._mark_done_notices_delivered(project_ns, body)` exists only in `_pump_lead_notify`; `_force_deliver_done_notices` (4838-4929) pops the durable queue at 4904-4905 and emits `leadInjected` at 4929 with no such call.
findings.fix: After the successful write at 4899-4905 call `self._mark_done_notices_delivered(project_ns, body)` (body already contains every rendered item).

findings.title: poll_wait uses the registration's started_ts, not the attaching client's → attached wait can report expired/‘never spawned’ on its first poll
findings.scenario: Lead is blocked in `takkub wait --timeout 1800` and the Lead pane is restarted (provider switch #698 / Restart Lead) — the CLI process dies without `end_wait`, its client entry lingers until `timeout+120s` after its last poll (line 229-233). 20 min later new Lead runs `takkub wait --role qa --timeout 600`: different role set → new client (line 276-294) with its own started_ts=now, but poll_wait computes `elapsed = now - active['started_ts']` (old) ≥ 600 → `expired=True` on the first poll → cli.cmd_wait line 3169 breaks → 'timeout with 1 role(s) still pending' after 0 s. Same staleness makes the 15 s never-spawned grace (line 413, `time.time() - started_ts`) already elapsed → a role assigned 2 s ago resolves 'gone: never spawned'.
findings.evidence: lead_wait.py:730 `client_started_ts = active.get("started_ts", now)`; 731 `client_timeout_s = client_info.get("timeout_s", active["timeout_s"])`; 778-779 `elapsed = now - client_started_ts` / `expired = elapsed >= client_timeout_s`; per-client `started_ts` stored at 280/308 is never read.
findings.fix: `client_started_ts = client_info.get('started_ts', active.get('started_ts', now))` and pass it to `_resolve_role_wait_status`/`_pending_user_input_interrupt`; for the same-role attach path (254-273) also record a per-client started_ts.

findings.title: Deny verdict built from up-to-5-min-old cached telemetry can override a live quota banner
findings.scenario: LimitStore polled 4 min ago at 93%; six panes burn 8% and one shows the banner. confirm_verdict_for_provider -> fetch_usage_shared(max_age_s=300) returns the cached 93% -> _usage_denies_limit -> 'denied' -> episode cleared as false positive, Lead told 'ไม่ได้ชนโควตา', no reroute. Pane stays frozen until the stuck watchdog force-respawns it (STUCK_THRESHOLD_S) and the next LimitStore poll (600 s cadence) finally shows 100%.
findings.evidence: L129: `usage = fetch_usage_shared(config_dir, max_age_s=300.0) if config_dir else None`   L134-135: `denied, pct = _usage_denies_limit(usage)` / `return ("denied", pct) if denied else ("unknown", 0.0)`
findings.fix: A 'denied' verdict must come from a fetch newer than the detection timestamp (pass max_age_s=0 / force refresh unless backed off) and/or require pct < threshold - margin; cached data may only produce 'confirmed' or 'unknown'.

findings.title: Quota reroute snapshot drops ps.worktree and last_assigned_task_file: rerouted --worktree pane never gets its branch merge-proposed
findings.scenario: Lead assigns backend with --worktree; backend hits quota on codex; _reroute_pane_to_provider calls close(keep_queue=True, suppress_pipeline=True, suppress_auto_chain=True) -> recovery_close, so close() pops _pane_state (orchestrator 6307) and skips _close_worktree_git (6332). _do_reroute_respawn rebuilds PaneState from scratch (L621-642) with cwd = old worktree path but ps.worktree=None and last_assigned_task_file=None. When the pane later runs `takkub done`, no worktree finalize/merge proposal happens; a later user close also finds had_worktree_close None -> orphan worktree + branch, `task show` loses the task file.
findings.evidence: L572-580 snapshot list: `snap_auto_chain`, `snap_requires_commit`, `snap_shard_total`, `snap_pipeline_run_id`, `snap_assign_*`, `snap_distinct_from` -- no `worktree`, no `last_assigned_task_file`, no `last_assigned_scope`.   L621-642 restores only those fields.
findings.fix: Snapshot and restore ps.worktree, last_assigned_task_file, last_assigned_scope (and task_delivered=False) alongside the existing fields; add a regression test with a worktree-assigned pane rerouted then done().

findings.title: Parked pane is force-respawned by the stuck watchdog at reset time, 3 min before the wake timer fires
findings.scenario: No reroute candidate -> _park_pane_for_limit; wake armed at reset_at + WAKE_BUFFER_S (180 s). At reset_at, orchestrator._rate_limit_suppressed (15031-15037) zeroes rate_limited_until; _emit_rate_limit_reset returns early for limit_parked (15155) WITHOUT the #53 last_content_change_ts stamp; _check_stuck_panes only skips `rate_limited_until > now` (13816) and has no limit_parked guard, so on the very next 5 s tick `content_stale = (now - last_content_ts) >= STUCK_THRESHOLD_S` (14037) is true (screen static for hours) -> _auto_recover_stuck close->respawn. _wake_parked_pane then finds ps popped / limit_parked False and no-ops; the pane got a hard respawn instead of the nudge, park round burned, Lead gets a 'stuck recovered' notice.
findings.evidence: L925-926: `delay_ms = max(0, int((reset_at + auto_resume.WAKE_BUFFER_S - time.time()) * 1000))` / `QTimer.singleShot(delay_ms, lambda: self._wake_parked_pane(project, role))`   orchestrator.py:13816: `if (self._pane_state.get(key) or PaneState()).rate_limited_until > now: continue`
findings.fix: Either set ps.rate_limited_until = reset_at + WAKE_BUFFER_S when parking, or make _check_stuck_panes skip ps.limit_parked, or stamp last_content_change_ts before the early return at orchestrator.py:15155.

findings.title: Claude's live .credentials.json is rewritten non-atomically, unlocked, by four independent threads/processes
findings.scenario: Token nears expiry; within the same seconds LimitStore._do_fetch, ProviderUsageStore (fetch_claude_usage -> fetch_usage_shared), the auto-resume confirm thread and the quota reprobe thread (plus a second cockpit instance on the same profile) each call fetch_usage -> _refresh_and_persist. Each POSTs a refresh with the same refresh_token and write_text()s the whole file. A kill/crash between truncate and write leaves an empty/partial credentials file -> every claude pane in the cockpit reports login lost; if the OAuth server rotates refresh tokens, the in-pane CLI holding the old token fails its next refresh.
findings.evidence: L206: `credentials_path.write_text(json.dumps(raw, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")`   L345-358 refresh decision has no lock; callers at limit_status.py:671, 526 and limit_autoresume.py:129 run on different threads.
findings.fix: Write via tmp + os.replace, serialize refresh behind a module-level lock (and the shared-state file for cross-process), and skip refreshing when the token is not yet expired for this fetch (or defer to the CLI as the keychain branch already does).

findings.title: describe_mcp_handshake('codex') counts `enabled=false` deny tokens as granted servers → doctor --pane reports denied MCPs as OK
findings.scenario: codex-cli 0.155.1 (installed here) is outside _CODEX_RESOLVE_SAFE_MAX_VERSION, so _codex_mcp_argv emits `-c mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false` for every inherited server not in the role's allowlist (:383-386). describe_mcp_handshake then regex-matches every `mcp_servers.<name>.` token, so server_names contains the DENIED names and has_mcp_config=True; `takkub doctor --pane qa` (doctor.py:1228-1237) prints them as `servers=[...]` with Status.OK, and a deny-all role (lead/codex) that got nothing shows OK instead of FAIL — misleading exactly when debugging #146/#304 'MCP never connected'.
findings.evidence: mcp_bridge.py:500-503 `for tok in mcp_argv: match = re.match(r"mcp_servers\.([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\.", tok)` / `names.add(match.group(1))` — no exclusion of `.enabled=false`.
findings.fix: Skip tokens ending in `.enabled=false` (or collect only `.command=` tokens) and derive has_mcp_config from the granted set.

findings.title: opencode resume picker / newest-session resolve scan only the 50 most recent sessions across ALL projects, then filter by cwd — busy projects vanish from the picker
findings.scenario: opencode.db is one machine-wide db (here 258 MB). list_recent_opencode_sessions runs `ORDER BY time_updated DESC LIMIT 50` with no directory filter and drops rows whose directory != cwd; once the user has >50 opencode sessions spread over projects, a project whose newest session is older than the global top-50 shows an empty resume picker (notify.py:1633-1638) even though it has history; resolve_opencode_session's newest branch (:237-243) has the same cap, so an ingest with not_before=0 (core/conversation/ingest/opencode_adapter.py:34) also fails. Here: 22 sessions / 12 dirs → not yet hit; 800 codex rollouts on the same machine show how quickly it will be.
findings.evidence: opencode_helper.py:411-416 `"SELECT id, directory, title, time_updated FROM session ORDER BY time_updated DESC LIMIT 50"` ... `if normalize_opencode_cwd(row["directory"]) != wanted_cwd: continue`.
findings.fix: Filter in SQL: `WHERE directory = ?` (try both raw and normalized forms, or `LOWER(REPLACE(directory,'\\','/')) = ?`) and only then LIMIT; same for resolve_opencode_session.

findings.title: _register_subagent / subagent_done run git worktree add and finalize inline on the Qt main thread
findings.scenario: `takkub assign --role docs --mode subagent --isolation worktree "..."` — cli_server handles mode==subagent synchronously on the QTcpServer slot (cli_server.py:940-961), assign() → `_register_subagent` → `WorktreeManager().create(...)` + `load_worktree_config` run inline (the #408 off-thread staging at cli_server.py:1014-1049 covers only pane mode). Later `takkub subagent-done` (cli_server.py:1174-1180, synchronous) → `subagent_done` → `_finalize_worktree` runs commit_count/real_dirty/merge_conflict_files/diffstat git subprocesses on the main thread (the exact class #640 moved off-thread for close()). Each freezes the cockpit UI (Lead typing lag, watchdog `main_thread_stall`) for the duration of the git work; on a large repo with post_create link copying this is seconds.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:2405 `info, warning = WorktreeManager().create(`; orchestrator.py:2627 `self._finalize_worktree(project_ns, role_name, state["worktree"], note=note)`; cli_server.py:940-941 `if cmd == "assign" and mode == "subagent":` / `ok, msg = self._orch.assign(`
findings.fix: Reuse the #408 staging for subagent mode: run `worktree_assign_inputs` + `WorktreeManager.create` via `_run_off_thread` and pass `worktree_prepared` into `_register_subagent`; run subagent_done's `_finalize_worktree` through the same worker used by `_close_worktree_git` (or cli_server's `_collect`/`_finish` off-thread pattern used for pane `done`).

findings.title: Subagent-assign path assigns create_assignment's (warning, path) tuple to `warning` → always truthy → _notify_lead raises → ledgerChanged never emitted
findings.scenario: Any `takkub assign --mode subagent`, and every auto-picked subagent assign (cli_server.py:848 `resolve_auto_assign_mode` chooses subagent for a <400-char task on claude with no model/provider/effort/shards/worktree, role not reviewer/critic). `create_assignment` returns `('', WindowsPath(...))`; `if warning:` is true; `_notify_lead(project_ns, warning, ...)` → lead_inbox.py:505 `(body or "").strip()` → AttributeError on tuple → swallowed by `except Exception` at 2506 → `ledger_hook_error stage=subagent-assign` logged on every such assign, `self.ledgerChanged.emit(project_ns)` skipped (Task dock / pending list not refreshed), and a genuine ledger write warning could never reach Lead.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:2491 `warning = create_assignment(` … :2501 `if warning:` … :2505 `self.ledgerChanged.emit(project_ns)`; task_ledger.py:231 `-> tuple[str, pathlib.Path | None]`; compare the correct pane path orchestrator.py:4051 `ledger_warning, _detail_path = create_assignment(`.
findings.fix: Change line 2491 to `warning, _detail_path = create_assignment(...)` (match line 4051).

findings.title: Governor re-admission closure drops subagent_fanout/scope/distinct_from/base_ref/team — --shards N silently becomes sequential
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub assign --role backend --shards 3 "..."` (or any assign with --scope deep / --distinct-from) while the ResourceGovernor denies the slot (machine overload latch, browser/heavy class cap — #543 shape). First pass sets `_fo_ps.subagent_fanout = 3` (line 2925). When the governor admits it, `on_admitted` re-calls `self.assign(...)` WITHOUT subagent_fanout/scope/distinct_from/base_ref/team, so line 2934-2937 (`elif not _fo_pane_alive: _fo_ps.subagent_fanout = 0`) clears the flag before spawn; spawn_engine.py:3573/3801 then read 0 and never add the Agent tool. The task text still carries the fan-out contract, so the pane runs the 3 shards one after another. `distinct_from` becomes None (PaneState.distinct_from=None at 4082 → quota reroute may pick the paired role's provider); Lead's explicit `--scope` is re-derived by `decide.scope()` and logged/ledgered as source="auto".
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:3099 `on_admitted=lambda token, r=role_name, c=cwd, t=task, rc=requires_commit, ac=auto_chain, st=shard_total, pl=plan, iso=isolation, p=project, f=feature, m=model, pr=provider, ef=effort, dp=detail_path, wp=worktree_prepared: (`  — no subagent_fanout/scope/distinct_from/base_ref/team; orchestrator.py:2934-2937 `elif not _fo_pane_alive:` / `_fo_ps.subagent_fanout = 0`; spawn_engine.py:3573 `[], _disallowed_tools, int(_ps_initial.subagent_fanout or 0)`
findings.fix: Capture and forward every assign() kwarg in the on_admitted closure (subagent_fanout, scope=resolved_scope, distinct_from, base_ref, team) — or build the closure from a single `assign_kwargs` dict; same for `_enqueue_assign`/`_drain_fanout_queue` (14798/14890).

findings.title: send() before task delivery: #586 merge appends to a task file a preloaded claude pane never reads, and the direct write has no ready-wait
findings.scenario: Lead assigns backend (claude, task preloaded via system prompt: `spawn_initial_task_state="delivered"`) and within the cold-boot window sends a follow-up `takkub send --to backend "อย่าลืม X"`. `task_delivered` is still False (only set when `_send_when_ready` pastes, lead_inbox.py:1445 — for preloaded panes that is the trigger paste, after boot), so send() appends the note to `last_assigned_task_file` and to `last_assigned_task`. The claude pane is told `_CURRENT_TASK_TRIGGER` = "Start the current task from the one-shot system-prompt block now." and never opens that file, so the merge is a no-op for claude. The body is also written immediately into the still-booting PTY (writer thread has no readiness gate; `_send_when_ready`'s ready-poll is only used for tasks) with a 30 s `expires_at` and no repaste (`payload=None`), landing in the trust/boot screen or being dropped, while the record stays "sent" until #705 retires it on the next assign. Lead's ack ("queued to backend") and `last_assigned_task` (now containing the note, replayed on auto-respawn) both misreport what the pane actually saw.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:5181-5195 `if not getattr(ps_send, "task_delivered", False) and getattr(ps_send, "last_assigned_task", None):` … `with _tf_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as _f:`; spawn_engine.py:277 `_CURRENT_TASK_TRIGGER = "Start the current task from the one-shot system-prompt block now."`; pty_session.py:1643-1647 (only `cancelled`/`expires_at` checked before `_proc.write`)
findings.fix: When the target's task is undelivered, do not write the body now: append it to the PENDING delivery (update `spawn_initial_task`/the DeliveryManager payload, or re-run `_send_when_ready` with the merged text) and skip the direct PTY write; for preloaded claude panes, merge into `spawn_initial_task` before the trigger is sent or queue the note via `_send_when_ready` after the trigger settles.

findings.title: send() to Lead writes straight into Lead's PTY, bypassing the Lead-inbox pump (draft guard, #133 single-chain lock, durability)
findings.scenario: A teammate follows IDLE_REMINDER_TEXT and runs `takkub send --to lead "blocked: ..."`. cli_server routes it to `orch.send("lead", ...)` (cli_server.py:1092), which has no Lead special-case: it calls `_safe_session_write` immediately with WritePriority.TASK and arms `_delayed_enter_verified`. The PTY writer thread pops and writes at once (pty_session.py:1633-1667, no readiness gate). So the message lands while the user is mid-draft in Lead's composer (the #3 `_lead_can_accept_injection` guard only protects `_pump_lead_notify`), or while a notify-pump `_delayed_enter_verified` chain is in flight (`_lead_notify_verify_active` is never checked here — exactly the two-chains race #133 fixed for notices). If Lead is restarting/rerouting (`session` dead), line 5073-5074 returns "lead is not running" and the message is dropped — unlike done notices, which fall back to `_pending_done_notices`.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:5073-5074 `if pane.session is None or not pane.session.is_alive:` / `return False, f"{to_role} is not running (spawn it first)"`; orchestrator.py:5235-5242 `_safe_session_write(_send_sess, body_payload, priority=WritePriority.TASK, kind="task", ...)`; cli_server.py:1091-1097 `elif cmd == "send": ok, msg = self._orch.send(req["to"], ...)`
findings.fix: In send(), when `to_role == LEAD.name`, route the body through `self._notify_lead(project_ns, body, from_role=from_role, kind="peer-to-lead")` (which already handles draft hold, busy backoff, verify-chain serialisation and the dead-Lead durable queue) instead of the direct write path.

findings.title: toggle_provider / set_plan_tier / set_team_preset / clear_team_preset_override / notify_roles_changed write `[system] …` + Enter straight into Lead's PTY, bypassing the draft guard and ready check
findings.scenario: User is halfway through typing a long prompt in the Lead pane and flips a provider or team preset in Settings. These five methods call `session.write(notice)` then `_delayed_enter(..., 150)` directly (6442-6445, 6485-6486, 6529-6530, 6566-6567, 6590-6591) instead of `_notify_lead`. `_lead_can_accept_injection` (lead_inbox.py:1069) is consulted only by the pump paths (lead_inbox.py:3845/4540/4709/4808), so the notice is spliced into the half-typed draft and the CR submits both together — the exact failure the #3 draft guard was written for. Same for a Lead mid-generation with no ready-prompt check.
findings.evidence:
6442: `_tog_sess.write(notice)`
6445: `_delayed_enter(lead, _tog_sess, 150)`
6529-6530 / 6566-6567 / 6590-6591: identical pattern
findings.fix: Route these through `self._notify_lead(project_ns, notice, kind="system")` (queued, draft-aware, ready-aware); if they must be immediate, gate on `_lead_can_accept_injection` and `is_at_ready_prompt()` and fall back to the queue.

findings.title: done() still shells out to git synchronously on the Qt thread (count_test_files_in_diff, UI-evidence gate porcelain, 2×N sibling reads) despite #408 moving 'the' git facts off-thread
findings.scenario: A clean `takkub done` from a shared-tree pane on a large repo with 2 other panes: `_finish` (cli_server.py:1164-1169) runs done() on the Qt thread, which then runs `git diff --numstat` + `git status --porcelain` (worktree_manager.py:2761/2769 via `count_test_files_in_diff`), `shared_tree_status_porcelain` for the UI gate (7686), and for each sibling `diffstat_since` + `shared_tree_status_porcelain` (7535-7536) — 7 subprocess.run calls with `_GIT_TIMEOUT_S = 30` each, none covered by `git_facts`. On Windows with a big untracked tree each `git status` is 1–5 s; a hung git freezes the cockpit 30 s.
findings.evidence:
7896: `_written_tests = count_test_files_in_diff(_diff_cwd, _diff_base)`
8083: `else self._sibling_shared_tree_touched_paths(project_ns, from_role, had_assign_git_root)` (unconditional, not fed by git_facts)
cli_server.py:1145-1146: `then run done() itself (fast, state-only) on the Qt thread`
findings.fix: Fold the numstat/status/sibling reads into `done_git_inputs` → `collect_done_git_facts` so they ride the existing worker thread, and skip `count_test_files_in_diff` when `git_facts` already carries a porcelain.

findings.title: `done --blocked` / delivery-failed reports set `_done_unread` but no regex ever clears it → permanent false '[role done] … missing' row in `takkub inbox`
findings.scenario: qa runs `takkub done --blocked "no test creds"`. done() sets `_done_unread[(proj,'qa')]` (8236) and sends a notice built by `_build_blocked_handoff` = `[qa BLOCKED] …` (7070). The pump clears markers via `done_roles_in_notice` (lead_inbox.py:365) whose regex `_DONE_NOTICE_TAG_RE` = `\[([\w][\w-]*)\s+(?:done|FAILED)\]` (lead_inbox.py:347) never matches BLOCKED or `[qa delivery-failed]` (7177). 120 s later `_inbox_report_raw` (9419-9443) emits a `queue: missing` item claiming the report 'หลุดจากคิวส่ง' for 24 h on every `takkub inbox` call, and `list_status_detailed` reports `done_unread: True`.
findings.evidence:
8236: `self._done_unread[(project_ns, from_role)] = time.time()` (runs for failed=True incl. blocked)
7070: `f"[{from_role} BLOCKED] {body}\n\n"`
lead_inbox.py:347: `_DONE_NOTICE_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\[([\w][\w-]*)\s+(?:done|FAILED)\]", re.IGNORECASE)`
findings.fix: Extend `_DONE_NOTICE_TAG_RE` (and `_FAILED_NOTICE_RE`/`_FAILED_TAG_RE`) to `(?:done|FAILED|BLOCKED|delivery-failed)`, or only set `_done_unread` when the notice body matches the tag the clearer knows.

findings.title: done(): `_note_path` re-declared as None after being set → deferred-close info never appended, grace-expiry kill is fully silent
findings.scenario: devops calls `takkub done` while `docker compose build` still runs. `_close_if_same_session` defers (line 8474). The only signal to Lead (#635 replaced the `_notify_lead` with an append to the session .md) reads `_note_path`, which line 8371 reset to None after line 7919 set it, so nothing is appended. Both terminal closes (8466, 8517) pass `suppress_live_children_warning=True` on the assumption 'the deferred notice already fired' — so after 15 min the build is killed with zero notice to Lead (exactly #234's original complaint). Only events.log records it.
findings.evidence:
7919: `_note_path = session_md_path  # Item 2 (#635)`
8371: `_note_path: str | None = None`
8491: `if _note_path:` (closure reads the None binding); test at tests/test_done_close_defers_live_children.py:139-141 only asserts no notify was sent, never that the file was appended
findings.fix: Delete line 8371 (keep the 7919 assignment) — and since the note file was already rendered into the Lead notice before the deferral happens, consider re-instating a one-shot `_notify_lead` (or passing `suppress_live_children_warning=False` on the grace-expiry close) so Lead is actually told the kill happened.

findings.title: Deferred-close poll runs a synchronous psutil process-tree walk on the Qt main thread every 5 s for up to 15 min (plus one more in close()) → UI freezes while a pane has live children after done
findings.scenario: Any pane whose done() leaves a child alive (leftover wrapper shell, long build, #537/#554 shapes). `_close_if_same_session` calls `_live_non_scaffolding_children(..., sync=True)` each `DONE_CLOSE_LIVE_CHILD_POLL_MS`=5 s tick (8408), which #658's own comment measures at 0.9–3 s per walk on prod; over the 15-min `DONE_CLOSE_LIVE_CHILD_GRACE_S` window that is ~180 blocking walks, i.e. the cockpit is frozen 20–60 % of the time and Lead's typed input stalls. The no-children path (8524) then calls close() → `_warn_if_live_children` → a second sync walk (6026) in the same tick. `close_all_teammates` (15397) does N sequential sync walks.
findings.evidence:
8408-8410: `names = self._live_non_scaffolding_children(project_ns, from_role, _pp.session, sync=True)`
5750-5756 comment: `captured at 0.9-3 s on prod, ×101 in one afternoon`
6026: `names = self._live_non_scaffolding_children(project_ns, role_name, session, sync=True)`
findings.fix: Run the poll's scan on `bg_pool` and re-enter the timer from the result callback (same pattern as `_refresh` at 5793), or use `sync=False` for poll ticks after the first and only force a fresh scan right before the actual kill.

findings.title: `_save_decision_note` drops any later report whose FIRST LINE repeats an earlier one (process-lifetime `_DEDUP_HASHES`) → session .md silently not written, Lead pointer/hot.md link dangle
findings.scenario: qa reports `done "PASS — all green\n…20 lines…"` at 10:00 for task A; at 14:00 for task B the note starts with the same first line. `_is_dedup_note` (vault_mirror.py:227-238, key = (project, role, md5(first line)), set never cleared) returns True → returns None before writing: no runtime/sessions file, no vault mirror, no knowledge-base distill. `session_md_path=None` so `_condense_done_note` (7202) pastes the full long note inline instead of the `📄 รายงานเต็ม:` pointer, `_recent_done` (8554) and hot.md record a filename that does not exist, and the #678 'missing' hint tells Lead to open `runtime/sessions/**/qa-*.md` which has no new file. Common first lines ('ทำเสร็จแล้ว', 'PASS', '[ref #x] fixed') make this routine within a day.
findings.evidence:
8920: `if _is_dedup_note(project, role, note):` → `return None`
vault_mirror.py:224: `_DEDUP_HASHES: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()` (only ever `.add`)
vault_mirror.py:233: `h = hashlib.md5(first_line.encode()).hexdigest()`
findings.fix: Key the dedup on (project, role, hash of whole scrubbed note) with a short TTL (e.g. 60 s — its stated purpose is 'rapid-fire duplicate done events'), or scope it to the vault mirror only and always write the runtime session file.

findings.title: BLOCKED / delivery-failed reports are invisible to `_has_pending_lead_notice`, `_notice_role_tag` and `_is_blocking_lead_notice` → `takkub wait` never wakes for them, `takkub inbox --role X` files them under 'system'
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub wait --role qa` while devops reports `done --blocked`. `_pending_notice_outside` (9163-9174) requires `_is_blocking_lead_notice` (lead_inbox.py:460, matches only `\bFAILED\b` inside brackets or the 4 system markers) → BLOCKED is not a wake trigger, Lead sits blind for the full --timeout although the report needs a human decision exactly like FAILED. Same regex gap in `_has_pending_lead_notice` (9105-9108) means the role drops out of `takkub list` while its BLOCKED report is still queued (only the #677 tombstone 'closed (HH:MM)' remains), and `_inbox_report_raw` (9349/9366) labels the item role 'system' so `takkub inbox --role devops` returns nothing.
findings.fix: Treat `[role BLOCKED]` and `[role delivery-failed]` as first-class failure tags in all four regexes (one shared alternation constant), then add a test that `done(blocked=True)` wakes an unrelated `wait` and is attributed to its role in inbox_report.

findings.title: pane_status_report walks every day directory under runtime/sessions per pane on the Qt main thread — UI stall grows with history
findings.scenario: `takkub status` (cli_server `_dispatch`, a QTcpSocket slot on the main thread) calls this. For each pane the `done_events` loop iterates ALL day dirs (119 on this machine) and every file in them, and evidence roles run a second full walk for cited screenshots (10785-10814); `_find_latest_transcript_path` adds a third when no live transcript. Measured here: 13,048 entries stat-ed in ~305 ms (warm cache) for 4 roles × 2 passes — cold cache / Defender scan is worse. Each Lead `takkub status` therefore freezes typing in every pane for hundreds of ms, and it only gets slower as sessions accumulate (nothing prunes empty day dirs). since_ts defaults to now-1h so only today's/yesterday's directories can ever match.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:10829-10835 `for day_dir in sorted(sessions_root.iterdir(), reverse=True): … for f in sorted(proj_dir.iterdir()):` (no break once day_dir is older than since_ts)
findings.fix: Stop iterating once `day_dir.name` (YYYY-MM-DD) is older than the day containing `since_ts`/`assign_ts`; skip the sorted() copies; or cache per-day listings with an mtime check. Longer term, run the report off-thread and reply asynchronously.

findings.title: harvest_info defaults since_ts to pane._spawn_ts; with 2.1.17 pane reuse the window covers the PREVIOUS task's artifacts
findings.scenario: Lead assigns task A to `backend`, it reports done, the pane stays alive (pane reuse, DONE_PANE_TTL_S=1800). Lead assigns task B to the same role: a shared-isolation re-assign pastes into the running pane (orchestrator.py:3664-3665) — no respawn, so `pane._spawn_ts` (set only in `attach_session`, agent_pane.py:674) is still task A's spawn time. `takkub harvest --role backend` without `--since` scans from that time and lists task A's screenshots/sources as B's harvest; the CLI may auto-confirm done on them (the same misattribution class #697 fixed across roles, now across tasks). `ps.assign_ts` (stamped on every assign, 4043) is the correct anchor and is already used by `pane_status_report` (10777).
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:10943-10945 `spawn_ts_raw: float = getattr(pane, "_spawn_ts", 0.0) or 0.0` / `if since_ts is None: since_ts = spawn_ts_raw if spawn_ts_raw > 0 else (time.time() - 3600)`
findings.fix: Default `since_ts` to `max(ps.assign_ts, spawn_ts_raw)` from `self._pane_state.get(_exit_key(project_ns, role))`, falling back to `_spawn_ts` only when no assign was recorded.

findings.title: _build_post_compact_brief reads the whole raw PTY transcript on the Qt main thread and injects unstripped ANSI/repaint fragments into Lead's context file
findings.scenario: User picks 'Restart Lead' (or switches Lead provider) while teammates are alive and `last-session.json` is <5 min old. `spawn()` (spawn_engine.py:2625 / 3007, main thread) calls this: `pathlib.Path(transcript_path).read_bytes()` loads the entire `.transcript.log` (raw PTY byte stream — lead transcripts on this machine reach 23.8 MB) and takes the last 5 non-empty RAW lines. Those lines are escape sequences / mid-repaint fragments (the #686 comment at 10706-10711 explains why raw tails are unusable and `pane_status_report` was changed to `_read_tail_bytes` + `_extract_transcript_lines`). lead_context.py:807-808 appends the brief verbatim (`suffix += post_compact_brief`) into Lead's AGENTS.md/system prompt, so the new Lead boots with garbage in its 'Post-compact status' block.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:11407-11409 `raw = pathlib.Path(transcript_path).read_bytes()` / `raw_lines = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()` / `tail = [ln for ln in raw_lines if ln.strip()][-5:]`
findings.fix: Use `_read_tail_bytes(path, _TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_BYTES)` + `_extract_transcript_lines(raw, max_lines=5)` (drop the partial first line like 10735-10736), or prefer `pane.session.display_lines()` when the pane is alive, exactly as `pane_status_report` does.

findings.title: QTimer.singleShot(0, _finish) called from a plain threading.Thread never fires → shell-open-dialog detector latches dialog_scan_in_flight=True forever and never notifies Lead
findings.scenario: Any working teammate pane that has been quiet for _SHELL_DIALOG_IDLE_GATE_S: the first scan sets `ps.dialog_scan_in_flight = True` (13648) and spawns `_scan_worker`, whose only way back is `QTimer.singleShot(0, _finish)` executed on the worker thread. Verified on this venv (PyQt 6.8.1 / Qt 6.8.2): a singleShot posted from a non-Qt thread targets a receiver living in that thread, which has no event loop, so the callback is never invoked (`fired: []`). `dialog_scan_in_flight` is reset nowhere else (grep: only 13665 inside `_finish`), so every later tick returns at 13637. A pane genuinely stuck on the Windows 'How do you want to open this file?' dialog (#104) is never reported to Lead; the feature is dead after one scan per PaneState.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:13664-13679 `def _finish() -> None: ps.dialog_scan_in_flight = False …` / `QTimer.singleShot(0, _finish)` (inside `_scan_worker`, run via `threading.Thread(target=_scan_worker …)`)
findings.fix: Marshal back to the Qt thread with a signal (declare e.g. `shellDialogScanned = pyqtSignal(str, str, bool)` on Orchestrator, emit from the worker, connect to a slot that runs `_finish`), or `QMetaObject.invokeMethod(self, …, Qt.ConnectionType.QueuedConnection)` with `self` as the receiver so the queued call lands on the main thread; audit the rest of the codebase for the same pattern.

findings.title: close-all / tab close resurrect any pane whose task had not reached it yet (close() undelivered-task auto-forward)
findings.scenario: Lead assigns codex/gemini pane (90 s boot) or a claude pane parked on the trust modal, then runs `takkub close-all` (or the user closes the project tab). `close_all_teammates` calls plain `close(n, project=...)`; in close(), `_task_undelivered_close` is True (task accepted, `task_delivered` still False), the branch at 6382-6391 schedules `_resume_after_close` regardless of keep_queue, which calls `spawn(..., _from_auto_respawn=True)` + `_send_when_ready(last_assigned_task)`. Result: `close-all` acks "closed N teammates" and the pane comes straight back with "[queued-assignment] X: undelivered task forwarded to replacement pane". On tab close, `_close_project_tab` already removed the tab, so `_ensure_teammate_pane` bails, spawn fails, and two stale notices (`_warn_lead_spawn_failed` + "retained; spawn failed") are durably queued for a project the user just closed and surface on its next open.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:15397-15398 `for n in names:` / `self.close(n, project=project_ns)`; orchestrator.py:6382-6391 `not suppress_pipeline and role_name != LEAD.name and (_task_undelivered_close or ...)` → `QTimer.singleShot(0, lambda: self._resume_after_close(project_ns, role_name, retained, closing_cwd))`; main_window.py:1589-1590 `self.orch.close_all_teammates(project=tab.project_name)` then `self.orch.close(LEAD.name, ..., force=True, reason="tab_close")`
findings.fix: Give close() an explicit `forward_undelivered: bool` (default True only for the single CLI `close` if that #484 behaviour is really wanted) and have close_all_teammates/_close_project_tab pass False (or reason="tab_close"/"close_all" → skip `_resume_after_close`); at minimum skip the forward when the project's Lead pane is gone.

findings.title: UI evidence gate rejects real screenshots whose path contains spaces or the $TAKKUB_ARTIFACTS_DIR form it itself recommends
findings.scenario: A frontend pane writes `$TAKKUB_ARTIFACTS_DIR/screenshots/login-390.png` (the exact form the rejection text at :365/:381 tells it to use) or `C:\Users\Mon Chai\...\shot.png` in its done note. _SCREENSHOT_PATH_RE stops at whitespace and `exists` never expands env vars, so every path is 'missing' and `takkub done` is rejected with 'ไม่พบไฟล์ screenshot' although the files exist; pane loops or reaches for --force.
findings.evidence: orchestrator_text.py:142 `_SCREENSHOT_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"[^\s\"'`<>()\[\]]+\.(?:png|jpe?g|webp)\b", ...)`; :393-395 `candidate = p if os.path.isabs(p) or not cwd else os.path.join(cwd, p); return os.path.isfile(candidate)` (no expandvars/expanduser).
findings.fix: Apply os.path.expandvars + expanduser before the isfile check; add a quoted-path alternative to the regex ("..."/'...') so paths with spaces are captured whole.

findings.title: `claude --version` subprocess runs synchronously on the Qt main thread on EVERY claude spawn, never cached
findings.scenario: Every claude spawn (Lead, each teammate, each auto-respawn, each fan-out pane) calls inject_claude_project_dir_name_env which blocks the GUI thread on subprocess.run([claude,'--version'], timeout=3). On Windows the npm shim is claude.cmd -> cmd.exe -> node, typically 0.5–1.5 s; with Defender scanning or a busy machine it hits the 3 s cap. A 4-pane fan-out freezes the cockpit 2–12 s, and this repeats on every respawn. mcp_bridge._codex_cli_version already caches the codex probe keyed on binary mtime for exactly this reason; the claude probe does not.
findings.evidence:
completed = subprocess.run(
    [claude_executable, "--version"],
    capture_output=True, check=False, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=3,
findings.fix: Cache the parsed version per (executable path, st_mtime) at module level (same shape as mcp_bridge's codex cache), or probe once at boot (boot_flow already runs `--version`) and read the cached value here.

findings.title: browser_driver:inline-import fires on text arguments — `grep "from playwright"` is denied for non-browser roles
findings.scenario: A backend/devops pane runs `grep -rn "from playwright" src/`, `rg "import selenium"`, `git log --grep "import puppeteer"` or echoes such text into a note: the hook denies with browser_driver:inline-import although the module docstring (line 32-35) promises reading about these tools is always allowed.
findings.evidence: line 388-390: `r"(?:require\s*\(\s*['\"]|from\s+['\"]?|import\s+['\"]?)" r"(?:@?(?:playwright|puppeteer)(?:[/-][\w-]+)?|selenium)"` — no interpreter-sink anchor. Probe: `classify('grep -rn "from playwright" src/', 'backend')` → `False, browser_driver:inline-import`.
findings.fix: Anchor the rule to an executing sink (`node -e`, `python -c`, heredoc whose introducer matches `_PYTHON_HEREDOC_SINK`/node), or skip matches that sit inside a quoted argument of grep/rg/echo/git log.

findings.title: machine-state.json (the primary busy source) carries bare role names, so the #646 project tag never shows and a same-named pane in another project is excluded from the busy check
findings.scenario: Lead in project `easy-ui` gets 'มี pane อื่นกำลังทำงาน (backend)' for a pane that belongs to another project (the #646 lie, still), because the project suffix is only synthesised from last-session.json's `projects` map (used ≤17% of the time).
