Conversely `backend` in project A running `npm run build` while `backend` in project B is working is NOT flagged busy (line 962 drops any entry whose base role equals its own).
findings.evidence: pane_guard.py:951-962 uses `data.get("working_panes")` verbatim when present and only builds `role@proj` in the `projects` fallback; the writer orchestrator.py:11976-11985 emits `working_panes = sorted(role for project, panes in self._panes_by_project.items() ...)` — role only — and line 12003 writes it as-is.
findings.fix: Write `f"{role}@{project}"` in `_maybe_write_machine_state` and, in the reader, exclude only the caller's own (role, project) pair instead of every same-named role.

findings.title: Lead direct-edit sensitive-content regexes deny any Python diff containing `return True` or the words token/session/login — the tiny-fix feature is effectively off for ordinary Python
findings.scenario: Lead makes a 1-line fix `return False` → `return True` in `src/foo/util.py` (scope tiny, 1 file): denied lead_direct_edit:deep_category. Likewise any diff mentioning `max_tokens`, `session_timeout`, `login_url` or a comment with the word 'token' — in this codebase nearly every module.
findings.evidence: line 1310: `r"verify[\s\-_]*signature|is[\s\-_]*admin|\bbypass\b|return\s+true\b"` and line 1303 `r"\b(?:tokens?|api[\s\-_]?keys?|secrets?)\b"` are applied at line 1320 to `diff_text.lower()` for every non-exempt file (path leg is test-exempt, content leg is not). The comment says the target was the JS `return true` bypass, but lowercasing makes Python `return True` match.
findings.fix: Restrict the `return true` / bare-word content patterns to the sensitive-path leg (or require both a sensitive identifier AND a bypass shape in the same hunk); at minimum do not lowercase before matching `return\s+true`.

findings.title: _worktree_role_owns matches `<role>-` on ANY path segment, so a sibling role's worktree under a project named `<role>-*` is treated as owned
findings.scenario: Project `backend-app` (or `mobile-app`, `qa-tools`): worktrees live at `.../worktrees/backend-app/frontend-<ts>/`. Role `backend` runs `git -C <frontend's worktree> reset --hard` / `checkout .` / `clean -fdx` (or has cwd there after a `cd`): `_in_worktree` returns True → #545 carve-out → frontend's uncommitted work is destroyed — the cross-role blast the #609 H2 check was written to stop.
findings.evidence: line 1957: `return any(seg == base or seg.startswith(prefix) for seg in norm.split("/") if seg)` — every segment is tested, not the leaf after `worktrees/<project>/`. Probe: `_worktree_role_owns('C:/x/worktrees/backend-app/frontend-123', 'backend')` → True; `_worktree_role_owns('C:/x/worktrees/proj/backend-123/qa-tests', 'qa')` → True.
findings.fix: Locate the `worktrees` segment, skip one segment (project), and test only that next segment against `base`/`prefix`.

findings.title: git default-deny allow-list omits common read-only plumbing (ls-remote, for-each-ref, show-ref, symbolic-ref, format-patch, diff-tree, range-diff, cherry, archive)
findings.scenario: Any guarded role on the shared tree runs `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, `git ls-remote --heads origin`, `git for-each-ref refs/heads`, `git show-ref`, `git format-patch -1 HEAD` to inspect state → denied git_shared_default_deny:<sub> and the pane routes around it or stalls.
findings.evidence: lines 3653-3679 `_GIT_SHARED_TREE_ALLOW_PLAIN` list; line 3901 `return sub` for anything not listed. Probes (role backend, cwd C:/proj): ls-remote, for-each-ref, show-ref, format-patch, symbolic-ref → all `allowed=False, rule=git_shared_default_deny:*`.
findings.fix: Add the read-only verbs (`ls-remote`, `for-each-ref`, `show-ref`, `symbolic-ref` (no 2nd positional), `diff-tree`, `diff-index`, `format-patch`, `range-diff`, `cherry`, `archive`, `fsck`, `verify-commit`, `var`, `whatchanged`) to the allow-list.

findings.title: Heredoc bodies are only stripped for the poll-loop and instance rules — git/browser/full-suite rules read a quoted issue body or commit message as executed shell
findings.scenario:
A qa pane files a bug: `gh issue create --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
repro:
git push origin main
EOF
)"` → denied git_lead_only:push; a worktree pane's `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` whose body has a line starting `pytest` → full_suite. Same class #287 documented for the poll loop (line 610-615) but never applied elsewhere.
findings.evidence:
`_strip_heredoc_bodies` is called only at line 3996 (poll loop) and 3048 (instance guard); line 3980 `cmd = _unwrap_shell_wrappers(cmd)` feeds every other rule the full heredoc text. Probe: `classify("gh issue create --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
repro:
git push origin main
EOF
)"", 'qa', cwd='C:/proj')` → `False, git_lead_only:push`.
findings.fix: After unwrapping, set `code = _strip_heredoc_bodies(cmd)` (keeping shell-sink heredocs, as the helper already does) and match all `_CMD_START`-anchored rules against `code`.

findings.title: Every gemini pane with a pinned model shows a permanent false '⚠ model mismatch' (live footer label is free text, spawn model is an id)
findings.scenario: Role pinned to gemini-3.7-flash-high via Settings picker (spawn_engine.py:2838 sets pane.model.spawn_model to that id). agent_pane.py:1007 passes live_model = session.current_model_label('gemini') which pty_session._GEMINI_MODEL_RE (pty_session.py:1394) returns as e.g. 'Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)' or 'Gemini 3.1 Pro · high'. shorten_model_name leaves both unchanged; _model_families_match('gemini-3.7-flash-high', 'Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)') is False -> mismatch=True -> header/tab text 'gemini · Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) ⚠' and tooltip 'ตั้งไว้ gemini-3.7-flash-high แต่รันจริง Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)' on every gemini pane, so a real Pro->Flash quota downgrade (#301/#591) is indistinguishable from the always-on false alarm. tests/test_pane_provider_label.py has no gemini case.
findings.evidence: pane_provider_label.py:100-106 `mismatch = (bool(live_model) and bool(spawn_model) and not _model_families_match(shorten_model_name(spawn_model), shorten_model_name(live_model)))`; pty_session.py:1394-1395 `_GEMINI_MODEL_RE = re.compile(r"(Gemini [\d.]+ (?:Pro|Flash)(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?(?:\s*[·:]\s*\w+)?)", re.IGNORECASE)`
findings.fix: Normalize the gemini footer label to id form before comparing (lowercase, strip '(' ')' '·' ':', collapse whitespace to '-': 'Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)' -> 'gemini-3.7-flash-high') in shorten_model_name or a gemini-specific branch, and add a gemini test vector.

findings.title: MCP/Plugins matrix hides the codex row although codex panes DO enforce this policy, while showing opencode/kimi/cursor rows whose toggles do nothing
findings.scenario: _MATRIX_EXCLUDED_ROLES drops 'codex' with the comment 'codex/gemini = non-claude binaries never load --mcp-config'. But mcp_bridge.py:372 `role_mcp_allowlist(base_role)` drives codex's session_override (`-c mcp_servers.*`) from this same policy, shared_dev_tools._ROLE_MCP_POLICY['codex'] = frozenset() (deny-all), and cli.py:5141 declares `_MCP_POLICY_ENFORCED_PROVIDERS = ("claude", "codex")`. A user who wants the codex role to get graft/playwright has no checkbox in Settings (only `takkub mcp allow --role codex`). Conversely opencode/kimi/cursor roles get a row and Save writes an override for them, but their specs are mcp_adapter_variant='none' and cli.py:5248 says they 'don't consult this policy' — the checkbox lies.
findings.evidence: pane_tools_dialog.py:33 `_MATRIX_EXCLUDED_ROLES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"shell", "codex", "gemini"})`; cli.py:5141 `_MCP_POLICY_ENFORCED_PROVIDERS = ("claude", "codex")`; mcp_bridge.py:372 `if role_mcp_allowlist(base_role) is not None:`
findings.fix: Derive exclusions from PROVIDER_REGISTRY: exclude a role iff its forced provider's spec.mcp_adapter_variant == 'none' or the role is 'shell' (so codex is shown, opencode/kimi/cursor are hidden or rendered disabled with a 'not enforced for this CLI' hint).

findings.title: Pipeline completion notice only reflects the LAST hop's failures — earlier-hop crashes reported as 'all hops complete ✓'
findings.scenario: Feature template (frontend+backend → devops → qa): frontend pane crashes/is closed without done in hop 1 → close() adds it to `hop_failed` (orchestrator.py:6350) and the hop advances; `_fire_pipeline_hop` for hop 2 resets `run.hop_failed = set()`; hops 2-3 finish cleanly → `_advance_pipeline` renders `status = "all hops complete ✓"` and Lead is told the pipeline succeeded although frontend never delivered.
findings.evidence: pipeline_executor.py:315 `run.hop_failed = set()` (per-hop reset); pipeline_executor.py:471-474 `if run.hop_failed: status = f"completed with failures (...)" else: status = "all hops complete ✓"`.
findings.fix: Keep a run-level accumulator (e.g. `run.failed_by_hop: dict[int, set]`) appended in close()/spawn-fail paths and render it in `_advance_pipeline`; leave `hop_failed` per-hop for the advance logic.

findings.title: Plugins button checks/installs/uninstalls against default_claude_config_dir() while panes load plugins from the project's profile dir
findings.scenario: A project with a named user profile (or a cockpit launched from a shell where CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is already set, which `_claude_env`'s setdefault honours but `installed_on_disk` ignores). `installed_on_disk()` and `_purge_plugin_cache()` look only in `default_claude_config_dir()/plugins/cache`; `lead_context._default_plugin_dirs(role, project)` (line 988) loads from `config_dir_for(project)/plugins/cache`. Result: the 🧩 button reports 'installed' while that project's panes never receive the plugin — or, when the CLI installed into the env-selected home, `install_plugin` misses on its own disk check and runs `uninstall_plugin` + purge (lines 269-270), removing a plugin that was correctly installed for the panes, then reports 'repair failed'. On this machine `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` already records frontend-design/code-review installPaths under `~/.claude-work/...` (a different home than the cockpit's `~/.claude` default), showing the two homes diverge in practice.
findings.evidence:
plugin_installer.py:114 `env.setdefault("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", str(default_claude_config_dir()))`
plugin_installer.py:166 `base = default_claude_config_dir() / "plugins" / "cache"`
lead_context.py:988 `config_dir = config_dir_for(project) if project is not None else default_claude_config_dir()`
findings.fix: Thread the same `config_dir_for(project)` through installed_on_disk/_purge_plugin_cache/_claude_env (pass project from user_actions), and never uninstall on a disk-check miss — report the mismatch instead.

findings.title: Preview reloads its page on every tab switch back to the project (SPA state/scroll lost)
findings.scenario: Preview shows http://localhost:3000; user navigates inside the app to /dashboard, switches to another project tab and back. MainWindow._sync_preview_to_active_tab (main_window.py:1658 -> :603-605) calls show_state with the same state; show_state unconditionally calls load_url(state.target), re-navigating to the original target and discarding in-app route, scroll and form state.
findings.evidence: preview_widget.py:330-337 `def show_state(...): self._ensure_view(); ... if state.mode == "url": self._view.load_url(state.target) else: self._view.load_file(state.target)` — no comparison with self._project/self._state.
findings.fix: Early-return the load when `self._view is not None and self._project == project and self._state == state` (PreviewState is a frozen dataclass, equality works); still refresh device/header.

findings.title: Explorer tree never re-lists a directory — files a pane creates/deletes never appear until the tab is recreated
findings.scenario: Expand `src/` in the Project Explorer, then a teammate pane creates `src/new_module.py` (or deletes one). `_LOADED_ROLE` was set True on the first expand and is never reset anywhere; collapse+expand returns at line 233; `refresh_changes()` (the only refresh entry, also what MainWindow calls on editor save / gitRefreshNeeded) only re-runs the git services. The new file is invisible in the tree (it may show under CHANGES only if git sees it) until the project tab is closed and reopened.
findings.evidence:
project_explorer.py:233 `if not item.data(0, _IS_DIR_ROLE) or item.data(0, _LOADED_ROLE):` `return`
project_explorer.py:235 `item.setData(0, _LOADED_ROLE, True)`
project_explorer.py:313-318 refresh_changes only calls request_refresh() on git services
findings.fix: Reset `_LOADED_ROLE` to False on collapse (itemCollapsed) or add a re-list of expanded items in `refresh_changes()` (re-request listing for every expanded directory item, diffing children).

findings.title: Git M/A/D badges never match when the first configured root is a subdirectory of the repo (porcelain paths are repo-root-relative)
findings.scenario: Project with paths {api: repo/api, web: repo/web} (the sibling layout graft_autobuild's docstring calls frequent). GitStatusService runs `git status --porcelain=v1` with cwd=repo/api; porcelain v1 output paths are ALWAYS relative to the repository top-level (`api/src/x.py`), but `_apply_badge` computes `rel` relative to `self.git_status.repo_root` = repo/api (`src/x.py`). Nothing ever matches → no file in the Explorer ever gets a colour badge, silently. #375's `_on_repos_discovered` corrects `self.git_changes.repo_root` to the discovered toplevel but never touches `self.git_status`.
findings.evidence:
project_file_index.py:378 `["git", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=normal"], cwd=str(self.repo_root)`
project_explorer.py:422 `rel = _safe_resolve(Path(path_str)).relative_to(self.git_status.repo_root).as_posix()`
project_explorer.py:338-346 only re-creates `self.git_changes`, `self.git_status` untouched
findings.fix: In `_on_repos_discovered`, re-create `GitStatusService(primary_toplevel)` (or compute `rel` against the discovered toplevel) so badge keys match porcelain paths.

findings.title: Import folder silently overwrites an existing project with the same slug (different folder)
findings.scenario: User already has project 'web' at C:/a/web (tab open, Lead running). They Import D:/other/web. The slug collides, projects.json paths for 'web' are replaced with the new folder, and because the tab is open the wizard just switches to it ('Updated project: web'). Lead keeps working in the old cwd while role cwd resolution (assign/lead_cwd) now points at the new folder.
findings.evidence: project_wizard.py:77-84 slugify + `_save_and_open_project(name, p, paths, ...)` with no existence check; :397-401 `data["projects"][name] = {... "paths": paths ...}` replaces the entry; :407-415 open tab -> only `setCurrentIndex`. `_new_project_with_rules` has the duplicate-name confirm at :104-120 that this flow lacks.
findings.fix: Reuse the duplicate-name check from `_new_project_with_rules` in `_import_existing_project` (offer rename / cancel), and when the project tab is open restart its Lead or refuse the path change.

findings.title: Boot-time pinned-model bump (refresh_provider_model) is never called from any production path — the module's whole purpose is unwired
findings.scenario: Module docstring: 'Runs in the SAME boot phase as the binary update (provider_update.py)'; settings_window.py:449 comment relies on it ('provider_model_refresh bumps a pinned model'). Grep of every *.py under src/ finds no caller of refresh_provider_model/_refresh_pins (only tests/test_provider_model_refresh.py). boot_flow.py imports only provider_update; app.py/boot_update_window never import this module. Result: a role pinned to gemini-3.5-flash-high or gpt-5.5-* stays pinned forever at boot (the exact user directive 2026-08-20 this module cites), while the docs/comments claim it auto-bumps. Only provider_model_catalog.refresh_cache (Settings picker) reuses its discovery functions.
findings.evidence: provider_model_refresh.py:411 `def refresh_provider_model(name: str, binary: str) -> ModelRefreshOutcome:`; boot_flow.py:83 `from .provider_update import _discover` (no model_refresh import); settings_window.py:449 `# when this list still topped out at 3.6: `provider_model_refresh` bumps a`
findings.fix: Either wire refresh_provider_model(name, binary) into boot_flow's per-provider update loop (after update_provider, for eligible providers) and surface STATUS_BUMPED in the boot window, or delete _refresh_pins/_pins_for/_apply_pin/refresh_provider_model/ModelRefreshOutcome/STATUS_* and fix the docstring + settings_window.py:449 comment.

findings.title: CLAUDE_DEFAULT_BUILTIN_TOOLS is stale — doctor WARNs 'new built-in tools detected' on every run today (ToolSearch, Monitor, TaskOutput, TaskStop, ListAgents, ScheduleWakeup…)
findings.scenario: Running `_scan_claude_transcript_tools()` on this machine returns tools absent from the list: ListAgents, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup, TaskOutput, TaskStop, ToolSearch (+ harness-only Artifact/StructuredOutput/Workflow). `takkub doctor` therefore shows `⚠ tools_drift new built-in tools detected: …` every run, and per the check's own docstring (doctor.py:357-362) the teammate allowlist derived from this tuple (`TEAMMATE_DEFAULT_BUILTIN_TOOLS`, provider_spec.py:636-638) omits them, so teammate panes lack e.g. ToolSearch (needed to load deferred tools in current Claude Code).
findings.evidence: doctor.py:377-378 `known = set(CLAUDE_DEFAULT_BUILTIN_TOOLS)\nnew_tools = sorted(set(current_defaults) - known)`; live scan output: tools= ['Agent','Artifact','AskUserQuestion',…,'ListAgents','Monitor',…,'ToolSearch',…]
findings.fix: Add the confirmed Claude Code built-ins (ToolSearch, Monitor, TaskOutput, TaskStop, ListAgents, ScheduleWakeup) to CLAUDE_DEFAULT_BUILTIN_TOOLS; have the drift check ignore harness-only names (Workflow, StructuredOutput, Artifact) via an explicit ignore set.

findings.title: _ReaderThread._flush runs concurrently on reader thread and threading.Timer threads -> batches fed to pyte/transcript/xterm out of order
findings.scenario: Timer T1 fires `_flush`, pops batch A under `_lock`, releases, and is inside `_on_data(A)` (pyte parse of a large chunk under GIL contention with N panes takes >10 ms). Reader thread reads B+C, hits `len(_pending) >= _batch_bytes`, calls `_flush` itself, pops B+C and runs `_on_data(B+C)` concurrently. `stream.feed`/transcript write/`bytesReceived.emit` order between the two threads is unspecified -> pyte screen parses an escape sequence split across A/B backwards (wrong `_cached_ready`), transcript file is permanently out of order, xterm.js paints garbage until next repaint.
findings.evidence: pty_session.py:1762-1772: batch popped under `self._lock`, then `self._on_data(batch)` and `self.bytesReceived.emit(batch)` executed outside the lock ("Call on_data and emit outside self._lock"); L1777 `threading.Timer(self._batch_sec, self._flush)` creates a second caller thread; L1850-1853 reader thread calls `_flush()` directly.
findings.fix: Serialize delivery: have the timer only wake the reader (e.g. set an Event / put a sentinel) and let the reader thread be the sole caller of `_on_data`+emit; or wrap `_on_data`+emit in a dedicated ordering lock taken while still holding the sequence position.

findings.title: Spawn-time console sweep SW_HIDEs the user's own Windows Terminal opened within 3.5 s of any pane spawn
findings.scenario: Windows 11, default terminal = Windows Terminal. Cockpit boots or auto-respawns a pane (spawns happen many times per session). User launches a new Windows Terminal window (class CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS) within the 150-3500 ms sweep window. `_sweep` computes `snapshot - pre_hwnds` and calls `hide_hwnds` -> `ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)` -> the user's terminal vanishes from screen, taskbar and Alt-Tab with its running shell; only recoverable via Task Manager.
findings.evidence: pty_session.py:1999-2005 `new = snapshot_console_hwnds() - pre_hwnds; if new: hide_hwnds(new)` with no ownership/class check; _win_console.py:74-76 includes CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS in the snapshot set and L82-85 admits "The spawn-time path may still hide it"; hide_hwnds L217-218 uses SW_HIDE.
findings.fix: In `_sweep`, skip HWNDs whose class is in `_UNOWNABLE_WINDOW_CLASSES` unless `_is_descendant_of(pid, root_pid)` proves ownership; keep unconditional hiding only for ConsoleWindowClass/PseudoConsoleWindow.

findings.title: macOS: descendants of a CLI that exits on its own are never reaped (Windows job object has no POSIX equivalent here)
findings.scenario: macOS pane (any provider) starts `npm run dev` / `next dev` in the background, then the CLI exits naturally (crash, OOM, user `/exit`, quota-triggered exit). `_on_exit` -> `_teardown_resources(kill_process=False)`: `_tree_kill` is only in the `if kill_process:` branch, and the `elif _job_object is not None` branch is Windows-only (`_job_object` is None on POSIX, L1989). The dev server keeps running orphaned, holding its port; next spawn fails with EADDRINUSE. Windows does not leak (job close reaps).
findings.evidence: pty_session.py:2356-2365: `if kill_process: ... _tree_kill(_pid)` / `elif _job_object is not None: _job_object.close()` — nothing runs for POSIX natural exit. `_tree_kill` POSIX path (L235-241) does `os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid))`, which also fails once the leader is reaped, so pgid must be captured at spawn.
findings.fix: Capture `pgid = os.getpgid(pid)` right after spawn on POSIX and, in the natural-exit branch, `os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)` (best-effort) to mirror the job-object semantics.

findings.title: Python gate hardcodes cockpit-only plugin flags/paths and only recognises `.venv` — any other Python project fails on tooling, not code
findings.scenario: qa pane runs `takkub qa-gate`/`--auto` inside a non-cockpit Python project (the #401 unittest fallback and `--exec` exist precisely for this). (1) `_pytest_cmd` always adds `--timeout=…`, `--max-worker-restart=0` (and `-n 4 --dist loadscope` on full) → pytest without pytest-timeout/pytest-xdist: 'unrecognized arguments' exit 4 → FAIL; ENV_GAP (#401) only detects a missing *tool*. (2) `_ruff_cmd` hardcodes `src/ tests/` → ruff exits 2 on a flat-layout repo. (3) `lint-imports` with no `[tool.importlinter]` config exits 1 → FAIL. (4) `shared_venv_bin` only looks for `.venv/` → a project using `venv/`/conda gets `py = sys.executable` = the cockpit's own venv python, so its imports fail and are reported as test failures.
findings.evidence: l.571-577 `[*base, "--timeout=300", "--timeout-method=thread", "--max-worker-restart=0", *targeted]`; l.596 `return [*base, "src/", "tests/"]`; l.227-231 `for sub in ("Scripts", "bin"): candidate = root / ".venv" / sub`; l.2133 `py = _resolve_tool(bin_dir, "python") or sys.executable`.
findings.fix: Probe plugins (`pytest --version` / importlib.metadata in the target venv) before adding flags; derive ruff paths from pyproject/`ruff check .`; skip lint-imports when no importlinter config; also accept `venv/`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `$UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`; when no project interpreter is found report ENV_GAP instead of using the cockpit's python.

findings.title: Python auto-targeted tier passes deleted/renamed test paths and non-test helper modules to pytest → exit 4/5 FAIL
findings.scenario: (a) Rename `tests/test_old.py`→`tests/test_new.py` uncommitted: `git diff --name-only HEAD` (l.1369) lists the deleted old path, `_TEST_FILE_RE` matches it, pytest gets a nonexistent path → 'file or directory not found' exit 4 → FAIL. (b) Edit only `tests/_subprocess_call_ast.py` / `tests/_qt_timer_leak_guard.py` / `tests/__init__.py` (real helper files in this repo): matched by `(^|/)(tests?/…)`, passed explicitly so pytest collects 0 tests → exit 5 → FAIL 'no tests ran'.
findings.evidence: l.1472-1474 `if _TEST_FILE_RE.search(f):\n    out.append(f)\n    continue` — no existence check and no `test_*.py` basename requirement; regex l.1293-1295 accepts any path under tests/.
findings.fix: In `_map_python_tests` keep only `(root / f).is_file()` and basename matching `test_*.py`; treat deleted paths as 'no test' (widen to full or drop).

findings.title: `qa-gate --auto` never writes the report/step logs even on the full tier, contradicting qa.md and disabling the #607 retry evidence
findings.scenario: The qa role is told to run `takkub qa-gate --auto` once per batch and that the report is 'auto-saved to <DATA_HOME>/runtime/qa-reports/' (.claude/agents/qa.md:35, docs/qa-gate-policy.md:44). With `auto=True`, `tier` is always a DiffTier so `write_report` is False → `log_dir=None` (l.2078-2080) and `finish()` skips `_maybe_write_report`. Lead finds no report; `_node_worker_timeout_flake` (l.917-923) then only sees the 6-line tail so the worker-timeout+passed-summary signature is almost never both present and the serial retry does not fire.
findings.evidence: l.2041-2042 `if write_report is None:\n    write_report = targeted is None and tier is None`; `_node_worker_timeout_flake` docstring l.905 claims 'every full-tier run does' write a log.
findings.fix: `write_report = targeted is None and (tier is None or tier.tier == "full")`, and set `log_dir` for auto-full as well.

findings.title: release failure message drops git/hook stderr — pre-commit hook failures surface as a bare 'exit status 1'
findings.scenario: `git commit` at l.387 runs the repo's pre-commit chain (ruff, docs-verify, import-linter, depgraph). When a hook rejects the commit, CalledProcessError is re-raised as `RuntimeError(f"release failed; working tree reverted: {exc}")`; `str(CalledProcessError)` is only "Command [...] returned non-zero exit status 1." so the user never sees which hook failed or why.
findings.evidence: l.427 `raise RuntimeError(f"release failed; working tree reverted: {exc}") from exc` — `exc.stderr` (captured via capture_output=True in `_git`, l.259-269) is never included.
findings.fix: Append `getattr(exc, 'stderr', '') or getattr(exc, 'stdout', '')` (tail ~40 lines) to the RuntimeError message.

findings.title: Image upload message is prefixed '[remote → lead] ' twice, so the phone mirrors a second 'me' bubble containing the raw workstation path
findings.scenario: Phone attaches an image (control mode). lead_upload_image builds `message = f'[remote → lead] แนบรูปจาก mobile ...: "{image_path}"'` and calls lead_say -> cli_server send -> Orchestrator.send(from_role='remote'), which prepends its own header (orchestrator.py:5205-5206), producing '[remote → lead] [remote → lead] แนบรูป... "C:\Users\...\remote-<uuid>.png"'. notify._strip_remote_prefix strips one copy, so history/live 'user' events carry '[remote → lead] แนบรูปจาก mobile ให้เปิดดูจากไฟล์นี้: "C:\...png"'; app.js:2247 echo-suppression compares against the optimistic '![name](data:...)' bubble, no match, so the phone renders an extra bubble with the leftover prefix and the absolute path (the data-min rule the module docstring promises to keep off the phone).
findings.evidence: api.py:628 literal prefix; orchestrator.py:5205 `header = f"[{from_role} → {to_role}] " if from_role and from_role != to_role else ""` and :5206 `body = header + _sanitize_pane_text(msg)`; notify.py:380-384 strips exactly one prefix.
findings.fix: Drop the literal '[remote → lead] ' from api.py:628 (send() adds it), and make the PWA suppress/relabel the mirrored upload line (e.g. server tags it `kind:'sys'` or the phone matches on the 'แนบรูปจาก mobile' marker).

findings.title: SSE 'report' event has no listener in the shipped PWA: `takkub report publish --send` says 'pushed' but the phone never shows the attachment card
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub report publish --send` (#390). cli._push_report_to_mobile -> report-send -> Orchestrator.push_report returns (True, 'pushed <name> to project ...') -> reportShared -> LeadNotifier._on_report_shared -> SSEBroadcaster.push('report', payload). app.js registers listeners only for working/idle/lead/user/done/session_changed/blocked_on_picker (app.js:2216-2284) and has no onmessage handler; a named SSE event with no listener is dropped by EventSource. User is told the report reached the phone; nothing appears.
findings.evidence: http_server.py:378-392 allowlist includes "report"; notify.py:2438-2448 pushes it; Grep of app.js for "report" / addEventListener("report" returns no match; orchestrator.py:5383 returns `f"pushed {name!r} to project {project_ns}"`.
findings.fix: Add `es.addEventListener("report", ...)` in app.js rendering {name,url,label,size_bytes,attachment} as a card (and bump sw.js CACHE_NAME), or remove the push path and make cmd_report print the plain link only.

findings.title: Lead history read parses up to 8 MB of JSONL on the Qt main thread for every phone history request
findings.scenario: Long-running Claude Lead session (tens of MB JSONL). Every /api/lead/history (project switch, reconnect, resume, and app.js:3182 `refreshOpenProjectHistories()` for EVERY open project each time the phone returns from >30 s in background) is an inline bridge action; _read_recent_claude_messages reads the last 8 MB and json.loads every line, then _redact_messages regex-scans 200 messages, all on the main thread. Multiple open tabs multiply it. The same size cap applies to codex/gemini readers.
findings.evidence: notify.py:110 `_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`; notify.py:857-874 full read + per-line json.loads; http_server.py:263-267 lead_history dispatched inline in _Bridge._handle.
findings.fix: Move lead_history (and lead_sessions) to _OFF_THREAD_ACTIONS after resolving the transcript path + provider on the Qt thread, or cache parsed history per (path, size) so repeated refreshes only parse the appended tail.

findings.title: Codex resume picker scans the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree (rglob + first-line read of every rollout) on the Qt main thread
findings.scenario: Lead provider = codex, user taps Resume on the phone. /api/lead/sessions is an inline bridge action (http_server.py:268-272) that runs on the Qt main thread; _list_recent_codex_sessions does `root.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl")` and `_codex_session_meta(path)` (open + readline) for every file in the store before sorting. The repo's own comment (notify.py:1259-1264) measured the cheaper rglob+stat variant at 2716 ms on 813 files; this variant reads each file too, so the desktop cockpit freezes for seconds (Lead typing lag, watchdog SOFT stall) every time the picker opens, growing with store size. Codex is one of the advertised providers.
findings.evidence: notify.py:1518-1528 `for path in root.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl"): meta = _codex_session_meta(path)` with no day-directory bound; http_server.py:202-209 documents lead_sessions as 'fully inline'.
findings.fix: Reuse _codex_rollout_candidates(root) (newest day first, lazy) with an early stop once `capped` matches are found, or move lead_sessions into _OFF_THREAD_ACTIONS (it only reads files + config, no Qt/orch state beyond the provider name).

findings.title: Windows tunnel launch via `cmd /d /c` + list2cmdline cannot start any executable/script whose path contains a space
findings.scenario: cloudflared resolved from PATH at C:\Program Files (x86)\cloudflared\cloudflared.exe (winget install), or a Windows user name with a space (DATA_HOME\bin\cloudflared.exe from cloudflared_install), or a .bat script path with spaces. _spawn builds `list2cmdline(argv)` -> '"C:\Program Files\...\cloudflared.exe" tunnel ...' then passes it as ONE argv element to ['cmd','/d','/c', command]; Popen re-quotes it with backslash-escaped quotes, which cmd.exe does not understand. Named mode surfaces "cloudflared exited immediately: '\"C:\Program' is not recognized"; quick/ngrok/bat modes fail silently (no URL, see the quick-tunnel finding).
findings.evidence: Reproduced on this machine with the exact Windows branch of _spawn (tunnel.py:169-186) and 'C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\echo.exe': rc=1, output `'\"C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\echo.exe\"' is not recognized as an internal or external command`; the same code with a space-free path succeeds.
findings.fix: Spawn the binary directly (`subprocess.Popen(argv, ...)`) for cloudflared/ngrok and only wrap .bat/.cmd scripts with `cmd /d /c`, passing the script as separate argv elements (['cmd','/d','/c', script, port]) instead of a pre-joined string.

findings.title: images.txt relative paths are resolved against the process cwd, not the content dir
findings.scenario: images.txt says `login|screenshots/login.png` (relative to report-content/, the natural reading of docs/lead/report-publish.md:38 `name|path`). Lead runs `takkub report build --content report-content` from the project root -> os.path.exists('screenshots/login.png') is False -> 'WARNING: image not found' then build aborts with 'Missing images'.
findings.evidence: report_builder.py:163-164 `if os.path.exists(path): data_uri = self._image_to_data_uri(path)` — bare `path` from images.txt, never joined with self.content_dir.
findings.fix: Resolve `p = Path(path) if os.path.isabs(path) else self.content_dir / path` (fall back to cwd-relative for compatibility) before exists()/read.

findings.title: Content-dir template.html override is dead: shipped template always wins (contradicts docs + docstring)
findings.scenario: User drops a custom template.html into the report content dir (documented in docs/lead/report-publish.md:33 as 'ชนะ template ที่ ship มา'). `takkub report build` silently ignores it and uses assets/report/template.html on every dev/installed build where the kit exists.
findings.evidence: report_builder.py:311-317 `asset_template = report_asset_root() / "template.html"; if asset_template.exists(): return ...` checked BEFORE `content_template = self.content_dir / "template.html"`; docstring :308-310 claims the content-dir override 'always wins over the shipped kit'.
findings.fix: Check `self.content_dir / "template.html"` first, then the shipped asset, then the fallback.

findings.title: spawn-service cannot start .cmd/.bat shims on Windows (npm/pnpm/npx) — works on macOS only
findings.scenario: `takkub spawn-service --name web -- npm run dev` (or pnpm/npx/yarn) on Windows: Popen without shutil.which resolution -> CreateProcess only appends .exe, so npm.cmd is not found -> both creationflags attempts raise FileNotFoundError -> ServiceSpawnError "could not start 'npm': [WinError 2]". Same command succeeds on macOS.
findings.evidence: service_spawner.py:199-208 `proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=str(workdir), env=child_env, ...)` — cmd[0] passed verbatim; no shutil.which anywhere in the module.
findings.fix: `exe = shutil.which(cmd[0], path=child_env.get("PATH"))`; if found, replace cmd[0] with it (which honours PATHEXT so npm.cmd resolves); otherwise raise ServiceSpawnError with a clear 'not on PATH' message.

findings.title: 'แชร์ session' runs convert_profile_to_shared on the Qt main thread — copies/renames the whole projects/todos/plugins/skills tree, freezing the UI
findings.scenario: Accounts → claude named account → 'แชร์ session' → OK. `user_profile.convert_profile_to_shared` walks `projects/` etc. with rglob and copies every file into ~/.claude (`_merge_tree`, user_profile.py:240-252), then renames and links — for a used Claude profile that is hundreds of MB of session JSONL, so the cockpit freezes for seconds to minutes and the stall watchdog/auto-issue fires; the whole file otherwise moves every probe off the main thread (`_AccountsRefreshWorker`).
findings.evidence: 637: `results = user_profile.convert_profile_to_shared(account.config_dir)` (synchronous, no thread); user_profile.py:246-252: `for p in src.rglob("*"): … copy`.
findings.fix: Run the conversion in a worker (QThreadPool/QRunnable like `_AccountsRefreshWorker`), disable the card's buttons meanwhile, show the results dict on the finished signal.

findings.title: Opening the new Settings window runs `claude plugin list --json` synchronously on the Qt main thread (30s timeout), and again on every plugin get/create/delete_plan
findings.scenario: TAKKUB_SETTINGS_UI=new: SettingsManagementWindow.__init__ calls plugins_page.refresh() (window.py:109) → plugins_repo.list() → _installed_entries() → plugin_installer.list_installed() → subprocess `claude plugin list --json` with timeout=30 on the GUI thread. The whole cockpit (all panes) freezes for the claude CLI cold start; a hung CLI blocks 30s. _installed_entries() is re-run on every list/get/delete_plan/create/_resolve_installed_id (lines 123, 130, 186, 203, 211) so every click on the Plugins page re-spawns the CLI.
findings.evidence: plugins.py:72 `data = plugin_installer.list_installed()` · plugin_installer.py:287-294 `def list_installed(timeout: float = 30.0)` / `proc = _claude("plugin", "list", "--json", timeout=timeout)` · window.py:106-109 `self.plugins_page = PluginsPage(self)` … `self.plugins_page.refresh()`
findings.fix: Run list_installed in a QRunnable/worker and paint from a cache (same shape as status_header's _PlanProbeWorker); cache the result per window and reuse it across get/delete_plan instead of re-spawning the CLI.

findings.title: Skills 'Project' root and Role Access skill list use Path.cwd() (cockpit process cwd), not the active project
findings.scenario: TAKKUB_SETTINGS_UI=new: an npm-installed cockpit launched from e.g. C:\Users\monch scans C:\Users\monch\.claude\skills as 'Project' skills (empty), and '+ New Skill' → create() → skill_scan.create_skill(roots[0], …) with project_ns=None writes <cwd>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md into the user's home/launch dir instead of the active project's central skills dir. roles_page._available_skills (roles_page.py:204) has the same cwd scope, so the Access-tab checklist cannot show shipped/project skills the Skills page lists (the repo's own LOW-2 note in assignable_names).
findings.evidence: skills.py:35-36 `def _project_roots() -> list[Path]: return [Path.cwd()]` · skills.py:173-177 `roots = _project_roots()` … `skill_scan.create_skill(roots[0], command.name, …)` (no project_ns) · roles_page.py:204 `return sorted(s.name for s in skill_scan.scan_skills([Path.cwd()]))`
findings.fix: Resolve the root from config.active_project() (lead_cwd) and pass project_ns to create_skill as the legacy window does; have roles_page use skills_repo.assignable_names().

findings.title: Usage page runs two full ledger rollups per account plus quota-file scans on the Qt main thread on every open/range switch
findings.scenario: User opens Settings > Usage (lazy builder -> _build_usage_view -> _render_usage) or flips the range combo. query_usage(refresh=True) calls rollup_daily per account (takes _UsageLock: 50 ms poll loop, up to 10 s if the Refresh import thread is mid-write; reads the current month jsonl + _seen_ids.json, rewrites daily.json) and then daily_series(refresh=True) rolls up EVERY account AGAIN; _query_quota reads every quota-YYYY-MM.jsonl in range (tens of thousands of rows/month, doubled by the dedup bug below). All synchronous on the GUI thread; the docstring's 'cheap' claim does not hold on a heavy month.
findings.evidence: L414: `result = usage_ledger.query_usage(provider=None, **kwargs)`   L416: `self._usage_last_sparkline_points = usage_ledger.daily_series(days=_SPARKLINE_DAYS)` (refresh defaults True -> rollup again)   usage_ledger.py:1159-1160 / 1328-1329
findings.fix: Call daily_series(refresh=False) after query_usage, and move the refresh=True query into a _CallableThread (same as Refresh) rendering from the result; render immediately with refresh=False.

findings.title: pending_team_preset is never consumed by the caller — orchestrator.set_team_preset (Lead broadcast + team_preset_set event) never fires from Settings
findings.scenario: Roles page → pick a team-size card → Save & Apply. The preset file is written (1637 `set_current`) but the comment at 974-980 promises the caller routes it through `orchestrator.set_team_preset` for the live-Lead broadcast; user_actions.py:402-408 reads only `pending_provider_disabled` and `pending_performance_reload`. The live Lead never receives '[system] team preset (โปรเจคนี้) → …' (orchestrator.py:6556-6568) and `team_preset_set` is never logged; it keeps operating under the old preset until its next assign is rejected. The status chip self-heals only because status_header.py:759 refreshes it on the periodic tick.
findings.evidence: Grep for `pending_team_preset` in src/: only settings_window.py (981, 1636-1637, 2320, 3101). user_actions.py:402: `for provider, target_disabled in dlg.pending_provider_disabled.items():` … 407: `if dlg.pending_performance_reload:` — no team-preset branch.
findings.fix: In `_open_legacy_settings_window`, after Accepted: `if dlg.pending_team_preset: self.orch.set_team_preset(dlg.pending_team_preset, _proj)` (the file write is idempotent) — or emit the broadcast from the dialog via a signal.

findings.title: โหมดเครื่อง / discard-renderer change is saved but never applied live: pending_performance_reload is only read when the dialog is Accepted, and General has Save & Apply disabled
findings.scenario: ทั่วไป page → change โหมดเครื่อง (or the discard toggle) → file is written and `pending_performance_reload=True` → footer Save & Apply is disabled on this page (284 `_NO_FOOTER_SAVE_VIEWS`, 1488) so the user closes with Cancel/X → `reject` → user_actions.py:387-388 returns before 407-408 → `orch.reload_performance_settings()` never runs → governor limits/pane discard unchanged until cockpit restart, contradicting the header 'มีผลทันทีและจำค่าไว้' (322).
findings.evidence: 2006/2016: `self.pending_performance_reload = True`; user_actions.py:387-388: `if dlg.exec() != dlg.DialogCode.Accepted: return`; 407: `if dlg.pending_performance_reload: self.orch.reload_performance_settings()`.
findings.fix: Apply the reload immediately in `_set_machine_mode`/`_on_pane_discard_toggled` via a callback/signal, or have the caller read `pending_performance_reload` regardless of the exec() result.

findings.title: Clicking a team-size card rebuilds the roster from disk and silently discards unsaved provider/model/effort edits on every role row
findings.scenario: Roles page → set backend's provider to codex and a model → then click 'ทีมเต็ม' card → `_rebuild_roster_panel()` deletes all rows and rebuilds them from `provider_config.role_provider_map` (2450) and `role_models.model_for` (2817) → backend is back to the on-disk value; the footer still shows 'มีการแก้ไขที่ยังไม่บันทึก' so Save & Apply looks like it will save the edit but writes the disk values.
findings.evidence: 2318-2323: `self.pending_team_preset = preset_id; self._mark_dirty(); self._refresh_team_size_panel(); self._rebuild_roster_panel()`; 2436-2441 clears every row widget; 2486-2489 resets the combo dicts.
findings.fix: Before rebuilding, snapshot each row's current provider/model/effort combo values and re-apply them to the rebuilt rows (or only update the enable toggles in place instead of a full rebuild).

findings.title: Claude API-override tab lists every provider's profiles (codex included) and resolves by first name match — override can be written into a codex home
findings.scenario: Accounts → 'การเชื่อมต่อ API (ขั้นสูง)' → profile combo shows codex accounts too (`user_profile.list_profiles()` returns all providers, user_profile.py:132-138, no filter). Saving for a codex account writes `takkub-claude-auth.json` into the codex home where nothing reads it (silently 'saved'). If a claude and a codex profile share a name (e.g. 'work'), `_users_auth_dir` (3810-3813) returns the first match, so the Claude override lands in the codex dir and the claude 'work' panes keep default auth.
findings.evidence: 3661: `self._up_profiles = user_profile.list_profiles()`; 3706-3707: `for p in self._up_profiles: self._up_auth_combo.addItem(p["name"])`; 3810-3812: `for p in self._up_profiles: if p["name"] == profile_name: return Path(p["config_dir"])`.
findings.fix: Populate the combo from `user_profile.profiles_for_provider("claude")` and key the lookup by (provider, name) / store config_dir as item data.

findings.title: Selecting another template (or Duplicate/Delete) drops the staged hop edits of the template being edited while the dirty flag stays set
findings.scenario: Pipeline page → edit hops of template A (add/remove roles; staged in `_pb_hops`) → click template B in the list (or press Duplicate/Delete, which reloads the list and reselects row 0 at 5092) → `_load_pb_hops(B)` replaces `_pb_hops` → A's edits are gone; Save & Apply then writes B's (unchanged) hops into pipelines.json (1645-1650) and clears dirty, so the user believes A was saved.
findings.evidence: 5108-5114: `tid = current.data(...)` … `self._load_pb_hops(tid)`; 5841-5843: `self._pb_hops = ([[dict(entry) ...] for hop in tpl["hops"]] if tpl else [])`; 5137/5154: `self._reload_templates_list()` after persist.
findings.fix: Keep a per-template staged-hops dict (`{template_id: hops}`) and flush every staged entry on Save; after Duplicate/Delete reselect the previously selected id instead of row 0.

findings.title: create_skill writes description into YAML frontmatter unescaped — ': ' / '#' / leading '[{*&!%@' / newline breaks the skill
findings.scenario: Settings → New Skill with description 'Use when: reviewing PRs' or 'ใช้เมื่อ: …' (colon-space), or a description containing ' #', or starting with '[', '*', '&', '%', '@', '`', or a quote. The written SKILL.md has invalid YAML: `_parse_frontmatter` returns {} so the Skill Matrix/catalog shows no description (falls back to dir name), and Claude Code's own skill loader cannot parse the frontmatter, so the skill never auto-triggers. `update_skill` (line 548) correctly uses `yaml.safe_dump`; only the create path is raw. Reachable from settings_window.py:4612 and settings_management/repositories/skills.py:175 and :208 (duplicate copies a description that came out of a YAML parse, so it can legitimately contain ': ').
findings.fix: Build the frontmatter with `yaml.safe_dump({'name': name, 'description': description}, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False)` exactly like update_skill.

findings.title: Native Chrome launch busy-waits up to 8 s with time.sleep on the Qt main thread for every qa/critic/designer spawn on Windows
findings.scenario: First assign to qa/critic/designer on Windows (CDP 9222 not up): spawn() calls NativeChromeManager.ensure_started() inline. browser_chrome.py:183-189 loops `while time.monotonic() < deadline: if self._cdp_ready()...; time.sleep(0.05)` with _START_TIMEOUT_SEC = 8.0 — the whole cockpit (all panes' terminals, Lead typing) freezes until headless Chrome exposes CDP (1–3 s normally, 8 s when Chrome is slow/blocked, e.g. AV or a stale profile lock). Repeats whenever Chrome was closed/killed between spawns.
findings.evidence:
chrome_ok, chrome_msg = manager.ensure_started()
_log_event("native_chrome", role=role_name, project=project_ns, ok=chrome_ok, msg=chrome_msg)
findings.fix: Popen Chrome and return immediately; poll _cdp_ready from a QTimer (or a worker thread) and log the result asynchronously — the pane does not need CDP before the ConPTY spawn.

findings.title: Non-claude teammate shard panes resolve cwd with the shard name (qa#2) instead of base_role, landing in the wrong project path
findings.scenario: Project paths {'api': ..., 'web': ...}; qa is routed to gemini/codex; `takkub assign --role qa --shards 2` (browser roles still fan out as real panes). The generic branch calls default_cwd_for_role('qa#1') — _ROLE_PATH_PREFS and the project's role_paths override are keyed by bare role, so lookup misses and falls to `next(iter(paths.values()))` = api/. The claude branch (line 3029) correctly uses base_role and lands in web/. Result: gemini/codex shards run tests, plant AGENTS.md and take screenshots in the wrong sub-project, while the same role on claude works.
findings.fix: Use default_cwd_for_role(base_role, project=project_ns) in the generic-provider branch, matching the claude branch.

findings.title: First codex/opencode/kimi spawn on an installed build seeds the isolated home synchronously on the main thread: unbounded rglob + up to 40 x 64 MB copies
findings.scenario: Prod install (DATA_HOME != REPO_ROOT), first ever codex pane: ensure_provider_home -> _seed_codex -> _clone_codex_sessions does `sessions.rglob('rollout-*.jsonl')` over the user's entire ~/.codex/sessions tree, stats every file, sorts, opens the head of each candidate, then copy2's up to RECENT_SESSIONS_CLONE=40 files each allowed up to _MAX_ITEM_BYTES=64 MB — all inline inside spawn() on the GUI thread. A user with months of codex history sees the cockpit hang for tens of seconds on the first codex assign, with no progress indication; _is_teammate_rollout reads a whole file when it has no user_message line.
findings.evidence:
files = [p for p in sessions.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl") if p.is_file()]
...
_copy_item(path, target)
findings.fix: Run the seed on a worker thread (or at boot in boot_update/boot_flow before any pane exists, as the module docstring already suggests for updates), and/or cap total bytes (e.g. 256 MB) and per-file size far below 64 MB.

findings.title: User typing `exit` in the Open-Shell pane is treated as a crash: Lead gets a 'process died mid-task' notice and the shell is auto-respawned twice
findings.scenario: User clicks Open Shell, runs a few git commands, types `exit` (code 0). AgentPane._on_process_exited -> decide_exit_state returns 'exited' (expected_exit only set by close()/done()). _on_session_exit sees state=='exited', calls _warn_lead_pane_exited('shell') -> Lead is told 'pane shell exited (code 0) without done-report — process ตายกลางงาน', then schedules _auto_respawn; a fresh pwsh appears 2.5 s later. Exiting again -> respawn after 5 s; third time -> _warn_lead_respawn_capped + close(). Same for a shell that the user closes with Ctrl-D.
findings.evidence:
if pane is None or pane.state != "exited":
    return
self._write_pane_exit_snapshot(role_name, project, session)
self._warn_lead_pane_exited(role_name, project, exit_code)
findings.fix: Early-return in _on_session_exit (before the notice and before scheduling _auto_respawn) when role_name == 'shell' (or when the pane's provider_name is 'shell'); also skip _warn_lead_pane_exited for shell.

findings.title: A failed auto-respawn is silent: Lead was told to wait for auto-respawn, but a spawn() failure is only written to events.log
findings.scenario: Pane crashes; _warn_lead_pane_exited tells Lead 'ถ้า auto-respawn อยู่รอรอบถัดไปได้'. 2.5 s later _auto_respawn -> spawn() returns (False, msg) — e.g. provider binary mid-update / missing (`spec.install_instructions`), role toggled off in Settings, McpResolutionError, cwd no longer valid (worktree finalized), or find_claude_executable RuntimeError. Only `auto_respawn_done ok=False` is logged; _warn_lead_spawn_failed (used by assign() at orchestrator.py:4002 and lead_inbox.py:3517) is never called here. The pane slot stays 'exited' forever, auto-chain/pipeline waits, `takkub wait` sits blind, and Lead believes recovery is in progress.
findings.fix: On `not ok`, call self._warn_lead_spawn_failed(role_name, project, msg) and run the same capped-pane bookkeeping as the AUTO_RESPAWN_MAX branch (auto-chain release, pipeline hop_failed, close()).

findings.title: _update_status (2s timer + every statusChanged) does ~17 uncached file reads on the Qt main thread per tick
findings.scenario: Every 2s and on each statusChanged emit: _update_provider_chip calls user_profile.profile_for up to 12× (6 providers in the text loop at 685-689 and again in the tooltip loop at 700-703); each call does an uncached `path.read_text` of projects/<slug>/user-profile.json (user_profile.py:401-404). _refresh_team_preset_chip adds 3 uncached team_preset._load_raw reads (current → current_preset_id, plus active_override), _refresh_plan_badge 2 more. #658 documented 1-10s read_text stalls on a wedged disk and converted _load_registry to cached_read, but the per-project profile file and team_preset.json were left uncached — on a slow/AV-scanned disk this is the exact 'Lead พิมพ์ช้า / main_thread_stall' symptom.
findings.evidence: status_header.py:685-689 `for p in PROVIDER_REGISTRY: ... prof = user_profile.profile_for(proj, provider=p)` · user_profile.py:401-402 `raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (no cached_read) · team_preset.py:237-240 `if not p.exists(): return {}` / `json.loads(p.read_text(...))`
findings.fix: Read user-profile.json and team_preset.json through cached_read.read_cached (with invalidate() in their writers), and compute profile_for once per provider per tick (build the text and tooltip from one dict).

findings.title: UNCERTAIN is in _IN_FLIGHT_STATES → every [delivery-uncertain] is followed ≤120 s later by a second [delivery-stale-reap] notice for the same delivery
findings.scenario: A gemini pane returns to its ready prompt after the paste (the #359/#404 shape). `_on_settled` marks UNCERTAIN and sends `[delivery-uncertain]` (lead_inbox.py:2678). The delivery keeps its 120 s TTL; `expire_stale()` (task_delivery.py:514) reaps it and `_reap_stale_deliveries` (lead_inbox.py:2528) sends `[delivery-stale-reap] … ยกเลิก delivery นี้แล้ว` — two contradictory instructions ('ไม่ต้อง assign ใหม่ / เปิด pane ดู' then 'ยกเลิกแล้ว แนะนำ assign ใหม่') for one event, unless the pane happens to show progress.
findings.evidence: task_delivery.py:73-80 `_IN_FLIGHT_STATES = {QUEUED, WAITING_RESOURCE, WRITING, WRITTEN, SUBMITTING, UNCERTAIN}`; lead_inbox.py:1648-1649 `manager.mark_uncertain(...)` / `self._warn_lead_delivery_uncertain(...)`; lead_inbox.py:2494 `for delivery in delivery_manager.expire_stale():`
findings.fix: Either exclude UNCERTAIN from `_IN_FLIGHT_STATES` (it already released its slot and was announced) or record the uncertain notice in `_stale_reap_notified` so the reaper's cooldown suppresses the second notice.

findings.title: _pending_writes grows unbounded on a discarded pane and is replayed as one giant termWrite on reattach
findings.scenario: Teammate pane in a background project tab goes idle >10s -> #364 discard fires (_page_ready=False, renderer discarded). Pane then receives a new task and works for 30-60 min: every PTY chunk (spinner repaints, tool output) goes to `_pending_writes` (raw ANSI, MBs/hour). User switches to that tab -> _reattach -> _on_page_ready L791-794 extends `_write_buf` with everything and `_flush_writes` does one `"".join` + `_strip_osc52` regex + `json.dumps` + `runJavaScript(termWrite(<N MB>))` -> renderer and main thread freeze for seconds; Python RSS also grows the whole time the pane is hidden.
findings.evidence: terminal_widget.py:547-548 `if not self._page_ready: self._pending_writes.append(text); return` — no cap; `_MAX_DISCARD_SNAPSHOT_LINES` (L72) caps only the snapshot. L791-794 replays all of it in one flush.
findings.fix: Cap `_pending_writes` (keep only the tail, e.g. last 256 KB / N lines, since xterm scrollback is 500 lines anyway) and, when truncated, prepend a `\x1b[2J` or rely on the Ctrl-L redraw; or stop queueing while `_discarded` and just request a redraw on reattach.

findings.title: 'Enable updates' converts to a git checkout synchronously on the Qt main thread (git init/remote/fetch/reset, up to ~2 min) → whole cockpit frozen
findings.scenario: A copied/ZIP install (no .git, not site-packages) shows '🔧 Enable updates'; user clicks OK on the confirm → `init_git_repo()` runs `git init` (15 s cap), `remote add` (15 s), `fetch origin main` (60 s — a full history fetch), `reset --hard` (30 s) inline; `_status.showMessage('Converting…')` never repaints because the event loop is blocked, panes stop updating, and the watchdog can mis-read the stall. Same class: `_on_update_clicked` line 948 runs `local_status()` (two git subprocesses) on the main thread.
findings.evidence: update_panel.py:921-923 `self._status.showMessage("Converting to git checkout — fetching origin/main…", 0)` / `ok, msg = init_git_repo()` / `self._status.clearMessage()` — no QRunnable/QThread; update_helper.init_git_repo 334-361 is plain subprocess.run.
findings.fix: Run init_git_repo (and the dirty re-check local_status) on a QRunnable like PullUpdateWorker/_safe_emit and finish in a slot; disable the chip while it runs.

findings.title: Silent self-update re-execs `python <path>/__main__.py` → ImportError on relative imports; the cockpit dies right after pulling on a git checkout
findings.scenario: Dev/git-checkout install launched the documented way (agent-takkub.bat:110 `start "" ".venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe" -m agent_takkub`). origin/main gains commits (e.g. dependabot merge), tree is clean → try_silent_self_update pulls, prints 'restarting...' and calls `os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, *sys.argv])`. Under `-m`, Python sets sys.argv[0] to the full path of agent_takkub/__main__.py, so the successor runs it as a top-level script and __main__.py:27/38 `from .cli import …` / `from .app import main` raise ImportError → no cockpit; the user has to relaunch by hand (which then works because the pull already landed).
findings.evidence: update_worker.py:352 `os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, *sys.argv])`; reproduced: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe src/agent_takkub/__main__.py --help` → `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` (exit 1) while `python -m agent_takkub --help` works. `_restart_cockpit` (update_panel.py:1166) and build_pip_sync_script already use the `-m agent_takkub` form.
findings.fix: `os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, "-m", "agent_takkub", *sys.argv[1:]])` (or reuse build_restart_successor_env + the same argv `_restart_cockpit` uses).

findings.title: Claude importer never reads subagent transcripts (projects/<slug>/<session>/subagents/*.jsonl)
findings.scenario: Every `takkub assign --shards N` (1 pane + N native subagents, #641) and every Lead-side Agent call writes its assistant turns to projects/<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl. import_claude only globs one level, so those tokens never reach the ledger: Settings > Usage and `takkub usage` under-report claude spend (verified on this machine: 27 subagents/ dirs under ~/.agent-takkub/claude-config/projects, 7 under ~/.claude/projects, each with .jsonl files).
findings.evidence: L668: `for jsonl_path in projects_dir.glob("*/*.jsonl"):`
findings.fix: Use `projects_dir.rglob("*.jsonl")` (or add `*/*/subagents/*.jsonl`); request-id dedup in record_turn already prevents double counting.

findings.title: 'วันนี้' / daily buckets use the UTC calendar day, not the user's local day
findings.scenario: Bangkok user (UTC+7) opens Settings > Usage at 09:00 and picks 'วันนี้' (settings_usage.py:80-81 -> days=1): start/end are UTC dates, and _aggregate_rows buckets by ts[:10] (UTC). The row set covers 07:00 today .. now only; turns from 00:00-07:00 local are attributed to yesterday and the sparkline's day columns are shifted by 7 h. Status line shows local time (settings_usage.py:613), reinforcing the mismatch.
findings.evidence: L1319-1321: `end_date = datetime.now(tz=UTC).date()` / `start_date = _date.fromordinal(end_date.toordinal() - (n - 1))`   L1006: `date_str = ts[:10]` (UTC ISO prefix)
findings.fix: Convert each row ts to local date when aggregating/filtering (datetime.fromisoformat(ts).astimezone().date()) and compute start/end with datetime.now().date(); or label the range as UTC.

findings.title: 'Lead ใช้ provider' menu hardcodes claude/codex/gemini; opencode, kimi and cursor Leads cannot be selected
findings.scenario: A user whose Lead runs on OpenCode/Kimi/Cursor (supported per lead_context.py and seen in the field) opens 🤖 Accounts -> 'Lead ใช้ provider': their current provider is not listed (no item checked) and they cannot switch to it from the UI.
findings.evidence: user_actions.py:200 `for prov in ("claude", "codex", "gemini"):` while :169 iterates the full `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` for the accounts section; lead_context.py:481 states Lead runs via Claude, Codex, Gemini/agy, OpenCode, Kimi, Cursor; doctor.py:3230 references a field OpenCode Lead.
findings.fix: Iterate `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` (filtered by installed/enabled via provider_state) for the Lead submenu instead of the literal triple.

findings.title: Settings -> Remote Enable runs the entire blocking remote start (bind, loopback probe, cloudflared spawn+sleep, 5 s public probe) on the Qt main thread
findings.scenario: User clicks Enable in the Remote dialog with a named tunnel or a slow/unreachable edge: the whole cockpit (panes, IPC, Lead typing) freezes for ~1-8 s; the watchdog logs a main_thread_stall. #640 only moved the BOOT path off-thread.
findings.evidence: user_actions.py:854 `self._remote = _remote_mod.RemoteControl.maybe_start(` -> remote/__init__.py:90 `prepare` -> :162-232 `_start_blocking` (`reap_orphan_tunnel` psutil walk, `start_server`, :208 `probe_local` timeout 2 s, :228 `Tunnel.start()` -> tunnel.py:554 `time.sleep(_STARTUP_CHECK_S)`); then user_actions.py:900 `_remote_start_warning(..., probe_public=...)` -> :937 `diagnostics.probe_public` with `_DEFAULT_PUBLIC_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0` (diagnostics.py:34). Boot path uses `self.cli.run_off_thread` (main_window.py:1047) instead.
findings.fix: Mirror the boot path: run `RemoteControl.prepare` and `probe_public` via `self.cli.run_off_thread`, then `finish_start()` + dialog `_render_state` in the main-thread callback; make `on_apply` async (dialog shows 'starting...').

findings.title: profile_for() does an uncached read_text per call; status header calls it 11x every 2s on the Qt main thread (the #658 class, only half-fixed)
findings.scenario: status_header._update_status runs on a 2s QTimer (status_header.py:651) and calls _update_provider_chip (L760), which calls user_profile.profile_for once for Lead plus twice per other provider in PROVIDER_REGISTRY (L679, L685-688, L700-703) = 11 calls, each doing `path.read_text` + json.loads of projects/<slug>/user-profile.json with no cached_read. #658 cached _load_registry (L105) for exactly this caller but left profile_for/default_provider uncached. On the wedged-disk condition the codebase documents (781 ms per read captured in #658), this is ~8s of blocking per tick -> UI freeze / main_thread_stall events.
findings.evidence: user_profile.py:402-403 `raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` / `data = json.loads(raw)`; status_header.py:685-688 `for p in PROVIDER_REGISTRY: if p != lead_provider: prof = user_profile.profile_for(proj, provider=p)`; status_header.py:651 `self._status_timer.setInterval(2_000)`
findings.fix: Read the per-project file through cached_read.read_cached(path, json.loads, missing={}) in profile_for/default_provider (the writer _atomic_write already invalidates at L85); and have _update_provider_chip read the file once and derive all providers from it.

findings.title: clean_isolated's 5-minute dir-mtime guard blocks explicit --branch/--force/--discard cleans and mislabels the reason
findings.scenario: Lead closes a pane and runs `takkub worktree clean --branch wt/backend-<ts> --discard` within 5 min of the pane's last top-level write (any build output or `pnpm install` bumps the worktree dir's own mtime, not just creation). Output: 'KEEP wt/backend-… — worktree สร้างใหม่ (120s ที่แล้ว) — pane อาจยังไม่ register' — wrong (worktree may be hours old) and the explicit request is silently refused; the user retries and thinks clean is broken. Worktrees whose dir is missing skip the guard (mtime=0) while intact ones don't.
findings.evidence: worktree_manager.py:2201-2209 `mtime = worktree_path.stat().st_mtime if worktree_path.exists() else 0` / `if elapsed < 300:` → `continue`, evaluated for every row before the force/discard/branch logic, with no bypass when `branch is not None`.
findings.fix: Skip the guard when `branch` is given or `force`/`discard` is set, and derive age from the registration (`.git/worktrees/<id>` creation time or the `.git` pointer file's mtime) rather than the checkout dir's mtime.

findings.title: done() still shells out to git on the Qt thread — #408 offload bypassed by later additions
findings.scenario: Any `takkub done` from a shared-tree pane in a project with 2-3 other shared-tree panes on a large Windows repo: cli_server._run_off_thread precomputes collect_done_git_facts off-thread, then runs Orchestrator.done() on the Qt thread via _mainThreadCall (cli_server.py:289-309, 1159-1171). done() then calls count_test_files_in_diff (orchestrator.py:7896 → worktree_manager.py:2761 `git diff --numstat` + :2769 `git status --porcelain`), _sibling_shared_tree_touched_paths (orchestrator.py:8083 → 7535-7540: diffstat_since + shared_tree_status_porcelain + dirty_snapshot per sibling pane), and dirty_snapshot again at 7414 and 7688 (each a `git status -z -uall` when collapsed untracked dirs exist). 8-14 git processes at 30-40 ms spawn cost plus multi-second `git status` on big repos = Lead's typed input freezes for seconds on every done.
findings.evidence: worktree_manager.py:2761 `res = mgr._run(diff_args, None)` and :2769 `res_status = mgr._run(["-C", cwd, "status", "--porcelain"], None)` called from orchestrator.py:7896 inside done(); orchestrator.py:7535 `sib_diffstat = mgr.diffstat_since(sib_cwd, sib_base_sha)` / :7536 / :7540 loop over every sibling pane, reached from done() at :8083.
findings.fix: Move count_test_files_in_diff and _sibling_shared_tree_touched_paths into the off-thread `_collect` payload (extend done_git_inputs/collect_done_git_facts to return `test_files` and `sibling_touched`), and have _compute_digest_facts reuse `dirty_snapshot` computed off-thread instead of re-running it at 7414/7688.

findings.title: Periodic sweeper's already_seen set is never pruned; recycled HWND values are never re-evaluated
findings.scenario: Long-running cockpit session: a console HWND value ruled 'not ours' (or already hidden) is destroyed and Windows recycles the same HWND value for a new codex `pwsh` console minutes later. `fresh = snapshot - already_seen` excludes it, so the parent walk never runs and the window stays visible (the flash the sweeper exists to hide); `_console_hwnds_seen` also grows monotonically.
findings.evidence: _win_console.py:190 `fresh = snapshot_console_hwnds() - already_seen`; L195 `already_seen.add(hwnd)`; no removal anywhere; pty_session.py:1425 module-global `_console_hwnds_seen` lives for the process lifetime.
findings.fix: Each sweep: `already_seen.intersection_update(current)` before computing `fresh`.

findings.title: SESSION_CAP_SETTING is read from QSettings at pane construction but nothing ever writes it (phantom knob, and would be stale if it were)
findings.scenario: The session-cap threshold is resolved once per pane from QSettings key `session_cap/prompt_tokens`; no Settings page or CLI path sets that key anywhere in the repo, so every user runs the hard default. If a writer were added later, existing panes would keep the old `_session_cap_spec` until re-created.
findings.evidence: Grep `SESSION_CAP_SETTING|session_cap/prompt_tokens` over *.py -> only session_cap.py:25 (definition) and agent_pane.py:37/132 (read). No `setValue`.
findings.fix: Either expose it in Settings > Performance and re-resolve in `apply_performance_settings`, or drop the QSettings read and make the default explicit.

findings.title: Constructing any pane overwrites the global "last zoom" fallback with that role's stored size
findings.scenario: User zoomed Lead to 14 pt (writes `pane/_default/font_pt`=14). Cockpit boots or a teammate pane is created: `_restore_font_size` finds `pane/<role>/font_pt`=10 -> `set_font_point_size(10)` -> emits `fontSizeChanged` -> `_save_font_size(10)` -> `pane/_default/font_pt`=10. The next brand-new role pane (e.g. qa#2) falls back to 10 instead of the user's last zoom; after boot the fallback is whatever pane happened to be built last.
findings.evidence: agent_pane.py:1165 `self._terminal.set_font_point_size(size)` -> terminal_widget.py:665 `self.fontSizeChanged.emit(size)` -> agent_pane.py:1167-1171 `s.setValue(self._FONT_SIZE_DEFAULT_KEY, int(size))`.
findings.fix: Have `_restore_font_size` apply the size without emitting (e.g. a `persist=False` flag on `set_font_point_size`), or only write `_FONT_SIZE_DEFAULT_KEY` from `_on_font_zoomed`/button paths.

findings.title: Auto clear-view writes Ctrl-L (\x0c) into every provider's PTY; redraw semantics only confirmed for claude
findings.scenario: A codex/opencode/kimi/cursor teammate pane sits hidden and quiet for 10 min (`_check_idle_auto_clear`) or enters `done` (`_on_done_clear_timeout`) -> `session.write("\x0c")`. If that TUI does not bind Ctrl-L to redraw, the byte is either ignored (pane stays blank until next output) or inserted into the composer ahead of the next paste. Not gated per provider and no ProviderSpec capability for it.
findings.evidence: agent_pane.py:1178-1184 `_clear_pane_view` unconditional `self.session.write("\x0c")`; callers L1186-1195 and L1197-1217 have no provider check; only comment L1176 asserts Ctrl+L redraw (claude behaviour).
findings.fix: Add a `ProviderSpec.clear_screen_seq` (None = skip the write, just wipe xterm) and gate the nudge on it; confirm per provider by capture before enabling.

findings.title: Export button writes only the visible pyte screen (36 rows), not the pane buffer/scrollback it advertises
findings.scenario: User clicks ⤓ ("Export pane buffer to .txt") on a pane after a long run expecting the transcript; the file contains just the last screenful (rows x cols of the pyte grid), everything scrolled off is missing.
findings.evidence: agent_pane.py:1230 `text = "\n".join(self.session.display_lines()).rstrip()` — `display_lines()` is the pyte screen memo (pty_session.py:2424-2438). `TerminalWidget.request_buffer_text` (terminal_widget.py:673) exists to fetch the real xterm buffer but is unused in production.
findings.fix: Use `self._terminal.request_buffer_text(lambda text: write(text))` with a fallback to `display_lines()` while discarded.

findings.title: Catch-all redaction regex blanks every ≥20-char identifier, so auto-filed tracebacks lose function names and paths
findings.scenario: Any auto-captured cockpit crash: `_redact` runs `\b[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{20,}\b` over the traceback, which matches ordinary Python identifiers (`_maybe_fire_auto_chain_handoff`, `_check_idle_teammates`, `_inject_shard_fanout_handoff`) and posix path fragments (`v2/state/issues/dedup`), so the GitHub issue body reads `in [redacted]` / `[redacted].py` and the maintainer cannot see which frame crashed; only the `file:line` in the title survives.
findings.evidence: auto_issue_capture.py:82 `re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{20,}\b"),` applied at :288 `tb_text = _redact(_scrub_home(tb_text))`.
findings.fix: Require token shape (must contain both letters and digits, or no `_`), skip tokens that are valid Python identifiers / follow `in ` on a `File "..."` frame line, or run the catch-all only on the exception message, not the frame lines.

findings.title: `stop_watch` is never called
findings.scenario: Only `start_watch()` is wired (app.py:1348); the scan thread is daemon so nothing breaks, but the stop API and `_stop` Event are unreachable in production.
findings.evidence: auto_issue_signals.py:394 `def stop_watch() -> None:` — only hit in src is the definition and `__all__`.
findings.fix: Wire into app shutdown or remove `stop_watch` + `__all__` entry (keep `_stop` for the loop).

findings.title: Order-mode click / quick action rebuilds the list, which clears selection and blanks the detail pane
findings.scenario: Owner toggles 'โหมดเลือกลำดับงาน' and clicks a card: `_on_click` → `_rebuild_list()` → `QListWidget.clear()` emits `currentItemChanged(None, prev)` → `_on_select(None)` sets the detail pane to '' and no item is current afterwards; every pick wipes the detail the owner was reading. Same after `พักไว้`/`เสร็จแล้ว` (`_quick` → `_reload`), so a follow-up ตกลง in non-order mode has no current id and silently does nothing (`_confirm` returns at `if not ordered`).
findings.evidence: backlog_dialog.py:166 `self._list.clear()`; :116 `self._list.currentItemChanged.connect(self._on_select)`; :193-195 `if cur is None: self._detail.setPlainText(""); return`; :245-249 `ids = [cur] if cur else [] … if not ordered: return`.
findings.fix: In `_rebuild_list` capture `self._current_id()` first, block signals during `clear()`/`addItem`, then re-select the row whose UserRole matches; in `_confirm` show a status hint when nothing is selected.

findings.title: Window's has_update (`latest != current`) ignores backend status/selected → phantom 'มีอัพเดต' rows whose 'อัพเดตที่เลือก' silently does nothing
findings.scenario: A provider whose `--version` probe fails/times out (current None) or whose installed build is newer than the registry's latest tag: backend sets status FAILED/UP_TO_DATE with selected=False (boot_flow.py:159-183, compare_versions-based) but the window computes `has_update = bool(latest) and latest != current` → row shows 'มีอัพเดต', an interactive checkbox, page A appears every boot ('พบอัพเดต 1 รายการ'), and clicking 'อัพเดตที่เลือก' passes the original item whose `selected` is False, which `run_provider_updates` (boot_flow.py:242-244 `if not item.selected: out.append(item); continue`) passes through untouched.
findings.evidence: boot_flow_window.py:1021-1022 `has_update = bool(latest) and latest != current` / `selected = bool(getattr(item, "selected", has_update))`; 188-193 `_has_update` same rule; 1071-1074 selected_items are the untouched backend items.
findings.fix: Drive rows from `item.status == PROVIDER_STATUS_UPDATE_AVAILABLE` (show FAILED rows as 'ตรวจสอบไม่สำเร็จ') and pass `replace(item, selected=True)` for user-checked rows.

findings.title: Remembered 'skip' still runs the full provider probe every boot (5 `--version` subprocesses + npm view calls) before proceeding
findings.scenario: User ticks 'จำตัวเลือกนี้ไว้' and 'ข้าม — ใช้เวอร์ชันเดิม'. Next boots: start() sees mode 'skip' but `_apply_remembered_choice` starts `_CallWorker(check_provider_updates(30.0))` first and only checks `mode == 'skip'` inside `_on_items`. Measured 1.8 s online here; offline/flaky network each `npm view` waits for its 30 s cap (claude, codex, opencode) plus 15 s `--version` caps, so a boot the user explicitly asked not to check providers on can stall 30–90 s and eat into the 180 s gate.
findings.evidence: 2160-2162 `def _apply_remembered_choice(self, mode, selected_names):` / `worker = _CallWorker(lambda: flow.check_provider_updates(30.0), self)`; 2168-2170 the `mode == "skip"` early-return is inside the result callback.
findings.fix: In start()/_apply_remembered_choice, `if mode == 'skip': self._proceed_to_migration_check(); return` before creating the worker.

findings.title: count_user_corrections / count_tool_retries / count_hook_fires have no callers (superseded by scan_hot_md_metrics)
findings.scenario: No call site anywhere in src/ (orchestrator uses scan_hot_md_metrics at 11897); the three functions each re-walk every jsonl and duplicate the logic inside scan_hot_md_metrics, so any future fix has to be made twice.
findings.evidence:
chatlog_scanner.py:325 `def count_user_corrections(`
chatlog_scanner.py:363 `def count_tool_retries(`
chatlog_scanner.py:562 `def count_hook_fires(`
findings.fix: Delete the three functions (and any tests that only exercise them) or make scan_hot_md_metrics the single implementation they delegate to.

findings.title: _instance_banner's installed-build branch probes REPO_ROOT/runtime/port where REPO_ROOT is <venv>/Lib — dead: prod CLI can never warn that a dev cockpit is also running
findings.scenario: User has both prod (installed) and dev cockpits up and runs `takkub list` from a prod pane: the code looks for the dev instance's port file at `Path(config.REPO_ROOT) / "runtime" / "port"`, but for an installed package `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` = `<venv>/Lib` (site-packages' parent), which never has runtime/port → FileNotFoundError swallowed at 426 → no ⚠ line. Only the dev→prod direction (401-402, hardcoded ~/.agent-takkub) works.
findings.evidence: cli.py:403-405 `else: other_port_file = Path(config.REPO_ROOT) / "runtime" / "port"; other_data_home = Path(config.REPO_ROOT)`; config.py:184 `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`.
findings.fix: Either drop the installed-build branch (accept one-directional warning) or resolve the dev checkout via a recorded path (e.g. a `dev-checkout` breadcrumb the dev cockpit writes into ~/.agent-takkub/runtime) instead of REPO_ROOT.

findings.title: cmd_provider install: `if … : pass` no-op block
findings.scenario: After a failed `takkub provider install <name>` for a manual-only provider the code evaluates `installable_providers()` and `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` only to execute `pass`; nothing observable happens on either branch.
findings.evidence: cli.py:4458-4460 `if not ok and name not in installable_providers() and name in PROVIDER_REGISTRY:` / `# manual-only provider — the message already carries the instructions` / `pass`.
findings.fix: Delete the three lines (and the now-unused `installable_providers` import at 4368).

findings.title: docs-verify / audit-skills write their report into `runtime/…` relative to the pane's CWD — litters a `runtime/` dir into the user's project repo
findings.scenario: A pane (any role — neither command is lead-gated) runs `takkub docs-verify` or `takkub audit-skills` while cwd is the user's project (the normal pane cwd): `Path(args.report)` = `runtime/docs_drift.md` relative to cwd, `output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (3300, 3376) creates `<user-project>/runtime/` and writes the report there, showing up in the user's `git status`.
findings.evidence: cli.py:6419 `sdv.add_argument("--report", default="runtime/docs_drift.md")`, 6464 `sas.add_argument("--output", default="runtime/skill_audit.md")`; 3299-3301 `output_path = Path(args.report); output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); output_path.write_text(report, …)`.
findings.fix: Default the report path under `config.RUNTIME_DIR` (e.g. `RUNTIME_DIR / "docs_drift.md"`) and anchor a relative `--report` to REPO_ROOT, not cwd.

findings.title: `mcp add --command` uses dest 'command' and overwrites the top-level subcommand name (same class as #483)
findings.scenario: `takkub mcp add foo --command npx …` → after parsing, `args.command == 'npx'` (not 'mcp'), so main()'s `_enforce_role_gate(args.command)`, the `_WRITE_COMMANDS_REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION` check and the `{list,status,inbox}` banner check all key on the MCP executable name; `--command list` prints the other-instance banner, and any future lead-only/confirmation entry for 'mcp' is bypassed. cmd_mcp itself still works because it self-gates and reads `args.command` as the executable.
findings.evidence: Verified live: `build_parser().parse_args(['mcp','add','foo','--command','list']).command` → `'list'` (mcp_command='add'). Code: `sm_add.add_argument("--command", required=True, metavar="CMD")` (6691) vs `sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)` (5418); the file's own #483 comment at 6389-6394 documents this exact hazard for spawn-service.
findings.fix: `sm_add.add_argument("--command", dest="mcp_exe", …)` and use `args.mcp_exe` in cmd_mcp (5266).

findings.title: `_done_auth_warned` latch is never cleared — only the first stale-token `done` per (project, role) ever reaches Lead
findings.scenario: backend's pane is respawned; its old shell (or a retried CLI) calls `takkub done` with the retired token → Lead gets `[done-auth-rejected] backend` once. Days later the same thing happens for a new backend pane → silently rejected, Lead sees 'nothing happened'.
findings.evidence: line 676-686: `warned = getattr(self, "_done_auth_warned", set())` … `warned.add((target_project, target_role))` with no removal anywhere (grep: single writer).
