findings.fix: Key the latch by token instead of (project, role), or clear the pair when a new token is minted for that role.

findings.title: "version" cmd alias is never sent by any client
findings.scenario: `elif cmd in ("instance-identity", "version")` — cli.py only ever sends `instance-identity` (cli.py:305, 3693); nothing in src/ sends `version`.
findings.evidence: Grep of `"cmd": "..."` literals in cli.py and remote/ shows no `version`.
findings.fix: Remove the alias (or document it as an external-client contract).

findings.title: `team set` escalation gate only checks `from == lead`; the command is neither lead-only nor token-gated, so a teammate pane can flip the project to solo-lead/pair
findings.scenario: A backend/codex pane runs `takkub team set solo-lead` (from: backend). cli.py LEAD_ONLY_COMMANDS (cli.py:37-70) has no `team`, the server's `_LEAD_ONLY_CMDS`/`_token_gated_cmds` don't include it, and line 1656 skips the B-M1 check for non-lead callers → `set_team_preset('solo-lead')` succeeds and `lead_may_implement` lifts Lead's Edit/Write guard for every future task in that project.
findings.evidence: line 1656: `if team_action == "set" and from_role_norm == "lead":` guards only the Lead caller; line 1686-1689 then applies the preset unconditionally.
findings.fix: Require the Lead token OR an empty `from` (non-pane terminal) for `team set`; reject any non-empty non-lead `from`.

findings.title: Generated takkub.cmd spawns a PowerShell child on every invocation (~220-260 ms) just to read 2 header bytes
findings.scenario: Any `takkub …` call routed through cmd.exe/PowerShell on Windows (codex/opencode panes use PowerShell; a user's PowerShell terminal; the dev `bin/takkub.cmd` has the identical `for /f … powershell -NoProfile` line 32) pays a full `powershell.exe` start before Python even launches — on top of Python startup, for every done/progress/send/status. Claude panes are unaffected (Git Bash resolves the sh shim).
findings.evidence: Measured 3× on this machine: 260 ms, 220 ms, 226 ms for the exact probe command. Code: `'for /f "usebackq" %%M in (`powershell -NoProfile -Command "$fs=[System.IO.File]::OpenRead(…)…"`) do set PYMAGIC=%%M'` (69).
findings.fix: Replace the PowerShell probe with a cmd-native check (e.g. `findstr /B /M /C:MZ` on the first bytes via `more +0` is unreliable; simplest: `certutil -encodehex … 1` or skip the magic check in the .cmd shim and rely on the size floor + `%PY% -c` exit code), or cache the verdict in a marker file keyed on python.exe mtime/size.

findings.title: `QLineEdit::placeholder` is not a Qt QSS sub-control — rule is ignored, placeholder stays unreadable
findings.scenario: Settings/New Role inputs on dark ground: the comment says this rule fixes the near-invisible placeholder, but Qt's style-sheet parser has no `::placeholder` pseudo-element, so the block is dropped and the palette default is still used.
findings.evidence: cockpit_theme.py:972-974 `QLineEdit::placeholder {{\n        color: {TEXT_MUTED};\n    }}`
findings.fix: Set `QPalette.ColorRole.PlaceholderText` on the application/dialog palette (retheme() hook) instead of a QSS pseudo-element.

findings.title: _ensure_git_excluded writes an unanchored `AGENTS.md` pattern to .git/info/exclude and never removes it — hides any future user AGENTS.md at any depth from git status
findings.scenario: Spawn any codex/agy teammate into a repo once → `.git/info/exclude` gains the line `AGENTS.md` (matches at every depth). remove_managed_context_files later deletes the planted file but the exclude line stays. When the user later writes their own AGENTS.md (root or e.g. apps/api/AGENTS.md) it never shows in `git status`/`git add .` — they ship without it and don't know why.
findings.evidence: codex_agents_md.py:319 `line = filename` (bare, no leading `/`); :328-329 appends it; remove_managed_context_files (:358-387) only unlinks the file.
findings.fix: Anchor the pattern (`/AGENTS.md`) and remove that exact line in remove_managed_context_files when the planted file is deleted.

findings.title: ensure_agents_md treats a user-owned EMPTY AGENTS.md as cockpit-managed, overwrites it, and later deletes it
findings.scenario: User keeps an empty AGENTS.md placeholder in their repo; a codex/agy pane spawns → `existing.strip()` is falsy so the user-owned check is skipped, the file is overwritten with the marker cheatsheet, and when the last pane closes remove_managed_context_files (orchestrator.py:2062) unlinks it — the user's file is gone.
findings.evidence: codex_agents_md.py:447 `if existing.strip() and TAKKUB_MARKER not in first: return False, "user-owned"`.
findings.fix: Treat any pre-existing file without the marker as user-owned regardless of content (`if TAKKUB_MARKER not in first:`).

findings.title: resolve_codex_jsonl_for_cwd opens every rollout in the whole store (no day bound, no cache) — 800 files here — and is called on the Qt main thread at resume
findings.scenario: Resume a codex Lead/teammate: spawn_engine.py:527-529 `_resume_uuid_matches_provider_cwd` → resolve_codex_jsonl_for_cwd(cwd, uuid) rglobs sessions/ + archived_sessions/ and read_codex_session_meta() opens + readline()s each rollout until the id matches; ~/.codex/sessions holds 800 rollout-*.jsonl on this machine, so a resume of an older session costs hundreds of file opens on the GUI thread (and the token-meter worker repeats it every 5 s once a session_uuid is known).
findings.evidence: codex_helper.py:134-141 `candidates = base.rglob("rollout-*.jsonl")` / `meta = read_codex_session_meta(path)` per file, unlike resolve_newest_codex_session_for_cwd which walks newest-day-first with a cutoff.
findings.fix: Walk day directories newest-first (reuse the sharded walk) and stop at a not_before cutoff; memoize id→path per process (a rollout's id/cwd never change).

findings.title: _write_json_atomic's `durable=True` branch is never taken
findings.scenario: No caller in src passes durable=True (grep finds the flag only in the docstring), so the opt-in fsync path at config.py:127-128 is dead-by-construction.
findings.evidence: config.py:112 `def _write_json_atomic(path: Path, data: dict, *, durable: bool = False) -> bool:`; config.py:127-128 `if durable:` / `os.fsync(f.fileno())`
findings.fix: Drop the parameter, or pass durable=True from the one writer that needs crash durability (e.g. auto_migrate_boot.py:154).

findings.title: Account pools are never written, so every selector strategy, switch_log and the pool branch of resolve_account_for are unreachable; ProviderAccount.limits is dropped on read
findings.scenario: No code in src calls `AccountPoolRegistry().upsert` (the Accounts & Pools page was removed — accounts_adapter.py:297-299 only shows leftover rows), so `_pool_for` (facade.py:27-34) always returns None and `Sticky/QuotaAware/CooldownFailover` selectors, `selector_for`, `log_switch`, `read_switches` and the `on_account_switch` hop never execute in production. Separately, `_account_to_record` (registry.py:23-26) persists `limits` via asdict but `_record_to_account` (registry.py:29-41) never reads it back, so `AccountLimits.max_concurrent` is silently lost on round-trip; nothing reads it anyway (scheduler's account cap comes from core_v2_settings).
findings.evidence: Grep `AccountPoolRegistry\(\)\.upsert|AccountRegistry\(\)\.upsert` outside core: none (only tests). Grep `max_concurrent|AccountLimits` outside core: only core_v2_settings.py fields. registry.py:30-41 constructor call omits `limits=`.
findings.fix: Delete AccountPool/selector/switch_log code paths or add a real writer; if keeping the registry, round-trip `limits` in `_record_to_account`.

findings.title: NativeBrainAdapter, facade.recall and the brain_read circuit breaker are never used
findings.scenario: NativeBrainAdapter is only exported from core/brain/__init__.py; nothing constructs it. facade.recall (facade.py:60-86) with its dedicated get_breaker('brain_read', 10 failures/20 s) has no caller: context_builder deliberately uses RetrievalEngine directly (context_builder.py:6-13). The breaker policy entry (core/resilience/policy.py:69) documents a path that never executes.
findings.evidence: grep `\brecall\(` in src -> adapter.py:38 (dead), facade.py:75 (RetrievalEngine.recall inside dead facade.recall), context_builder.py:96/124 (RetrievalEngine, not facade).
findings.fix: Delete adapter.py, facade.recall/submit's public surface if unused, the brain_read breaker registration, and tests/test_core_brain_adapter.py + tests/test_core_brain_facade_recall_breaker.py (or wire recall into a real consumer).

findings.title: Global brain bucket (_global.jsonl) is queried on every assign but nothing ever writes to it
findings.scenario: _recall_records runs a second RetrievalEngine(BrainStore(None)).recall(...) per assign and doctor.py:3984 counts BrainStore(None). Every writer (facade.on_pane_done -> submit(candidate, project=project), lines 305-315) appends to the PROJECT file regardless of candidate.scope; no code routes Scope.GLOBAL/USER candidates to the _global bucket store.py:1-4 describes. The global query is therefore always empty (one extra file stat + no records per assign) and doctor's global count is always 0.
findings.evidence: context_builder.py:124-126 `global_recs = RetrievalEngine(BrainStore(None)).recall(` ... `scope=Scope.GLOBAL`; facade.py:93 `manager = MemoryManager(BrainStore(project))` with no scope-based routing.
findings.fix: Route GLOBAL/USER-scoped candidates to BrainStore(None) inside facade.submit (store by scope, not caller project), or remove the global query.

findings.title: gate_budget's retry ceiling multiplier can never change the budget
findings.scenario: facade.build_context_for_assign applies escalate_for_retry first (facade.py:176-178), so any retry_count>0 arrives with size already >= medium (ceiling 8000/12000), while base_budget from budget_tokens_for is clamped to <= 6000 (context_builder.py:38 _BUDGET_CEILING). min(base_budget, ceiling*multiplier) therefore always equals base_budget; the 25 %/2x staging documented at lines 164-171 is unreachable arithmetic.
findings.evidence: context_gate.py:194-197 `if retry_count > 0:` / `multiplier = min(1.0 + retry_count * _RETRY_CEILING_STEP, ...)` / `return min(base_budget, ceiling)` with base_budget <= 6000 < 8000.
findings.fix: Either raise _BUDGET_CEILING / apply the multiplier to base_budget, or delete the retry_count kwarg and its tests.

findings.title: Context trace always saved with sources=() / latency 0 / dedup 0 -> doctor [context] and Settings Knowledge show hollow numbers; the whole context_sources layer is unused
findings.scenario: _save_gate_trace builds ContextTrace(mode=..., sources=(), total_tokens, budget_tokens, dedup_count=0, latency_ms=0.0) on every gated assign, so trace_store/last_context_trace.json never carries per-source counts, real latency or dedup. doctor_section.build_findings (doctor_section.py:54-58) then prints `total=N/budget dedup=0 latency=0ms` with an empty source list every time (`takkub doctor`, settings_knowledge_design.py:230/558). Meanwhile BrainSource/ConversationSource/ResourceSource, collapse_near_duplicates, apply_scope_and_trust, wrap_untrusted_reference, SourceTrace and ContextTrace.render (core/context_sources/base.py, brain_source.py, conversation_source.py, resource_source.py; context_builder.py:275-316) have zero callers: context_builder.build_context reads brain/summary directly (213-264). The 'UNTRUSTED REFERENCE' security framing therefore never runs.
findings.evidence: facade.py:231-237 `trace = context_builder.ContextTrace(` / `mode=f"gated:{task_size}",` / `sources=(),` ... `latency_ms=0.0,`; grep for BrainSource|ConversationSource|ResourceSource|collapse_near_duplicates in src hits only their own definitions.
findings.fix: Either wire build_context through the ContextSource layer (measure latency, fill SourceTrace, run collapse_near_duplicates/apply_scope_and_trust) or delete core/context_sources/{base,brain_source,conversation_source,resource_source}.py's unused parts plus tests/test_core_context_sources.py:24-41 and tests/test_core_context_sources_sources.py:38-236; stop printing latency/dedup in doctor_section until they are real.

findings.title: Three brain ingest adapters (decision notes, knowledge base, role memory) are never called
findings.scenario: from_decision_note_text, knowledge_source.from_knowledge_base_text (knowledge_source.py:30) and role_memory_source.from_role_memory_text/parse_bullets (role_memory_source.py:24,36) have no caller in src; only reflection_source and digest_facts_source are wired via facade.on_pane_done (facade.py:299-315). Existing runtime/sessions decision notes, runtime/knowledge/*.md and role-memory bullets never reach the Second Brain despite the package docstring promising WRAP adapters for them.
findings.evidence: grep `from_decision_note_text|from_knowledge_base_text|from_role_memory_text|parse_bullets` in src -> only the three definition files.
findings.fix: Wire them into on_pane_done/boot backfill, or delete the three modules plus tests/test_core_brain_sources.py:35-125.

findings.title: Thai file-count regex never matches 'N ไฟล์' followed by space/end (\b after ์ fails)
findings.scenario: A Thai Lead assigns 'แก้ 3 ไฟล์ ใน src' or 'แก้ 3 ไฟล์'. `\b(\d+)\s*(?:files?|ไฟล์)\b` requires a word boundary after ์ (U+0E4C), but ์ is not \w (isalnum() False) and neither is the following space/end, so there is no boundary and the count is ignored -> estimated_files=0 -> smaller size/budget than intended. Verified with the project venv: re.search returns None for both strings and matches only 'แก้ 3 ไฟล์ที่'.
findings.evidence: task_complexity.py:118 `_EXPLICIT_FILE_COUNT_RE = re.compile(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:files?|ไฟล์)\b", re.IGNORECASE)`; python check: thai_isalnum False, match_end False, match_space False, match_word True.
findings.fix: Use `(?:files?\b|ไฟล์)` so the trailing \b applies only to the ASCII alternative.

findings.title: Lockless cross-process append to events.log from the guard hook subprocess
findings.scenario: `log_capability_event` runs inside the `takkub _guard` hook subprocess (cli.py:4997 → PermissionEngine.evaluate_shell_command) on every DENIED Bash call, appending to the same `runtime/events.log` the cockpit process appends to, with a plain `open(..., 'a')` and no lock. On Windows two processes appending concurrently can interleave/lose lines; the size-based rotation at line 60-61 (`os.replace` to `.old`) can also fire from the hook process while the cockpit holds the file open, failing with PermissionError (swallowed, line 62-63) or racing the cockpit's own rotation.
findings.evidence: audit.py:75-76 `with open(events_log, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(line + "\n")`; audit.py:60-61 rotation from a subprocess. Docstring lines 7-13 acknowledges it is a fourth copy of the same unlocked pattern.
findings.fix: Route hook-side audit lines through the IPC server (cockpit is the single writer) or use a per-process side file merged by the cockpit; at minimum skip rotation from the hook process.

findings.title: CapabilityRegistry, PluginManager, design_integrations.build_client and the Figma/21st clients have no production callers
findings.scenario: `CapabilityRegistry` (registry.py:46) and `PluginManager` (plugin_manager.py:39) are never instantiated outside core; `build_client` (design_integrations.py:255) is only reached through the dead `CapabilityRegistry.design_integration_client`, so `TwentyFirstClient`, `FigmaClient`, `IntegrationDeniedError` and the permission gate around them never run. The only live client use is `PenpotClient.get_profile` from settings_knowledge_design.py:677, which deliberately bypasses `build_client`.
findings.evidence: Grep `CapabilityRegistry|PluginManager|design_integration_client|build_client\(|FigmaClient\(|TwentyFirstClient\(|IntegrationDeniedError` in src: hits only inside core/capabilities/* (plus settings_knowledge_design.py:677 for PenpotClient).
findings.fix: Delete registry.py, plugin_manager.py, `build_client` + TwentyFirst/Figma clients (keep `detect_storybook`, `integration_config_status`, `optional_design_mcp_status`, `register_twentyfirst_mcp`, `PermissionEngine`, `PenpotClient`) or give `build_client` a real caller (e.g. a `takkub design fetch` command).

findings.title: Every done() writes a 6-file checkpoint and re-parses the whole message history, but no product code ever reads checkpoints
findings.scenario: _on_pane_done_impl always calls CheckpointManager(cs).create, which (checkpoint.py:87-103) writes summary/working-context/tasks/git-state/provider-binding/runtime-state under checkpoints/checkpoint-NNNNN/ and calls store.read_messages (store.py:154-169: loads and json-parses EVERY rotated part) to keep the last 20 messages. The only reader, CheckpointManager.load (checkpoint.py:113), is called solely by resume.build_resume_context (resume.py:51), which has no caller anywhere in src (its own docstring :12-16 says the resume half is not wired). Result: unbounded checkpoint dirs (4 in 40 min for one role on dev: runtime/core/conversations/agent-takkub/conv-agent-takkub-backend/checkpoints) and O(history) CPU under the GIL per done for output nobody consumes.
findings.evidence: facade.py:131 `CheckpointManager(cs).create(project_id, conversation_id)`; checkpoint.py:90 `messages = self._store.read_messages(project_id, conversation_id)[-_WORKING_CONTEXT_TAIL:]`; grep for build_resume_context/render_resume_prompt/CheckpointManager.load finds only resume.py and tests.
findings.fix: Drop the per-done checkpoint (or gate it behind an actually wired resume path) and delete resume.py; if kept, read only the last part's tail. Tests pinned to it: tests/test_core_conversation.py:232-340 (checkpoint + resume tests).

findings.title: on_account_switch is a permanent no-op: the only caller never passes conversation_id
findings.scenario: core/accounts/selector.py:190-192 calls on_account_switch(pool.id, pool.provider_id, prior_id, picked_id, reason=...) without conversation_id, so line 152 `if not v2_conversation_enabled() or conversation_id is None: return` always returns. The 'checkpoint before account switch' feature never fires in a real cooldown failover.
findings.evidence: facade.py:152 `if not v2_conversation_enabled() or conversation_id is None:` / `return`; selector.py:190 `on_account_switch(` / :191 `pool.id, pool.provider_id, prior_id, picked_id, reason="cooldown_failover"`.
findings.fix: Either derive conversation ids from the pool's live panes (conversation_id_for(project, role)) at the call site or delete on_account_switch + tests/test_core_conversation.py:432-520.

findings.title: Byte-offset ingest advances the cursor past a torn trailing line, dropping that record forever
findings.scenario: The ingest thread starts the instant `takkub done` returns (orchestrator.py:7936), while the pane's CLI is still flushing the current turn's JSONL line (tool_result / assistant text). read_new reads to EOF, the incomplete last line fails json.loads and is skipped, but next_cursor is set to the full file size, so the next ingest starts after it and that message is never stored. Same code in codex_adapter.py:153-166, cursor_adapter.py:63-76, gemini_adapter.py:95-123, kimi_adapter.py:60-73.
findings.evidence: claude_adapter.py:47-50 `try: rec = json.loads(line) except json.JSONDecodeError: continue` then :68 `return IngestBatch(source_id, messages, str(size))`.

findings.title: Persisted breaker state stores time.monotonic() values that takkub doctor renders as absolute times and as a live OPEN state
findings.scenario: `open_until`/`last_healthy` are `self._clock()` = `time.monotonic()` (default at line 101), snapshotted to DATA_HOME/resilience/state.json (lines 239-242). `doctor_section.build_findings` (doctor_section.py:76-77) prints `open_until=<monotonic seconds since that machine booted>` and flags WARN for state=open even though every new cockpit process starts CLOSED (module docstring lines 28-31) — a user running `takkub doctor` sees a stale 'figma open' warning with a meaningless number. Also line 101 annotates `clock: callable[[], float]` using the builtin `callable` instead of `typing.Callable` (harmless only because of `from __future__ import annotations`).
findings.evidence: circuit_breaker.py:101 `clock: callable[[], float] = time.monotonic`; :153/:158 `self._open_until = self._clock() + self.cooldown_s`; doctor_section.py:77 `detail += f" open_until={snap['open_until']:.0f}"`.
findings.fix: Persist wall-clock equivalents (e.g. `time.time() + (open_until - monotonic_now)`) or a remaining-seconds field; render OPEN from a snapshot as 'last seen open' info rather than WARN; use `Callable`.

findings.title: Backpressure ladder is non-monotonic: PAUSE_BACKGROUND admits LOW priority that the milder THROTTLE_NEW denies
findings.scenario: `_MIN_PRIORITY_ADMITTED` maps THROTTLE_NEW->NORMAL (denies LOW, BACKGROUND) but the harsher PAUSE_BACKGROUND->LOW (denies only BACKGROUND). A LOW-priority request is refused while the machine is merely warm and accepted once it is overloaded. No production effect today because every caller uses the default Priority.NORMAL (orchestrator.py:3047 passes no priority), which is admitted at every rung except QUEUE.
findings.evidence: backpressure.py:60-65: `THROTTLE_NEW: Priority.NORMAL, PAUSE_BACKGROUND: Priority.LOW`. tests/test_core_scheduling.py:177 `admits(THROTTLE_NEW, Priority.LOW) is False` and :180 `admits(PAUSE_BACKGROUND, Priority.LOW) is True` enshrine the inversion.
findings.fix: Make the table monotonic (PAUSE_BACKGROUND -> Priority.NORMAL or THROTTLE_NEW -> Priority.LOW) and fix the two asserts; or drop the Priority axis entirely since nothing sets it.

Update the resource_governor.py:321-329 comment.

findings.title: Design-tool tokens are written world-readable on macOS (default write_text permissions)
findings.scenario: Settings → Knowledge/Design → save credential (settings_knowledge_design.py:464) or `takkub design integrations enable --token` (cli.py:2011) stores the Figma/Penpot/21st token via `FileSecretBackend.set`, which writes `~/.takkub/secrets/<id>.json` (plus a `.tmp`) with `write_text` — 0644 under the default umask on macOS, readable by every local user; the token is plaintext by design. The CodeQL fix e4fd8f93 restricted venv executables but not this file.
findings.evidence: file_backend.py:36-40: `tmp = self._path.with_name(self._path.name + ".tmp")` / `tmp.write_text(value, encoding="utf-8")` / `os.replace(tmp, self._path)` — no `os.open(..., 0o600)`/`chmod`.
findings.fix: Create the file with `os.open(tmp, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600)` (and `os.chmod` the parent dir 0o700) before writing; on Windows optionally tighten the ACL.

findings.title: Corrupt core-v2-settings.json silently reads as defaults; the next Settings save writes defaults back, erasing the TypeSafe API key / scheduler policy
findings.scenario: File becomes unparsable (partial disk, hand edit). load() swallows the error, caches _default_payload() under the corrupt file's stat key, and every save_* helper does `payload = load(); payload[key] = …; save(payload)` — so a Settings → Usage save of decide_mode rewrites the file with typesafe_api_key='' and an empty scheduler policy. No warning is logged.
findings.evidence: core_v2_settings.py:188-189 `except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError): merged = _default_payload()` · :266-271 `payload = load(); payload["decide_mode"] = value; return save(payload)`
findings.fix: Log a warning with the path on parse failure and archive the corrupt file via config.archive_settings_file before any save overwrites it.

findings.title: cursor_first_user_preview: `if session_uuid == path.parent.name: session_uuid = path.parent.name` is a no-op branch
findings.scenario: The assignment sets the variable to the value it was just compared equal to; the intended case (file named differently from its session directory) is never handled, so a flat `<uuid>.jsonl` vs `<dir>/<other>.jsonl` layout is not normalized.

findings.title: cursor_exec / find_cursor_executable / _default_cursor_paths and opencode_exec have no production caller (tests only)
findings.scenario: Binary discovery for cursor is done by provider_spec._discover_cursor (provider_spec.py:514, own shutil.which loop) and there is no `takkub cursor` / `takkub opencode` one-shot command (cli.py defines only cmd_codex :3579 and cmd_gemini :3606). Only tests/test_cursor_helper.py and tests/test_opencode_helper.py import cursor_exec / opencode_exec, so ~90 lines of subprocess code (cursor_helper.py:62-105, 476-516; opencode_helper.py:637-674) plus their tests are dead weight that still claims 'Backs the cockpit's cursor provider role'.

findings.title: `takkub prune --level review --yes` with no --category implicitly deletes chat-history (user's own ~/.claude/projects on a dev checkout) and orphan-worktrees-review (source code)
findings.scenario: With categories omitted, prune() expands to every category whose rank <= review, which includes `chat-history` (default_claude_config_dir()/projects/**/*.jsonl older than 30 days — on a dev checkout that is the user's personal ~/.claude history for ALL their sessions, not only cockpit panes; breaks /resume) and `orphan-worktrees-review` (checkouts still holding uncommitted/unmerged source). cli.py:1541-1547 passes dry_run=not args.yes, and only orphan-worktrees-review targets are printed (cli.py:1556); chat-history files are deleted without listing them.
findings.evidence: disk_usage.py:1283-1287 `requested = (list(categories) if categories else [c for c in VALID_CATEGORIES if _LEVEL_RANK[_category_level(c)] <= _LEVEL_RANK[level]])`; disk_usage.py:1083 `root = default_claude_config_dir() / "projects"`; disk_usage.py:1275 docstring 'review must be requested explicitly, never implied'
findings.fix: Require an explicit --category whenever level==review (refuse the implicit expansion), and print every chat-history/exports target path before deletion like orphan-worktrees-review already does.

findings.title: prod-profile auth check is file-only, contradicting the Keychain/Credential-Manager handling 100 lines above → false 'not logged in' WARN on installed builds
findings.scenario: Installed cockpit (DATA_HOME != REPO_ROOT). The default-profile branch (l.113-145) reads the macOS Keychain and on Windows treats a missing file as SKIP 'not directly checkable'. The prod-profile branch checks only `_DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR / ".credentials.json"` → on macOS (token in Keychain) and on Windows installs whose token lives in Credential Manager, `takkub doctor` WARNs 'prod Claude profile not logged in yet' for a working login and tells the user to run `claude login` again.
findings.evidence: l.213-214 `prod_creds = _DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR / ".credentials.json"\nif prod_creds.is_file():` vs l.109-111 comment 'macOS keeps the OAuth token in the login Keychain instead … not a file at all'.
findings.fix: Reuse the same platform ladder for the prod profile (Keychain lookup on darwin; SKIP not WARN on win32 when the file is absent).

findings.title: npx baseline grading is dead on Windows: probes bare `npx` instead of the resolved `npx.cmd` path it just found
findings.scenario: `shutil.which("npx")` returns `…\npx.cmd`, but `_run(["npx", "--version"])` passes the bare name; CreateProcess cannot launch a .cmd without its extension, so rc≠0 and `_core_finding` always reports 'present · not probed' (l.432-433). The min/recommended npx version check therefore never runs on Windows by construction.
findings.evidence: l.460-463 `npx = shutil.which("npx")\nif npx:\n    rc, ver = _run(["npx", "--version"])` — same pattern as node (l.450) which only works because node is an .exe.
findings.fix: `_run([npx, "--version"])` (and `_run([node, "--version"])` for symmetry).

findings.title: machine_fanout_cap and MAX_FANOUT have no production callers (docstring-only mention in orchestrator)
findings.scenario: orchestrator uses machine_total_pane_cap() only; the only 'machine_fanout_cap' text in src outside this module is a docstring at orchestrator.py:14727. The module docstring itself says it is 'exercised directly by tests for that reason'.
findings.evidence: exec_mode.py:96 `def machine_fanout_cap() -> int:` · :112 `return max(1, min(MAX_FANOUT, _base_pane_cap()))` · grep `machine_fanout_cap(` in src → only orchestrator.py:14727 docstring
findings.fix: Remove machine_fanout_cap + MAX_FANOUT and the tests that pin them; keep machine_total_pane_cap.

findings.title: Watch is lost after delete-then-recreate (git checkout/stash, safe-write editors) -> later external edits unseen
findings.scenario: File open in the editor; `git checkout <branch>` unlinks and recreates it. Qt drops a deleted path from the watcher; _on_file_changed only re-adds when p.exists() at signal time, so if the recreate lands after the signal the file gets a diskRemoved banner and is never watched again until the tab is closed. Subsequent external edits produce no 'disk changed' banner; the next Ctrl+S hits a surprise conflict dialog instead.
findings.evidence: file_watch_service.py:143-144 `if p.exists() and path not in self._watcher.files(): self._watcher.addPath(path)`; _flush (:148-158) never re-adds a path that exists again.
findings.fix: In _flush, when `p.exists()` and `path not in self._watcher.files()`, call addPath(path) before dispatching the snapshot worker.

findings.title: resolve_agy_project_id sleeps up to 4 s on the Qt main thread when a second gemini spawn hits an unregistered cwd within 60 s
findings.scenario: Spawn a gemini pane into a cwd agy has not yet registered (first spawn claims _MINT_INFLIGHT), then within 60 s restart that Lead or spawn another gemini role into the same cwd before agy has written ~/.gemini/config/projects/<uuid>.json (agy boots 5-10 s): provider_spec.py:491 `_resolve_gemini_project_id` runs inside spawn() on the GUI thread and enters the `time.sleep(0.25)` poll loop for _MINT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SEC=4 s → GUI frozen 4 s, then falls back to --new-project anyway.
findings.evidence: gemini_helper.py:571-579 `if inflight_since is not None and (now - inflight_since) < _MINT_INFLIGHT_TTL_SEC:` / `while time.monotonic() < deadline: time.sleep(_MINT_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC)`; docstring :485-487 states the calls come from the single Qt event loop.
findings.fix: Return None immediately with a `minting` hint and let spawn re-check after boot, or move the poll into the async spawn path; never sleep in spawn().

findings.title: Overlapping _StatusWorker runs have no generation guard — a slow `git status` can deliver a stale CHANGES list after a newer one
findings.scenario: Big repo where `git status --porcelain=v2` takes longer than the 1.5 s debounce while a pane writes files continuously: request_refresh fires _run every 1.5 s, each starting a new _StatusWorker on the global pool; workers serialize on SUBPROCESS_LOCK in no guaranteed order, and every one emits changesChanged when done, so an older result can overwrite a newer list in the panel (and N redundant `git status` runs burn CPU).
findings.evidence: git_changes_service.py:523-533 `request_refresh` → `_timer.start()`; `_run` creates a worker unconditionally; `_on_status_finished` emits whatever arrives with no run-id check.
findings.fix: Stamp each worker with an incrementing `_status_gen` and drop results whose gen < the latest dispatched; skip starting a new worker while one is in flight (set a pending flag and re-run on completion).

findings.title: `git ls-files --cached` keeps worktree-deleted tracked files in the staging mirror (hardlink keeps the old bytes alive)
findings.scenario: A pane deletes a tracked file with plain `rm`/Edit-delete (no `git rm`). The file is still in the index so `--cached` lists it; `_sync_staging` keeps it in `desired` and never unlinks the mirror copy, and because the mirror entry is a hardlink the deleted content stays on disk. graft keeps answering with symbols/callers from a file that no longer exists until the deletion is committed.
findings.evidence:
graft_autobuild.py:331-335 `"ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"`
graft_autobuild.py:471 `if rel not in desired:` (only removes rels absent from git's list)
findings.fix: Drop rels whose source `stat` fails (or add `--deleted` handling: subtract `git ls-files --deleted` from the set) before computing `desired`.

findings.title: done()-triggered rebuild is dropped (not queued) while a build for the same dir is already past its staging sync
findings.scenario: Two roles share a cwd. Role A `takkub done` → 20s debounce → `graft build` starts (minutes on a real repo). Role B edits files and calls done 30s later → its debounce fires → `_build_one` returns at line 614 because the key is still in `_building`; A's build already ran `_sync_staging` (line 566) before B's edits. B's new files are never indexed until a third done() on that dir; `resync_staging_only` (orchestrator.py:12196) only runs for panes in state 'working', so once both panes are idle the graph stays stale and Lead/reviewer get pre-B answers. The docstring's 'picked up on its own next trigger' assumes a trigger that does not exist for idle panes.
findings.evidence:
graft_autobuild.py:612-615 `with _lock: if key in _building: return` 
graft_autobuild.py:566 `_sync_staging(target, rel_paths, staging)` (runs once, before the long Popen)
findings.fix: Record a 'dirty' flag when single-flight rejects a call and re-run `_build_one` once in the `finally` of the in-flight build when the flag is set.

findings.title: iter_store_dirs has no callers (disk_usage uses read_store_manifest with its own directory walk)
findings.scenario: No call site in src/.
findings.evidence: graft_store.py:326 `def iter_store_dirs() -> list[Path]:`
findings.fix: Delete, or make disk_usage.py use it.

findings.title: Headless boot leaves the last saved tab as the active project instead of the persisted active one → `takkub assign/send` without --project and the PWA target the wrong project
findings.scenario: Headless cockpit restarts with tabs [A(active), B, C] saved: boot() opens A then B then C and `_open_project_tab` calls `set_active_project(project_name)` each time, so active ends as C. cli.py:3425/3540 default `args.project or active_project()[0]` and remote/api.py:120 read the same key, so a `takkub assign --role backend ...` typed without --project after the restart lands in project C.
findings.evidence: headless_window.py:101-108 `names = list(dict.fromkeys(([active] if active else []) + saved))` / `for name in names: self._open_project_tab(name)`; 145 `set_active_project(project_name)` unconditionally per tab; no restore after the loop (MainWindow restores via the tab widget's current tab).
findings.fix: After the loop in boot(): `if active and active in self._tabs: set_active_project(active)`.

findings.title: role_wants_concise / role_wants_remote_control are matched on the shard name (qa#1), so shards never get Concise and explicit role lists miss them
findings.scenario: spawn_engine.py:3448 passes role_name ('qa#1', 'qa#2') not base_role. Default roster {'qa'} matches 'qa' only, so a fan-out of the pilot role gets full output style on every shard (the token-diet measurement in #318 is skewed); likewise TAKKUB_CONCISE_ROLES=qa or TAKKUB_REMOTE_CONTROL_ROLES=qa never apply to qa#N.
findings.evidence:
roles = {r.strip() for r in raw.split(",") if r.strip()}
return role_name in (roles or ())
findings.fix: Strip the `#N` suffix before matching (or pass base_role from spawn_engine.py:3448-3449).

findings.title: `_ROLES` tuple is defined but never referenced
findings.scenario: Constant is not used for validation or labels anywhere; role labels are built from the caller-supplied `role` string.
findings.evidence: issues.py:34-44 `_ROLES = ("frontend", … "gemini",)` — no other occurrence of `_ROLES` in issues.py or callers.
