findings.title: `"Could not resolve" in msg.lower()` can never match (mixed-case literal vs lowercased message)
findings.scenario: `gh repo view` fails with 'could not resolve to a Repository' → the friendly 'no GitHub remote found … gh repo create' hint is never produced; the user gets the generic 'cannot detect GitHub repo: …' text instead. No functional impact beyond the message (outer callers catch RuntimeError either way).
findings.evidence: issues.py:164-167 `if ("not a git repository" in msg.lower() or "no git remote" in msg.lower() or "Could not resolve" in msg.lower()):`
findings.fix: Use `"could not resolve" in msg.lower()`.

findings.title: audit_lead_bash / detect_write_intent are dead — no runtime caller, only tests
findings.scenario: Nothing wires this as a hook (hook_wiring.py only installs `takkub _guard`, `_activity`, session-report); the docstring's settings.json snippet was never applied. `tests/test_lead_bash_audit.py` and the conftest monkeypatch at tests/conftest.py:528-530 exercise code that never runs in production. The `r">>?"` pattern (line 56) would also flag every `2>&1`.
findings.evidence: Grep for `audit_lead_bash|lead_bash_audit` in src/ matches only the module itself; other hits are tests/conftest.py:347,528, tests/test_lead_bash_audit.py, pyproject.toml:214 (import-linter list), docs.
findings.fix: Delete the module, its test file, the conftest entry and the pyproject contract line (or actually wire it if Phase 2 is still wanted).

findings.title: Plugin version dirs sorted lexically — '4.10.0' loses to '4.9.0' when a plugin update leaves the old dir
findings.scenario: `claude plugin update` writes `<plugin>/4.10.0/` while `4.9.0/` remains; `sorted(reverse=True)` on strings picks '4.9.0' → panes are spawned with `--plugin-dir` of the stale version. Latent on this machine (one version dir per plugin today).
findings.evidence: lead_context.py:1006 `versions = sorted((v for v in plugin.iterdir() if v.is_dir()), reverse=True)`
findings.fix: Sort with a numeric version key (e.g. `packaging.version` or split-on-dot ints, non-numeric names last).

findings.title: _flush_pending_done_notices re-queues durable items without from_role → adaptive digest window can never shrink for them
findings.scenario: Any done notice that took the durable path (Lead was down/busy) is re-fed through `_notify_lead` with the default `from_role='system'`; `_other_roles_still_active(project_ns, 'system')` then counts the reporting role's own (still 'done'/'working') pane as another active role, so the 3 s adaptive settle (#264) never applies and Lead waits the full 15 s window on every re-flush. `_wait_is_watching_role` still works because it parses the body tag.
findings.evidence: lead_inbox.py:4747-4753 `self._notify_lead(project_ns, item["body"], pane_token=..., queued_ts=..., kind="pending-done-flush")` — `item.get("role")` is dropped; 4336 `if not self._other_roles_still_active(project_ns, from_role):`
findings.fix: Pass `from_role=item.get('role', 'system')` (and `note=item.get('note')`).

findings.title: ref_count is written in five places and never read
findings.scenario: #598 docstring says pops happen 'only when ref_count reaches 0', but every decision uses `if not clients:` — `ref_count` is bookkeeping nobody consumes.
findings.evidence: lead_wait.py:263-265, 286, 303, 796, 841 assign `active["ref_count"]`; grep shows no read anywhere in src.
findings.fix: Delete the field and the docstring claim.

findings.title: _wait_echo_by_id grows without bound (one entry per resolved wait_id, never pruned)
findings.scenario: Every resolved/expired/interrupted `takkub wait` stores its full result dict under its wait_id; nothing removes entries after `_WAIT_RESOLVED_ECHO_GRACE_S`. A cockpit left running for days with an autonomous Lead polling `takkub wait` in every turn accumulates thousands of dicts.
findings.evidence: lead_wait.py:803-805 `if not hasattr(self, "_wait_echo_by_id"): self._wait_echo_by_id = {}` / `self._wait_echo_by_id[wait_id] = ...`; only reader is 706 (`.get(wait_id)`).
findings.fix: Prune entries older than `_WAIT_RESOLVED_ECHO_GRACE_S` when inserting, or use a bounded OrderedDict.

findings.title: After a cockpit restart an already-elapsed quota stall is never cleared or announced (docstring claims re-arm)
findings.scenario: codex quota-hit recorded at 14:00 with reset 19:00; cockpit restarted at 20:00. No reset QTimer exists in the new process, _maybe_reprobe_quota_stalls skips entries with reset_at <= now, and nothing else calls _clear_provider_quota_stall -> provider-quota.json keeps the stale entry forever (until codex hits again), the Lead never gets the 'quota reset แล้ว' notice, and the #663 docstring's 'also re-arms after a cockpit restart' only holds for still-future entries.
findings.evidence: L763-765: `for provider, reset_at in stalls.items():` / `if reset_at <= now: continue`
findings.fix: In _maybe_reprobe_quota_stalls, for reset_at <= now call _clear_provider_quota_stall(project, provider, reason='window_elapsed') (once), or re-arm _schedule_provider_quota_reset_notice for every loaded entry at boot.

findings.title: save_shared_state uses one fixed tmp filename: concurrent writers collide and the 429 backoff is silently not persisted
findings.scenario: LimitStore thread and ProviderUsageStore thread (or prod + dev cockpit sharing one profile dir) both save at once: both write takkub-usage-state.json.tmp; on Windows the second tmp.replace() hits PermissionError while the first still has it open -> swallowed at L508-509 -> that writer's backoff_until/payload is lost -> the other process fires a fresh request and re-arms the endpoint penalty, the exact failure this file exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: L505-507: `tmp = path.with_suffix(".json.tmp")` / `tmp.write_text(...)` / `tmp.replace(path)`   L508-509: `except OSError: _log.debug(...)`
findings.fix: Unique tmp name (pid + thread id / uuid) and a module-level lock around load+merge+write.

findings.title: class Poller is dead code (no caller in src or tests); main_window.py:159 comment still references it
findings.scenario: Poller (L740-833, threading.Timer-based single-profile poller) was superseded by LimitStore; the only mentions are its own docstring (L631) and a stale comment in main_window.py:159. Never instantiated anywhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: L740: `class Poller:`   grep '\bPoller\b' over *.py -> only limit_status.py:631,740 and main_window.py:159 (comment).
findings.fix: Delete the class and fix the main_window comment to say LimitStore.

findings.title: `_EVENT_COLOR` is never referenced (dead)
findings.scenario: n/a — module-level dict built from cockpit_theme tokens at import but no reader anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: Grep for `_EVENT_COLOR` across src/ matches only its definition at logs_panel.py:60-66.
findings.fix: Delete it.

findings.title: LogsPanel polls events.log every second on the main thread even while its dock is hidden (the default)
findings.scenario: events.log grows hundreds of times a minute, so nearly every 1 s tick re-reads 256 KiB, splits lines, json-parses 120 rows and calls setPlainText on a widget nobody sees, for the whole session.
findings.evidence: logs_panel.py:147-152 timer starts in __init__ and :170-214 does the read/parse/render; main_window.py:439-441 constructs the panel and `self._logs_dock.hide()`; only `_on_toggle_logs` (:1178) ever shows it.
findings.fix: Start the timer in showEvent / stop in hideEvent (or gate `_poll` on `self.isVisible()`), and do the initial fill on first show.

findings.title: `_on_project_changed` / hidden `_project_combo` path and `_refresh_rtk_button` stub are dead-by-construction
findings.scenario: n/a — the combo is hidden, `_refresh_project_list` blocks its signals while mutating it, nothing else pokes it, so the slot never runs; `_refresh_rtk_button` is `pass` yet called 4x; `DEFAULT_TEAMMATES` is imported only to be assigned to `_`.
findings.evidence: main_window.py:1331-1339 slot (own comment: 'nothing routes here anymore'); :1318-1329 blockSignals around every mutation; status_header.py:1706-1708 `def _refresh_rtk_button(self): ... pass`; calls at main_window.py:951, :1339, :1537, :1684; :1890-1892 `_ = DEFAULT_TEAMMATES`.
findings.fix: Remove `_on_project_changed`, the `_project_combo` wiring, the `_refresh_rtk_button` stub and its call sites, and the `DEFAULT_TEAMMATES` import.

findings.title: Tab open runs `git ls-files` synchronously on the Qt main thread (15 s timeout) via skill-link repair
findings.scenario: Opening a project tab (manual + or each boot-restored tab) blocks the UI for the duration of a git subprocess; on a slow disk/AV-scanned repo this is a visible stall per tab.
findings.evidence: main_window.py:1450 `skill_scan.migrate_legacy_project_skills(roots[0], project_name)` -> skill_scan.py:280-285 `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ..., "ls-files", ...], timeout=_GIT_LS_TIMEOUT_S)` with `_GIT_LS_TIMEOUT_S = 15` (skill_scan.py:32), called from `_open_project_tab` :1503 before the tab is built.
findings.fix: Run `_ensure_project_skill_links` through `self.cli.run_off_thread` (it only touches the filesystem) and report results to the status bar in the callback.

findings.title: _other_cockpit_events_log's installed-build branch points at <venv>/Lib/runtime/events.log — never exists
findings.scenario: On an installed build config.REPO_ROOT is Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] = <venv>/Lib (config.py:184), so `Path(_REPO_ROOT) / "runtime" / "events.log"` is `<venv>/Lib/runtime/events.log`, which is filtered out by `p.is_file()` (maintenance.py:532, 626). `takkub ma` run from an installed cockpit never pairs with the dev checkout's log, contrary to the docstring's 'mirrors cli._instance_banner's dev/prod pairing'; only the dev→prod direction works.
findings.evidence: maintenance.py:510-514 `other = ((Path.home() / ".agent-takkub" / "runtime" / "events.log") if is_dev else (Path(_REPO_ROOT) / "runtime" / "events.log"))`
findings.fix: Drop the prod→dev branch (return None when not is_dev) or resolve the dev checkout's DATA_HOME the way cli._instance_banner does.

findings.title: mb fallback grant is a lockless read-check-write on a non-atomic file — two shards can both be told 'granted', then one is denied by the hook
findings.scenario: Two browser shards whose Playwright MCP failed run `takkub mcp-fallback request` at nearly the same moment (separate processes, cli.py:5037): both _read_lock() see no holder (or a torn half-written JSON → None at :66-68), both _write_lock() and return granted=True; the last writer owns the file, so the other shard's next `mb` call is denied by pane_guard via is_granted() (cli.py:4877) with no explanation — or, if the guard reads the winner's stale file mid-rewrite, both drive CDP 9222 (#92).
findings.evidence: mcp_fallback.py:85-86 `lock = _read_lock()` / `if lock and lock.get("holder") != role and ...` then :99 `_write_lock({...})`; :74 `_lock_path().write_text(json.dumps(data), ...)` (no tmp+os.replace, no O_EXCL).
findings.fix: Write via tempfile + os.replace and re-read after write to confirm holder == role before returning granted; or take an OS-level lock (msvcrt.locking / fcntl.flock) around request().

findings.title: Dedup index is write-only: lookup/all_records/NoteMetadata.touched are never called, so nothing is ever deduplicated
findings.scenario: `vault_mirror.distill_session_facts` only calls `record_write` (line 809); `lookup` (line 28/90), module `all_records` (102) and `obsidian_metadata.NoteMetadata.touched` (89) have no callers in src/ (doctor uses only `count`). The JSONL under core_store_path('obsidian_dedup') grows one record per distilled fact forever and never prevents a duplicate; the only real dedup is `_append_decision_entry`'s verbatim `entry in text` check (which includes the timestamp, so a re-reported fact at a different second is appended again).
findings.evidence:
obsidian_dedup.py:28 `def lookup(self, knowledge_id: str)` (no callers)
vault_mirror.py:809 `obsidian_dedup.record_write(` (only use)
obsidian_metadata.py:89 `def touched(self, *, now=None)` (no callers)
findings.fix: Either consult `lookup(meta.knowledge_id)` before appending in distill_session_facts (and compute knowledge_id from the fact text without the timestamp) or remove the index + touched() as dead.

findings.title: Fan-out queue (TAKKUB_QUEUE_FANOUT) is default-off dead code; when enabled it drops worktree_prepared/subagent_fanout/base_ref
findings.scenario: `_fanout_queue_enabled()` is false unless the env var is set, so `_should_queue_assign`, `_enqueue_assign`, `_drain_fanout_queue`, `_fanout_queue_path`, `_save_fanout_queue`, `_load_fanout_queue` and the close() drain hook (6380-6381) never execute in production (memory: opt-in features never get used). If someone turns it on, `assign()` at 3187-3208 enqueues without `worktree_prepared` (a worktree cli_server already created off-thread is orphaned; on drain `_assign_with_worktree(prepared=None)` creates a second one inline on the main thread), without `subagent_fanout` (same sequential downgrade as the governor closure) and without `base_ref`/`team`.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:1036 `return os.environ.get("TAKKUB_QUEUE_FANOUT", "").strip().lower() not in (`; orchestrator.py:3192-3208 `return self._enqueue_assign(role_name, cwd, task, ... distinct_from, scope=resolved_scope,)` (no worktree_prepared/subagent_fanout/base_ref); orchestrator.py:14890-14906 `self.assign(item["role"], item["cwd"], item["task"], ...)`
findings.fix: Either delete the six methods + `_fanout_queue` state + close() hook + `docs/reviews/2026-06-30-queue-gap.md` reference, or make it real: default-on, carry the full assign kwargs (incl. worktree_prepared/subagent_fanout/base_ref) in the queued item.

findings.title: assign() creates PaneState via _ps() before validation; rejected/subagent assigns leave ghost state that steers resolve_pane_role
findings.scenario: `takkub assign --role qa --provider bogus` (rejected at 3003) or `--role reviewer --mode subagent` (no pane ever) still executes `self._ps(_exit_key(project, role))`, which get-or-creates `_pane_state["proj::qa"]`. Later `takkub send --to reviewer` / `takkub close --role reviewer` with no live pane hits resolve_pane_role's `_pane_state` fallback (2256-2259) and resolves to the ghost role, and `_queued_resource_roles`/status paths that iterate `_pane_state` see a role that never existed. spawn_engine.py:1471 documents `_ps` is create-on-read and read-only callers must use `.get`.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:2886 `_fo_ps = self._ps(_exit_key(role_check_project_ns, role_name))`; orchestrator.py:2256-2259 `key = _exit_key(project_ns, c)` / `if key in self._pane_state:` / `return c`; spawn_engine.py:1471-1472 "Callers that only need to *read* without creating an entry should use ``self._pane_state.get(key)``"
findings.fix: Read with `self._pane_state.get(key)` for the `subagent_fanout` comparison and only call `_ps()` inside the `subagent_fanout > 1` / clear branches after mode/provider/model validation has passed (move the block below line 3023).

findings.title: decide.scope() runs 2-3 times per assign (cli, orchestrator, routing_planner.classify) → duplicate paid Jev probes and log rows in shadow/on mode
findings.scenario: Operator enables `TAKKUB_DECIDE_MODE=shadow` (or on). One `takkub assign`: cli.py:776 asks Jev in the CLI process, orchestrator.py:2946 calls `decide.scope(task)` unconditionally even when a concrete `--scope` was already shipped, and (preset=auto) orchestrator.py:2840 `suggest_team_size` → `routing_planner.classify` → decide.py:1098 `decide.scope` asks a third time. Spend meter (`typesafe_bridge.stats`) and `decide_shadow` disagreement rows are inflated ~3x per assign.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:2946 `auto_scope = decide.scope(task).scope` (before the `if requested_scope == "auto"` branch); routing_planner.py:1098 `scope_dec = decide.scope(user_message)`; cli.py:776 `auto_decision = decide.scope(task_text)`.
findings.fix: In `assign`, call `task_scope.classify` for the audit metric when `requested_scope != "auto"` and only `decide.scope` when it is auto; let `routing_planner.classify` accept a precomputed ScopeDecision (or use `task_scope.classify` there).

findings.title: _dispatch_next_assignment tells Lead "forwarded when pane ready" when the item was actually re-queued
findings.scenario: done()/idle-drain pops the queued item and calls `_assign_dispatch(**item)`; if the pane reads busy at that instant, `_assign_dispatch` re-inserts the item at position 0 and returns `(True, "... queued after current task")` (3607-3617). The caller only checks `ok`, so Lead receives "[queued-assignment] backend: task abcd1234 forwarded when pane ready" although nothing was forwarded; the real state is only visible in events.log.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:3487-3493 `ok, message = self._assign_dispatch(**item)` … `+ ("forwarded when pane ready" if ok else f"retained; dispatch failed: {message}")`; orchestrator.py:3614-3617 `bucket.insert(0, pending_item)` / `return True, f"{role_name}: task {pending_id[:8]} queued after current task"`
findings.fix: Have `_assign_dispatch` return a distinguishable status (e.g. third tuple element or message prefix) for the re-queue branch and word the notice accordingly, or suppress the notice when the popped item is still at bucket[0] after the call.

findings.title: Idle provider/cwd-switch respawn releases the governor slot and the replacement pane spawns uncapped
findings.scenario: qa (browser class) is idle; Lead re-assigns it with `--provider codex`. `_assign_dispatch` calls `close(..., keep_queue=True)`, which pops+releases the (project, role) ResourceToken (close() 6168-6171), then 2 s later calls `_assign_dispatch` directly — only `assign()` ever calls `governor.request_slot`, so the replacement pane never re-acquires a token. The browser/heavy per-class cap now under-counts by one; a second browser pane can be admitted concurrently, and on that pane's later close `release_slot(None)` is a no-op. Same shape in `_reroute_pane_to_provider` (limit_autoresume.py:608-618).
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:3752-3758 `self.close(role_name, project=project_ns, suppress_pipeline=True, suppress_auto_chain=True, keep_queue=True)`; orchestrator.py:3759-3761 `QTimer.singleShot(2_000, lambda: self._assign_dispatch(`; orchestrator.py:6168-6171 `resource_token = getattr(self, "_resource_tokens", {}).pop((project_ns, role_name), None)` / `resource_governor.release_slot(resource_token)`
findings.fix: Either keep the token across a recovery close (skip the pop when `recovery_close`) or re-enter through `assign(..., _resource_token=None)` so the replacement requests a slot.

findings.title: Worktree pre-trust resolves the provider from the bare qa/critic row instead of settings_role_for (reviewer row)
findings.scenario: `takkub assign --role reviewer --mode e2e --isolation worktree` (→ qa). `_assign_dispatch` spawns on `effective_provider_for(settings_role_for("qa"))` = the reviewer row (claude). `_assign_with_worktree` decides pre-trust with `effective_provider_for(role_name)` = the stale qa row in role-models.json (e.g. codex, the #590 "invisible qa/critic entry" case), so `pre_trust_worktrees_root` is skipped; the claude pane opens in a never-seen worktree, the folder-trust dialog's auto-answer gives up after 90 s and the task is never delivered (#444 regression). Also ignores a watchdog `ps.provider_override`.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:4507-4513 `resolved_provider = (provider or "").strip() or effective_provider_for(role_name, project=project_ns)` / `if resolved_provider == CLAUDE: ... pre_trust_worktrees_root(project_ns)`; orchestrator.py:3628 `settings_role_a = _team_preset_a.settings_role_for(base_role_a, project_ns)`; orchestrator.py:3792 `effective_provider = ps_assign.provider_override or effective_provider_for(settings_role_a, ...)`
findings.fix: Resolve exactly as `_assign_dispatch` does: `ps.provider_override or effective_provider_for(team_preset.settings_role_for(base_role, project_ns), project=project_ns)`; better, move the pre-trust into `_assign_dispatch` right before spawn where `effective_provider` is already final.

findings.title: `_reap_role_messages` tells Lead 'ส่งซ้ำให้แล้ว N ข้อความ' using len(pending) even when items were abandoned (empty body / replay cap) and nothing was replayed
findings.scenario: A role's pending record hits `MAX_REPLAYS` (5652) or has an empty body (5649) → marked abandoned, no `_send_when_ready`. The notice after the loop still reports `len(pending)` replayed, so Lead believes the message reached the respawned pane and waits for a reply that never comes.
findings.evidence:
5652-5656: `if int(rec.get("replays", 0)) + 1 > role_messages.MAX_REPLAYS: … mark_abandoned … continue`
5673: `f"ตรวจได้ด้วย… ส่งซ้ำให้แล้ว {len(pending)} ข้อความ "`
findings.fix: Count actual replays in a local counter and skip the notice when it is 0; mention abandoned count separately.

findings.title: `kill_pane_children` sort key calls `c.parents()` after `is_running()` without try/except → psutil.NoSuchProcess escapes if a child exits between the two calls, killing nothing
findings.scenario: Lead runs `takkub kill --role devops` on a build tree whose short-lived helper (e.g. a `cmd.exe` shim) exits mid-sort. `sorted(...)` raises NoSuchProcess from `Process.parent()`/`ppid()` on Windows; the exception propagates out of the method (only the per-child loop at 5728 is guarded), cli_server's generic catch returns an error string and no process is killed — Lead has to retry.
findings.evidence: 5723: `for child in sorted(children, key=lambda c: -len(c.parents()) if c.is_running() else 0):`
findings.fix: Wrap the key in a helper that returns 0 on `psutil.Error`, or sort by a pre-collected `(pid, depth)` computed inside try/except.

findings.title: `_child_scan_cache` is keyed by PID, never evicted on close, and Windows reuses PIDs → a new pane can be served the previous process's stale child list; dict grows for the cockpit's lifetime
findings.scenario: Pane A (pid 4212) closes with an entry in `_child_scan_cache`. Hours later a new pane gets pid 4212 (Windows PID reuse is aggressive). First non-sync probe hits `hit is not None`, age > TTL → returns `list(hit[1])` (dead psutil.Process objects whose `.name()` is cached on Windows) while a bg refresh runs, so `_idle_no_progress_real_activity` (9684) reports 'live child process(es)' and suppresses the idle notice for that tick. No writer ever pops entries.
findings.evidence:
5783-5785: `hit = cache.get(pid)` … `return list(hit[1])`
5803: `return list(hit[1])` (stale hand-back while refresh in flight)
findings.fix: Pop `cache[pid]`/`inflight` in close() and `_on_session_exit`, and key the cache on `(pid, session_generation)` or the session object id.

findings.title: `_find_evidence_files` materialises the whole `rglob('*')` tree before applying the node_modules/vendor exclusion → done() walks tens of thousands of entries on the Qt thread
findings.scenario: #500/#567 already documents a pane that npm-installed playwright inside the exports scratch dir. `list(directory.rglob("*"))` (6774) lists every file under node_modules first; the `_EVIDENCE_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES` check (6780) only skips them afterwards. done() calls this up to 4× (6846, 6857, 6955, 6965) synchronously, so each such done() stalls the cockpit for seconds and stats every file.
findings.evidence:
6774: `candidates = list(directory.rglob("*")) if directory.is_dir() else []`
6780: `if _EVIDENCE_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES.intersection(path.parent.parts): continue`
findings.fix: Walk with `os.walk` and prune excluded dir names in place (`dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in _EVIDENCE_EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES]`), or cap the walk.

findings.title: Evidence scan/dedup use done-time date while the pane writes to the spawn-time `TAKKUB_ARTIFACTS_DIR` → screenshots taken after midnight are invisible to done()
findings.scenario: qa pane spawned 23:50 gets `TAKKUB_ARTIFACTS_DIR=…/exports/2026-09-22/<proj>` (pane_env.py:359-365, computed once at spawn). It finishes at 00:10 and done() scans `RUNTIME_DIR/exports/<today=2026-09-23>/<proj>` (6843-6844, 6943-6944) → no evidence found → note gets `⚠ no evidence cited`, `ui_evidence_gate`/dedup gates see nothing, and `_compute_last_progress_ts` (9607-9608) misses the screenshots dir mtime.
findings.evidence:
6843-6844: `today = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` / `artifacts_dir = RUNTIME_DIR / "exports" / today / project_ns`
pane_env.py:359-360: `today = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` / `artifacts_dir = config.RUNTIME_DIR / "exports" / today / project_ns`
findings.fix: Store the artifacts dir actually handed to the pane on PaneState at spawn (or derive from `assign_ts`'s date) and scan that, not `datetime.now()` at done time.

findings.title: `_language_nudge_suffix` never nudges when task_id is None (`seen.get(key) == None` is True on first call)
findings.scenario: A hand-driven pane (`takkub spawn` then typed instructions) or any PaneState without `task_id` calls `takkub done`/`progress` in English while the team language is Thai. `seen.get(key)` returns None for an unseen key and `task_id` is None → equal → returns "" — the #621 nudge is silently disabled for exactly the panes with no bookkeeping.
findings.evidence: 7615: `if seen.get(key) == task_id:` / `return ""`
findings.fix: Use a sentinel: `if key in seen and seen[key] == task_id`.

findings.title: `_pending_notice_roles` reads only the in-memory `_recent_done` (never snapshotted) → after a cockpit restart, roles whose done report is in the durable `_pending_done_notices` store vanish from `takkub list`
findings.scenario: backend reports done while Lead is holding a draft; the notice is parked durably. Cockpit restarts (crash / `takkub restart`). `_recent_done` is initialised empty (1979) and only appended by done()/subagent paths (2649, 8554) — no snapshot/restore path touches it — so the #163 'done (report queued…)' row is never produced although the report is still pending in `_pending_done_notices`.
findings.evidence:
1979: `self._recent_done: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []`
9230: `for done_ns, done_role, _fname in getattr(self, "_recent_done", ()):`
findings.fix: Also iterate `_pending_done_notices[project_ns]` roles (already durable) in `_pending_notice_roles`, or persist `_recent_done` in `write_session_snapshot`.

findings.title: Snapshot writes session_uuid but restore_teammates never reads it — restored panes always cold-boot and get the whole task re-pasted
findings.scenario: Cockpit restart (npm update / Restart button) with a teammate mid-task. `_collect_pane_snapshot_data` persists `session_uuid` '(#9) … so restore_teammates can … resume the session', but `restore_teammates` (11556-11716) only reads role/cwd/last_task/worktree fields; `_recent_exits` is stamped without a uuid, so `spawn()` cannot resume and 11673 `_send_when_ready(role, last_task)` re-runs the task from step 1 in a blank session. The docstring at 11562-11565 concedes 'session_uuid has no value for these roles yet'. Grep confirms no other reader of the snapshot's `session_uuid` key.
findings.evidence:
orchestrator.py:11472 `"session_uuid": ((ps_snap.session_uuid if ps_snap else None) or ""),` (written)
orchestrator.py:11598-11599 `self._recent_exits[_exit_key(project, role)] = {"cwd": cwd, "ts": time.time()}` / `ok, _ = self.spawn(role, cwd=cwd, project=project)` (uuid never consulted)
findings.fix: Either restore `self._ps(key).session_uuid = entry.get("session_uuid")` before spawn (and send `_STUCK_RESUME_NUDGE` instead of the full task when `last_spawn_resumed`), or delete the field from the snapshot and the misleading comments.

findings.title: _venv_incident_notified is never cleared after a successful repair — a second python.exe clobber is repaired silently with no Lead notice
findings.scenario: The #341/#696 incident happened twice in one day. First clobber: repair OK, key `<path>::ok` added, Lead told. Hours later a pane clobbers `venv/Scripts/python.exe` again: `find_problems` reports it, `repair` succeeds, but `key in notified` → `continue` at 12070-12071, so Lead never learns that panes' `takkub done` calls failed in that window and should be re-run (the notice text at 12074-12077 exists precisely for that).
findings.evidence: orchestrator.py:12069-12072 `key = f"{path}::{'ok' if ok else 'fail'}"` / `if key in notified: continue` / `notified.add(key)`
findings.fix: Clear `_venv_incident_notified` (or drop the `::ok` key) in the `if not problems: if was_broken:` healthy-again branch at 12048-12052 so each new clobber episode notifies once.

findings.title: getattr(pane, "provider", None) is always None — AgentPane has no such attribute — so provider-specific feedback-prompt gating/skip-key are dead and the generic regex path is always used
findings.scenario: `_check_feedback_prompts` (13565), `_check_stale_markers` (12723) and `_check_stuck_panes` (14120, 14133) all read `pane.provider`/`pane._provider`. Neither exists (the only provider attribute is `pane.model.provider_name`, agent_pane_model.py:155; grep of *pane*.py finds no `provider` property). `is_at_feedback_prompt(None)` therefore skips `auto_skip_feedback_for()` and `feedback_prompt_markers_for()` and falls to the hard-coded agy regexes (pty_session.py:327-334); `feedback_prompt_skip_key_for(None)` always yields the default '0\r'. It works for agy by coincidence; `ProviderSpec.auto_skip_feedback` / `feedback_prompt_skip_key` (provider_spec.py:461-462) can never take effect for any provider, and the logged `provider=None` in `feedback_prompt_auto_skipped` events is useless.
findings.evidence:
orchestrator.py:13565 `provider = getattr(pane, "provider", None) or getattr(pane, "_provider", None)`
orchestrator.py:14133-14134 `_provider = getattr(pane, "provider", None)` / `skip_key = feedback_prompt_skip_key_for(_provider) or "0\r"`
findings.fix: Resolve the provider like the other watchdogs: `effective_provider_for(role, project=project_name)` (falling back to `pane.model.provider_name`), and pass that to `is_at_feedback_prompt` / `feedback_prompt_skip_key_for`.

findings.title: Pane-header × closes by role name in the projects.json active project instead of the pane's own project (project_ns computed then dropped)
findings.scenario: Two project tabs open. `_on_pane_close_clicked` derives `project_ns` from the emitting pane via `_project_ns_for_pane` (15417) and uses it for the confirm dialog, then calls `self.close(role_name)` with no project → `close()` → `_resolve_project(None)` → `active_project()` from projects.json. If that record lags the displayed tab (the stale-active class fixed for tab removal in 2.1.27 but not for every switch path), the click closes the same-named role in the other project, or no-ops while the pane the user clicked stays open. The tab-bar × path (main_window.py:555-559) passes `project=project` correctly.
findings.evidence:
orchestrator.py:15417-15422 `project_ns = self._project_ns_for_pane(pane) if pane is not None else None` … `self.close(role_name)`
main_window.py:559 `self.orch.close(role, project=project)`
findings.fix: `self.close(role_name, project=project_ns)`.

findings.title: tiny-scope screenshot bypass counts untracked new style/text files as 0 lines
findings.scenario: scope=tiny, pane creates a new 400-line .css/.md file (untracked) and touches nothing else. touched_files = that path (style/text OK) but `git diff --numstat HEAD` never lists untracked files -> filtered_numstat empty -> total_lines 0 <= 20 -> is_tiny True -> the UI screenshot gate is skipped regardless of size.
findings.evidence: orchestrator_text.py:291-296 `filtered_numstat = [... for added, deleted, path in numstat if path... in norm_touched]; total_lines = sum(...)`; :302 `return total_lines <= 20`
findings.fix: If any touched file is absent from numstat (untracked/new), treat the diff as not tiny, or count its lines via `git diff --numstat --no-index /dev/null <file>`.

findings.title: Profile/home injection helpers swallow every exception with bare `pass`, so a pane can silently spawn against ~/.claude or the OS-wide provider home
findings.scenario: inject_user_profile_env (523-528), inject_curated_claude_config_dir (543-547), inject_provider_home_env (651-654, 658-665): any failure (corrupt profiles.json, link creation failing on a locked dir, provider_config_dir_for raising) leaves CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME / XDG_* unset with no log line. On a prod cockpit the pane then reads the user's personal ~/.claude (different login, all global skills, wrong transcript store so the remote mirror shows nothing) and the operator sees 'why is this pane logged in as someone else / why does it have every skill' with nothing in events.log.
findings.evidence:
except Exception:
    pass
findings.fix: Replace `pass` with _log.exception(...) plus a `provider_capability_fallback`-style _log_event so doctor/events.log show the degradation.

findings.title: _ensure_opencode_no_autoupdate_config rebuilds opencode.json from {} when the existing file is unreadable or unparseable, wiping the seeded OpenCode config
findings.scenario: Prod build with an isolated opencode home seeded from the user's real ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (providers, keybinds, MCP servers). On a later opencode spawn, if read_text raises OSError (file momentarily locked on Windows) or json.loads raises (user added a JSONC comment/trailing comma, which OpenCode tolerates), the code swallows it, sets data = {}, and write_text's `{"autoupdate": false}` over the file — every other setting is gone. The write is also non-atomic (write_text), so a crash mid-write truncates it.
findings.fix: On OSError/ValueError skip the write (log and leave the file alone); write via tmp + os.replace.

findings.title: Instance-guard 30 s caches are dead-by-construction (one-shot hook process) and evaluate_instance_guard runs twice per Bash call
findings.scenario: Every candidate Bash call (any `>`/`2>&1`/`.md` mention — `_CANDIDATE_MUTATE_RE` line 2964) re-scans tempdir, TCP-probes each port file and imports psutil in a fresh `takkub _guard` subprocess; the #658 comment about 'the Qt main thread (1.5 s captured)' describes a caller that no longer exists. cli.py:4943 calls `evaluate_instance_guard` and then `classify()` line 4035 calls it again for the same command → double probe cost per call.
findings.evidence: line 2307-2313 module globals + `_CACHE_TTL_S = 30.0`; line 2376 `clear_instance_guard_cache` has zero callers (grep). Only callers of the guard functions outside pane_guard.py are cli.py:4916-4943 (hook subprocess, hook_wiring.py:42 `GUARD_COMMAND = "takkub _guard"`).
findings.fix: Drop the module-level caches and `clear_instance_guard_cache`, and have `classify()` skip `evaluate_instance_guard` when the caller already ran it (pass a flag), or persist the probe result on disk with the TTL.

findings.title: from_dict / validate / PerformanceSettings.to_dict have no production callers since #515 (load() derives from preset())
findings.scenario: grep across src (excluding this module) finds no from_dict/to_dict/validate use for performance settings; load() now returns preset(get_mode()) so the parsing path is test-only.
findings.evidence: performance_settings.py:166 `def from_dict(payload: dict) -> PerformanceSettings:` · :225-229 `def load(...): return preset(get_mode(settings_path))` · grep `performance_settings.(from_dict|validate|to_dict)` in src → no hits
findings.fix: Delete from_dict/validate/to_dict and their tests, or keep validate only if a future UI re-exposes numeric fields.

findings.title: `with_providers` / `provider_disabled_targets` have no production caller (kept only for tests)
findings.scenario: Docstring says the consuming dialog (`pipeline_dialog`) was removed 2026-07-10; grep of src finds no caller of either function.
findings.evidence: pipeline_config.py:358 `def with_providers(` and :370 `def provider_disabled_targets(`; module docstring lines 10-14 admit 'used by the old standalone Pipeline-Settings dialog … removed'.
findings.fix: Delete both functions and their tests, or move to the settings page bridge that actually needs them.

findings.title: list_marketplaces has no callers
findings.scenario: settings_management/repositories/plugins.py uses list_installed and install_by_id only; nothing calls `claude plugin marketplace list --json`.
findings.evidence: plugin_installer.py:306 `def list_marketplaces(timeout: float = 30.0) -> list[dict] | None:`
findings.fix: Delete.

findings.title: Dead API: set_device / set_approved / check_navigation have no callers; nav_block_counts is always 0
findings.scenario: `takkub preview` only supports open-url/open-file/close/status (orchestrator.py:10419-10437); PreviewHost calls the pure navigation_allowed directly, never controller.check_navigation. So `_nav_block_counts` is never incremented and the `takkub doctor --workspace` row read at orchestrator.py:10334 always reports 0 blocks while the widget is actually blocking; PreviewState.approved can never become True; the toolbar device switch never reaches the controller so `takkub preview status` reports the open-time device.
findings.evidence: preview_controller.py:199 `def check_navigation(...)`, :236 `def set_device(...)`, :244 `def set_approved(...)` — grep across src finds no callers outside preview_controller.py; preview_widget.py:63 imports `navigation_allowed as _controller_navigation_allowed` and calls it directly (:379).
findings.fix: Either route PreviewHost.navigation_allowed through controller.check_navigation (so doctor's count is real) and add device/approve actions to preview_command, or delete the three methods and the counter (and the doctor row).

findings.title: _repaint_badges resolves every tree item on the Qt main thread (Path.resolve under RESOLVE_LOCK) on every git status refresh
findings.scenario: Expand a few thousand rows in the Explorer. Every `statusChanged` (fired after each directory listing and after every editor save via gitRefreshNeeded, debounced 1.5s) recurses the whole tree calling `_apply_badge` → `_safe_resolve(Path(path_str))` = one GetFinalPathNameByHandle syscall per row, on the main thread, while contending for RESOLVE_LOCK with listing workers. Hundreds of ms of stall per refresh with a large expanded tree; the same lock the comment at project_file_index.py:52-57 says must only be held for 'one fast stat'.
findings.evidence:
project_explorer.py:292-293 `self._apply_badge(item)` / `self._repaint_badges(item)`
project_explorer.py:422 `rel = _safe_resolve(Path(path_str)).relative_to(...)`
findings.fix: Store the pre-computed repo-relative key on each item at creation (paths came from a resolved listing already) and skip resolve() in _apply_badge.

findings.title: `if claude is None` branch is unreachable (find_claude_executable raises) and generate_project_rules() blocking wrapper has no callers
findings.scenario: config.find_claude_executable never returns None — it raises RuntimeError at config.py:1329 — so the None check and its message never fire (the RuntimeError text shown to the user is config's, not this one). project_wizard.py:41-43 uses generate_project_rules_proc + collect_result; the blocking `generate_project_rules` at line 92 is unused.
findings.evidence:
project_rules.py:46 `if claude is None:` `raise RuntimeError("claude binary not found — ...")`
config.py:1329 `raise RuntimeError("Could not locate claude CLI. ...")`
project_rules.py:92 `def generate_project_rules(prompt: str, project_name: str) -> str:`
findings.fix: Remove the None branch and the blocking wrapper.

findings.title: Dead guard in _seed_opencode: dest_data.exists() is always False from the only caller
findings.scenario: ensure_provider_home returns False at line 285-286 whenever dest_data exists, so _seed_opencode's `dest_data.exists() and src_data.resolve() == dest_data.resolve()` branch can never be taken; the resolve() calls are wasted and the intent (refuse to seed from itself) is not actually enforced when src == dest but dest is absent (it then mkdirs a .partial next to a non-existent dir and copies nothing).
findings.evidence:
if src_data is not None and dest_data.exists() and src_data.resolve() == dest_data.resolve():
    return False
findings.fix: Drop the dest_data.exists() term (compare resolved parents / strings as _seed_codex does) or delete the branch.

findings.title: effective_provider_for reads the quota-reset file uncached (exists+read_text) on every watchdog tick per pane, despite the module note that TTL-cached this exact path for stalls
findings.scenario: orchestrator._check_stuck_tool_panes (L14309) and _check_idle_teammates (L12380) call effective_provider_for(role, project) for every working non-claude pane on the 5s tick. Since #572 that path ends in provider_state.is_quota_ready -> load_quota_resets (provider_state.py:142-146: `path.exists()` + `path.read_text` + json.loads, no cached_read); pick_substitute_provider (L480) repeats it per ring candidate. The comment block at L365-377 documents that this call chain was the root cause of main_thread_stall events and caches only the PATH probe, so the newer quota read re-introduces uncached per-pane-per-tick disk I/O on the Qt main thread (0.7-2s each on the wedged-disk condition it cites).
findings.evidence: provider_config.py:530 `if provider_state.is_quota_ready(desired):`; provider_state.py:143-146 `if not path.exists(): return {}` / `data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`; provider_config.py:372-373 `... fully uncached, directly on the Qt main thread ... Confirmed root cause of recurring `main_thread_stall``
findings.fix: Make provider_state.load_quota_resets use cached_read.read_cached(quota_path(), json.loads, missing={}) and invalidate in its writer (L164-165 tmp.replace) — or cache is_quota_ready per provider with the same 15s TTL used for the CLI probe.

findings.title: lead_capability_gap() has no production caller (docstring claims Settings UI + remote API use it)
findings.scenario: Settings uses lead_capability_gap_for_provider (settings_management/pages/roles_page.py:263) and remote/api.py:834 uses lead_missing_capability; lead_capability_gap itself is referenced only by tests/test_provider_config.py:746-768.
findings.evidence: provider_config.py:912 `def lead_capability_gap(project: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, list[str]] | None:`; provider_config.py:917-918 `Used by the Settings UI (capability-warning badge on the Lead row) and the remote API`
findings.fix: Delete lead_capability_gap and its tests, or have the Lead-row badge actually call it.

findings.title: provider_models.all_models() has no production caller
findings.scenario: Referenced only by tests/test_provider_models.py:41-78; every runtime consumer uses model_for/set_model/clear_model/path (settings_window.py:515/1579/2152/3090, settings_management/repositories/providers.py:78/186/188).
findings.evidence: provider_models.py:99 `def all_models() -> dict[str, str]:`
findings.fix: Delete all_models() and its test assertions (replace with _load() in tests), or leave as documented test seam.

findings.title: is_ready_marker_calibrated() is test-only; its own docstring says no spawn-time warning is wired
findings.scenario: Only tests/test_auth_failure_detection.py:415-426 call it; orchestrator uses uncalibrated_providers() instead (orchestrator.py:9987). The spawn-time Lead warning the docstring defers ('whoever wires that follow-up should call this') was never wired, so a cursor pane (empty ready_rules) still silently stalls delivery until the busy-wait ceiling.
findings.evidence: provider_spec.py:1940 `def is_ready_marker_calibrated(provider: str) -> bool:`; provider_spec.py:1934-1936 `no spawn-time Lead warning is wired to it yet`
findings.fix: Either call it in spawn_engine/lead_inbox to emit a one-shot Lead notice for an uncalibrated provider at spawn, or delete it and keep uncalibrated_providers().

findings.title: eligible_providers(), _TERMINAL_STATUSES and UpdateOutcome.ok are dead in production
findings.scenario: boot_flow.py (the only production consumer) calls provider_update.eligibility_gap/update_provider/STATUS_* directly; eligible_providers() is referenced only by tests/test_provider_update.py:59. _TERMINAL_STATUSES (L120) has no reference anywhere in src/ or tests/. UpdateOutcome.ok (L152) is never read (every `.ok` hit in src is MigrationOutcome/StepReport; test_provider_update.py has no `.ok`).
findings.evidence: provider_update.py:203 `def eligible_providers() -> list[str]:`; provider_update.py:120 `_TERMINAL_STATUSES = frozenset(`; provider_update.py:152-154 `@property def ok(self) -> bool:`
findings.fix: Delete eligible_providers, _TERMINAL_STATUSES and UpdateOutcome.ok (and the test for eligible_providers), or wire boot_flow to eligible_providers if the docstring's 'Callers MUST have already filtered through eligible_providers()' is meant to hold.

findings.title: gemini cache discovery stat()s outside try: a file replaced between glob and stat turns the whole card into 'unexpected error' for 5 min
findings.scenario: Antigravity rewrites its quota cache (delete+create). fetch_gemini_usage globs candidates, then `p.stat()` in the sort key raises FileNotFoundError; only fetch_provider_usage's catch-all (L1420-1422) catches it -> ProviderUsage(error, 'unexpected error') until the next 300 s poll, and the live RPC path is never attempted that cycle.
findings.evidence: L992: `candidates.sort(key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True)`
findings.fix: Stat each candidate inside try/except OSError and drop missing ones before sorting.

findings.title: 2-second status-bar tick does uncached filesystem work on the Qt main thread (codex home glob/resolve + per-project profile read)
findings.scenario: status_header._status_timer (setInterval 2000, status_header.py:651) -> _refresh_active_provider_usage (limit_panel.py:126) -> config_dir_for -> user_profile.profile_for -> path.read_text (user_profile.py:402, NOT cached unlike the #658-cached registry) and _refresh_limit_label -> get_all_account_usages -> codex_usage_targets(): Path.home().glob('.codex*'), is_dir/is_file per home, .resolve() per candidate (provider_usage.py:1260, 1284-1289), every 2 s. On the wedged-disk case #658 measured (781 ms/read) this is a periodic GUI stall (the 'Lead พิมพ์ช้า' symptom).
findings.evidence: L1492: `targets = codex_usage_targets()` (inside get_all_account_usages, called from limit_panel.py:95 on every tick)   L1284: `homes = sorted(Path.home().glob(".codex*"), ...)`   limit_panel.py:136: `data = store.get(user_profile.config_dir_for(project))`
findings.fix: Memoize codex_usage_targets() with a short TTL / stat-validated cache and route profile_for through cached_read like _load_registry.

findings.title: Full-gate lock is per-DATA_HOME, not machine-wide as documented — dev and prod cockpits can run full gates concurrently
findings.scenario: User runs the dev cockpit and the installed prod cockpit at once (two DATA_HOMEs). A full `takkub qa-gate` from a pane of each resolves a different `RUNTIME_DIR/locks/qa-gate-full`, so both acquire slot-0 and run simultaneously — exactly the CPU pile-up #472 introduced the lock to stop; `_active_full_gate_count` also cannot see the other instance, so the #472 contention retry never triggers.
findings.evidence: l.648-652 docstring '`DATA_HOME/runtime/locks/qa-gate-full` — runtime state … this lock is machine-wide' but `return _runtime_dir() / "locks" / "qa-gate-full"` is DATA_HOME-relative.
findings.fix: Put the lock under a per-user OS temp/state dir (e.g. `Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "takkub-qa-gate-lock"`) shared by every instance.

findings.title: check_ingress_mismatch runs for quick/ngrok modes too, producing a spurious 'hostname mismatch' heads-up when an old named-tunnel config.yml is still on disk
findings.scenario: User switched from a named Cloudflare tunnel to Quick tunnel (or ngrok fixed). runtime/tunnel/config.yml from the named setup remains; _start_blocking compares its ingress hostname with the new public_url and sets hostname_mismatch_note, which _remote_start_warning shows in a 'Remote enabled — heads up' box on every Enable even though no named cloudflared is involved.
findings.evidence: __init__.py:193-197 unconditional call; tunnel.py:149-158 only named mode writes config.yml and nothing deletes it on mode change.
findings.fix: Gate the check on `self.config.tunnel.type == "cloudflared"` (named) or delete config.yml when the mode changes.

findings.title: Resume response returns transcript messages without the #441 secret redaction that /api/lead/history applies
findings.scenario: Phone resumes a Lead session whose transcript contains a value a pane once printed from an env file. read_resume_session_messages calls scanner.read_messages directly (notify.py:1987) and the raw list is returned to the phone and painted immediately (app.js:2476-2489); the same messages fetched via /api/lead/history would go through _redact_messages.
findings.evidence: notify.py:1966-1987 has no _redact_messages call; notify.py:1830-1852 read_recent_lead_messages does.
findings.fix: Return `_redact_messages(scanner.read_messages(...))` from read_resume_session_messages.

findings.title: Loopback/public probes use urllib's default opener, which honours system/env proxies, so a proxied Windows box gets a false 'Local loopback probe failed' warning on every Enable/boot
findings.scenario: Machine with a system proxy (IE/WinHTTP settings or HTTP_PROXY env). probe_local GETs http://127.0.0.1:<port>/... through the proxy (urllib's `<local>` bypass only covers dot-less hosts), the proxy refuses loopback, probe_http returns (False, ...), RemoteControl sets local_probe_note and the Settings dialog shows 'Remote enabled — heads up: Local loopback probe failed' although the server is fine.
findings.evidence: diagnostics.py:69 `with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=timeout) as resp` (no ProxyHandler({}) opener); __init__.py:208-211 turns any failure into a user-facing note.
findings.fix: Build the loopback probe with `urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))`.

findings.title: /api/team-preset GET/POST and api.team_preset_status/set are unreachable from the shipped PWA
findings.scenario: No client calls them: app.js has no 'team-preset'/'preset' string at all (only tests exercise the route). The bridge branches at http_server.py:306-321 and api.py:696-746 are dead weight in this subsystem.
findings.evidence: Grep 'team-preset|preset' over remote/static/app.js: no matches; only callers are tests and http_server.py:658/808.
findings.fix: Either wire a Team card into the PWA (Pulse page) or delete the route/api functions and their tests.

findings.title: _read_from_conversation_store_v2 can never return data (no writer for the Lead conversation) and would break the session-exact mirror if it ever did
findings.scenario: read_recent_lead_messages first consults ConversationStore for `conv-<project>-lead`. The only writer is core.conversation.facade.on_pane_done, invoked from orchestrator.done() for teammate roles (orchestrator.py:7936-7948, args=(project_ns, from_role)) and the subagent path (:2574-2579); Lead can never `done` (cli_server.py:549-551), so the lead conversation is never written and the function always falls through. If any future writer populates it, /api/lead/history would return the per-project merged store instead of the pane's current session (contradicting _resolve_claude_jsonl_path's 'exact session only' rule).
findings.evidence: notify.py:1843-1845 `v2_messages = _read_from_conversation_store_v2(project_ns, limit)`; store.py:43-50 conversation_id_for is per (project, role); Grep of append_message/ingest_provider_transcript callers: facade.py only.
findings.fix: Remove the read-through (and the redact detour) or key it by the pane's session_uuid via bind_provider_session before enabling it.

findings.title: --title containing a backslash crashes the build (re.sub replacement escapes) and is not HTML-escaped
findings.scenario: `takkub report build --title "คู่มือ C:\Reports\v2"` -> re.sub treats the f-string replacement as a template -> `re.error: bad escape \R` -> 'build failed: bad escape'. A title with `&`/`<` is also injected raw into <title>.
findings.evidence: report_builder.py:234 `head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{title}</title>", head)`
findings.fix: Use a callable replacement: `re.sub(pat, lambda m: f"<title>{html.escape(title)}</title>", head, count=1)`.

findings.title: Dead code: BackgroundSampler.stop and ResourceGovernor.overloaded() have no callers; git_changes_service.changes_sync has no src caller
findings.scenario: grep across src (excluding the defining modules) finds no `_sampler.stop(`/`.stop()` on the sampler (the daemon thread is never stopped on shutdown), no `.overloaded()` calls (callers read snapshot()['overloaded']), and no `changes_sync(` (workers use _changes_sync_diag). Tests may reference them (test_worktree_manager/test_task_dock not checked for these three).
findings.evidence: resource_governor.py:296 `def stop(self) -> None:`; :498 `def overloaded(self) -> bool:`; git_changes_service.py:199 `def changes_sync(repo_root: Path) -> list[FileChange]:` — no external references in src/agent_takkub.
findings.fix: Either wire BackgroundSampler.stop into orchestrator shutdown (it is the only way to stop the psutil thread) or remove it; drop overloaded() and changes_sync (or keep changes_sync only if a test-only helper is wanted, and say so).

findings.title: Lock held by a dead pane is not reclaimed until the 30-minute TTL — no pid liveness check
findings.scenario: A pane takes `takkub lock web-build`, then the watchdog kills it (#655) or it crashes mid-build. try_acquire only reclaims when `expired(now)` (acquired_ts + ttl_s, default 1800 s) or same holder, so the next pane's `takkub lock web-build --wait 600` polls for 10 min and fails, or a different role waits the full 30 min; `takkub lock` list shows 'held by qa (pid 1234)' for a pid that no longer exists. Lead has to notice and `unlock --force`.
findings.evidence: resource_lock.py:140 `if current is None or current.expired(now) or current.holder == mine.holder:` — `current.pid` is stored (:131) but never checked; format_lock_line :209 reports 'held' purely from expiry.
findings.fix: In try_acquire/release/format_lock_line treat a lock whose `pid` is not alive (os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX / OpenProcess or psutil.pid_exists on Windows) as stale, keeping the stdlib-only constraint with a small platform helper.

findings.title: read() maps any OSError to [] and every writer read-modify-writes the whole file → a transient read failure clobbers the entire message log
findings.scenario: On Windows an AV/indexer sharing violation makes `open()` raise PermissionError for one tick. `read()` returns `[]`; the very next `append`/`_update`/`abandon_unconfirmed_for_role` writes back only its own record, deleting every earlier message for the project.
findings.evidence: role_messages.py:84-86 `records = read_cached(path, _parse_lines, missing=())` / `except OSError: return []`; 130-150 `_append_record` rewrites the full list from that read.
findings.fix: Distinguish 'missing' from 'unreadable' (raise or skip the write on OSError other than FileNotFoundError); append with `open(path, 'a')` instead of rewriting.

findings.title: Accounts refresh latch drops refreshes requested while a probe is in flight — rows that land can predate an add/remove/login
findings.scenario: macOS (keychain `security` probe up to 5s per claude account) or slow disk: open Accounts (refresh #1 running) → immediately '+ เพิ่มบัญชี' → `_accounts_reload_shared_state` → `_accounts_refresh()` returns at 397-398 because `_accounts_refresh_busy` is True → job #1 lands with rows computed before the add → new account missing until the user triggers another action.
findings.evidence: 397-399: `if self._accounts_refresh_busy: return` … `self._accounts_refresh_busy = True`; 405-409 never re-runs a refresh requested meanwhile.
findings.fix: Set a `_accounts_refresh_pending` flag when busy and start another job in `_on_accounts_refreshed` if it is set.

findings.title: Context Strategy / theme write-through ignore the save() bool — UI shows the new choice while nothing was persisted, no feedback
findings.scenario: Knowledge → click 'Deep' while the config file is unwritable (locked/OneDrive) → `core_v2_settings.save_context_strategy` returns False (core_v2_settings.py:196-225 swallows exceptions) → buttons flip to Deep, next open shows the old value. Same shape at settings_window.py:2025-2029: `theme_settings.save` returns bool (theme_settings.py:48-53) so the `except (OSError, ValueError)` never fires on failure and the theme silently reverts on next launch.
findings.evidence: 552: `core_v2_settings.save_context_strategy(value)` (return unused); settings_window.py:2025: `theme_settings.save(mode)` inside try/except that cannot see a False.
findings.fix: Check the bool and show the same QMessageBox.warning the machine-mode/team-language handlers already use (2004, 2039).

findings.title: Module docstring says unknown TAKKUB_SETTINGS_UI values fall back to NEW; resolve() returns LEGACY

findings.scenario: user_actions._open_settings_window (user_actions.py:333-337) is the only production router and opens the new window only when feature_flags.resolve() is NEW; resolve() returns LEGACY for unset/unknown, so the whole package (window, 5 pages, 5 repositories, services, transaction) is unreachable in real use. Inside it, window.py:33 _WIRED equals _SIDEBAR_ENTITIES, so the '(soon)' placeholder loop (124-131) and the else-branch at 173-174 never execute. feature_flags.py:25 docstring says unrecognized values 'fall back to NEW' while the code returns LEGACY.

findings.title: toggle_provider_requested hook is never wired by the shell → new Providers page toggle skips orchestrator.toggle_provider (no Lead broadcast)

findings.title: 'coming soon' placeholder branch is unreachable — every sidebar entity is in _WIRED

findings.title: Status-strip 'Template: X' tooltip points to a control that does not exist — nothing in the UI can change activeTemplate, and the Pipeline page opens on row 0 with no active marker

findings.title: Foldable-section sidebar code is dead by construction (_FOLDABLE_SECTIONS is empty)

findings.title: Save & Apply rollback snapshot omits the team-preset file — a later write failure reports 'rolled back ทุก store' while the preset change stays on disk
findings.scenario: Pick a team-size card + toggle an MCP → Save & Apply → tools-policy write fails (1706/1710 raise OSError) → `_rollback()` restores routing/pipelines/policies/models, but `_team_preset.set_current` (1637) and `note_manual_roles_change` (1670) already rewrote the project's team-preset file, so the project is now on the new preset (or flipped to custom) while the dialog says everything was rolled back.

findings.title: New Role and Add MCP dialogs copy the Settings stylesheet without the #settingsWindow objectName — dialog background stays native/light in dark theme
findings.scenario: Dark theme → Roles page → '+ ตำแหน่งเฉพาะโปรเจค' (or Tools → '+ Add MCP server') → dialog chrome/background renders in the OS palette with dark panels inside, unreadable Cancel/labels — exactly the defect the `_RolePermissionsDialog` docstring (settings_knowledge_design.py:162-169) fixed by using `CockpitDialog`. `_AutoskillsConfirmDialog` (844) and `_LoginPaneDialog` (settings_accounts.py:252) get no stylesheet at all.
findings.evidence: 3121: `dlg.setStyleSheet(self.styleSheet())`; 4099 same; cockpit_theme.py:737: `QDialog#settingsWindow, QWidget#settingsWindow, QDialog#cockpitDialog {{ background: …` — bare `QDialog(self)` has no objectName.
findings.fix: Derive these dialogs from `cockpit_theme.CockpitDialog` (or set objectName 'cockpitDialog') instead of copying the stylesheet.

findings.title: _clear_stale_singleton_locks is a no-op on Windows (Chromium's Windows singleton is a named mutex, not SingletonLock files) — comment and #39 rationale are wrong for the platform it targets
findings.scenario: Called on every browser-role spawn (browser_profile_mcp_config_path :517). On Windows Chromium never creates SingletonLock/SingletonCookie/SingletonSocket (POSIX-only, process_singleton_posix.cc); the profile-in-use error on Windows comes from a still-live chrome.exe holding the named mutex, which unlinking files cannot fix. On POSIX Chromium already reclaims a stale symlink whose pid is dead. So the function never changes an outcome on either OS.
findings.evidence: shared_dev_tools.py:381-397 comment `on Windows they don't self-recover` + `for fname in _SINGLETON_LOCK_FILES: (profile_dir / fname).unlink(missing_ok=True)`.
findings.fix: Delete the helper (and the doctor docstring's 'clears singleton-lock files' caveat, doctor.py:1170-1175) or replace with a real check for a live Chromium holding the profile.

findings.title: audit_new_role_text and audit_existing_role have no callers (docstrings claim the New-Role dialog / Skill Catalog use them)
findings.scenario: settings_window.py and settings_management/repositories/skills.py only import `load_all_role_docs`; no code path computes role overlap for a new/selected role, so the '✓ won't overlap' warning described in the docstrings does not exist in the UI.
findings.evidence:
skill_audit.py:152 `def audit_new_role_text(`
skill_audit.py:182 `def audit_existing_role(`
findings.fix: Wire them into the New-Role dialog / catalog as documented, or delete them.

findings.title: Legacy skill migration runs `git ls-files` synchronously on the Qt main thread at every project-tab open (incl. boot restore)
findings.scenario: main_window._open_project_tab → _ensure_project_skill_links → migrate_legacy_project_skills → _git_tracked_skill_names runs a git subprocess with a 15s timeout on the GUI thread for every tab whose `<root>/.claude/skills` exists. On a repo on a network mount / under AV scanning / with a wedged git, boot freezes up to 15s per restored tab before any pane spawns.
findings.evidence:
skill_scan.py:280-285 `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(project_root), "ls-files", "-z", "--", ".claude/skills"], ..., timeout=_GIT_LS_TIMEOUT_S`
main_window.py:1450 `migrations = skill_scan.migrate_legacy_project_skills(roots[0], project_name)`
findings.fix: Run the migration/link repair on a worker (QRunnable) and only block the spawn on its completion, or cache the tracked-name set per root.

findings.title: _launch_session TOCTOU re-defer drops resume_uuid, so a codex/gemini Lead resumed from the mobile picker silently comes back as a fresh session
findings.scenario: remote/api.py:857 calls orch.spawn(LEAD.name, ..., resume_uuid=<picked>) for a Lead on codex/gemini. If the final InSendMessageEx re-sample fails, _launch_session calls _toctou_redefer WITHOUT resume_uuid (the claude branch at 3883-3892 passes it). The retry spawns with resume_uuid=None -> no `resume`/`--conversation` flag -> the user asked to resume a conversation and gets a blank one, with a 'spawned' success message.
findings.evidence:
self._toctou_redefer(
    role_name, cwd, project, project_ns, _from_auto_respawn, _shard_total,
    pane_tok=pane_tok,
)
findings.fix: Pass resume_uuid=resume_uuid to _toctou_redefer in _launch_session (the parameter already exists and the claude branch uses it).

findings.title: Any exception while writing hook-settings.json silently spawns the claude pane with NO hooks: no Stop/idle signal, no Bash/Edit/Write guard, no rtk, remoteControlAtStartup left to Claude's auto-on default
findings.scenario: ensure_hook_settings_file does config.ensure_runtime() + tmp.write_text + tmp.replace on the first spawn after a content change (rtk toggle, concise/rc roster change) — on Windows a sharing violation (AV/indexer holding the freshly written file) or an unwritable runtime dir raises PermissionError/OSError. The bare `except Exception: pass` leaves settings_argv empty, so the pane boots without `--settings`: pane_guard never runs (the only enforcement of the shell/tool policy, see godfile-map hidden edges), turn-end detection falls back to screen scraping, and Remote Control turns on for a teammate. Nothing is logged.
findings.evidence:
except Exception:
    pass  # hook wiring must never block a spawn
findings.fix: Log the exception with _log_event('hook_settings_write_failed', ...) and _log.exception, and fall back to the last known-good settings path (or an inline minimal settings JSON) instead of no hooks.

findings.title: _project_combo is built and hidden; _refresh_project_list/_on_project_changed only maintain it
findings.scenario: Combo hidden at :589; main_window.py:1317-1339 keep repopulating it and comment 'nothing routes here anymore'.

findings.title: _btn_claude_auth is built, styled, wired and hidden but never placed in the bar

findings.title: _refresh_rtk_button is a no-op `pass` still called from 5 sites
findings.scenario: Called at status_header.py:634 and main_window.py:951/1339/1537/1684; does nothing.

findings.title: DeliveryManager._deliveries is never pruned; snapshot() dumps the full history into the session snapshot every write
findings.scenario: Every assign creates a TaskDelivery (payload included) that stays in `_deliveries` forever; `snapshot()` (orchestrator.py:10204) serialises all of them each time the session snapshot is written, and `cancelled_deliveries`/`expire_stale` scan the whole dict every tick.
findings.evidence: task_delivery.py:252-253 `with self._lock: self._deliveries[delivery.delivery_id] = delivery`; no removal path other than process exit.
findings.fix: Drop terminal deliveries older than a TTL (e.g. in expire_stale) or cap per pane.

findings.title: DeliveryState.WAITING_RESOURCE / create(waiting_resource=True) has no caller
findings.scenario: No call site passes `waiting_resource=True` (grep), so the state is never entered; it only pads `_IN_FLIGHT_STATES`/`_UNDELIVERED_STATES` and the state enum.

findings.title: supersede_for_session can never cancel anything (every delivery is kind='task') → _RESEND_ELIGIBLE_STATES branch and send()'s [delivery-cancelled] notice are dead
findings.scenario: The only `DeliveryManager.create` call is lead_inbox.py:1456 (default kind='task'). In `_cancel_for_session(only_delivered=True)` every kind=='task' delivery either `continue`s or goes to `kept`, so `cancelled` is always empty. orchestrator.py:5097-5131 (`[delivery-cancelled]` notice, `_last_delivery_ids` pop) and task_delivery.py:459-469 are unreachable; `_RESEND_ELIGIBLE_STATES` (124-129) is unused in practice.

findings.fix: Either delete `_RESEND_ELIGIBLE_STATES` + the 459-466 branch and the dead send() notice, or make send() create kind='send' deliveries if that path is meant to be live.

findings.title: With no tab open, TaskDockWidget renders a card for any project whose ledger changes
findings.scenario: User closes the last tab (dock cleared via set_project(None)); a background ledger write (pending done-notice reaper, remote `task reconcile`) emits ledgerChanged for project X and the Task List dock shows X's card even though X has no tab.
findings.evidence: task_dock.py:865 `if self._project is not None and project != self._project: return` falls through when `_project is None`; main_window.py:468 connects `ledgerChanged` -> `refresh_project`; main_window.py:1652 `set_project(None)` on last-tab close.

findings.title: `flush_index_writes` has no caller — INDEX.md background writes are never drained at shutdown
findings.scenario: Assign/done then quit the cockpit immediately: the daemon `ledger-index-writer` thread may be killed before `_atomic_write` runs, so INDEX.md lags `.ledger-state.json` until the next assign/done. Function exists for exactly this but nothing (app shutdown, `end_session`) calls it.

findings.fix: Call `task_ledger.flush_index_writes()` from app shutdown / `end_session` (next to `flush_events_log`), or delete it and make the state save regen INDEX synchronously on exit.

findings.title: Fix-loop ceiling API (`MAX_FIX_LOOP_ATTEMPTS`, `FixLoopDecision`, `check_fix_loop_ceiling`, `FixLoopTracker`) and its routing_planner re-exports have no production caller
findings.scenario: The #585 round-3 fix-loop ceiling is never consulted by the orchestrator's verify-fail handoff path; the 2-round ceiling the docs promise is enforced only by prose in Lead docs, not by code.

findings.fix: Either wire `FixLoopTracker` into `_build_verify_fail_handoff` (count attempts per failure signature and stop at MAX_FIX_LOOP_ATTEMPTS) or delete the block, the re-exports and tests/test_fix_loop_ceiling.py.

findings.title: TerminalWidget.clear() and request_buffer_text() have no production callers
findings.scenario: Dead by construction: `clear()` (L577-581) is never called (only `clear_view`/`reset` are); `request_buffer_text()` (L673-687) is referenced only by tools/spike_pane_discard_ram.py:125.
