findings.title: Wheel/Ctrl+0 zoom not stored in _font_px, so discard/reattach reverts the font (and idle flag is never re-asserted)
findings.scenario: User Ctrl+wheel-zooms a teammate pane to 14 pt, switches project tab for >25 s (pane discarded), switches back -> page reloads -> `_on_page_ready` re-applies `self._font_px` (still the pre-zoom value from `_restore_font_size`/None) -> font snaps back. Same reload resets JS `idle` to false but `AgentPane._last_idle` still says True, so `_sync_idle_flag` never resends `termSetIdle(true)` and local echo stays off until the ready state toggles.
findings.evidence: terminal_widget.py:667-671 `_on_font_zoomed` only emits `fontSizeChanged`, never updates `self._font_px`; L767-768 `if self._font_px is not None: runJavaScript(termSetFontSize(self._font_px))`. agent_pane.py:729-731 `if idle == self._last_idle: return`.
findings.fix: In `_on_font_zoomed` set `self._font_px = int(pt * 1.333)`; in `_on_page_ready` also re-send idle/lock/newline state (or have AgentPane reset `_last_idle = None` when the terminal reports a fresh page).

findings.title: session_project_dir_for_cwd has no callers
findings.scenario: Only referenced in docstrings (spawn_engine.py:481, remote/notify.py:757); every real caller uses session_project_dirs_for_cwd / find_session_by_uuid.
findings.evidence: token_meter.py:169 `def session_project_dir_for_cwd(config_dir, cwd) -> Path:`
findings.fix: Delete and update the two docstrings.

findings.title: npm self-update click path compares versions by string equality (unlike the chip) → offers an 'update' when metadata is unreadable ('?') or the local build is newer
findings.scenario: Installed build where `importlib.metadata.version('agent-takkub')` fails (current='?') or local wheel is ahead of the registry (fresh publish lag / prerelease): chip correctly stays green (`compare_versions(cur, latest) < 0` at 780) but clicking it shows 'agent-takkub vX is available (you have ?)' and, on OK, runs `npm install -g agent-takkub@latest` + a restart for no reason (or a downgrade).
findings.evidence: update_panel.py:698 `if latest == current:` vs 780 `if npm.get("ok") and cur and latest and compare_versions(cur, latest) < 0:`.
findings.fix: Use `compare_versions(current, latest) >= 0` in `_checked` and treat `current == '?'` as 'cannot determine' (warning, no install).

findings.title: Dead: ClaudeUpdateCheckWorker + the Claude-CLI native update dialog chain in update_panel.py + 10 helpers in claude_update.py have no caller
findings.scenario: Nothing instantiates `ClaudeUpdateCheckWorker` (only its own docstring mentions it), so `update_panel._on_claude_update_check_done` (429), `_show_claude_update_dialog` (459), `_count_live_claude_panes` (554), `_confirm_and_apply_claude_update` (570), `status_header._claude_update_busy` (479) and, in claude_update.py, `CHANGELOG_URL` (47), `COCKPIT_CLAUDE_USAGE` (52), `slice_changelog` (133), `build_analysis_prompt` (157), `parse_verdict` (186), `build_issue_title` (209), `build_issue_body` (220), `fetch_changelog` (278), `analyze_compatibility` (290), `build_updater_script` (322) are unreachable in the app; update_panel.py:423-427 already admits 'not wired to any widget'. `update_panel._run_update_check` (415) also has no caller. Live in claude_update.py: `_run`, `_npm`, `parse_version`, `compare_versions`, `current_version`, `latest_version`, `apply_update` (used by boot_flow.py and provider_update.py:334/369).
findings.evidence: grep across src for `ClaudeUpdateCheckWorker|_on_claude_update_check_done|_show_claude_update_dialog|_confirm_and_apply_claude_update|_count_live_claude_panes|build_updater_script|analyze_compatibility|fetch_changelog|slice_changelog|parse_verdict|build_issue_title|build_issue_body` hits only their definitions, their mutual calls, the docstring at update_worker.py:117-118, and the comments at update_panel.py:423-427 / status_header.py:476-479; `_run_update_check` hits only update_panel.py:415.
findings.fix: Delete the worker, the four update_panel methods, `_claude_update_busy`, `_run_update_check`, and the ten claude_update helpers (keep the live seven); a separate audit should drop the tests that pin them.

findings.title: _UsageLock spins forever (no sleep, no deadline) when os.open keeps raising PermissionError and no lock file exists
findings.scenario: Ledger dir (RUNTIME_DIR/usage or TAKKUB_USAGE_LEDGER_DIR) exists but is write-denied (protected folder / read-only mount / ACL). os.open raises PermissionError -> stat() raises FileNotFoundError -> `continue` bypasses both the deadline check and the sleep -> 100% CPU busy loop. Reached on the Qt main thread via Settings > Usage (_render_usage -> query_usage -> rollup_daily) whenever an account dir already exists -> Settings hangs.
findings.evidence: L182-184: `try: age = _time.time() - self._path.stat().st_mtime` / `except OSError: continue`   deadline check only at L192.
findings.fix: On stat failure fall through to the deadline check and sleep (or break fail-open immediately).

findings.title: Quota sample dedup only compares the last row, so multi-window providers append duplicate samples every poll that reuses cached data
findings.scenario: ProviderUsageStore polls claude every 300 s; fetch_usage_shared often returns the SAME cached UsageData (same fetched_at) -- always during a 429 backoff. _record_quota_ledger writes windows in order five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet; on the next poll the last row is seven_day_sonnet so five_hour(ts) is not a repeat -> all three rows re-appended. Same for codex primary/secondary and gemini's N tiers. 'Samples' in Settings > Usage / `takkub usage` is inflated and quota-*.jsonl grows ~2x (also slows finding F7).
findings.evidence: L435: `if last is not None and last.get("window") == window and last.get("ts") == ts_iso:`   provider_usage.py:1678-1686 loops `for w in windows or (): usage_ledger.record_quota_sample(...)`
findings.fix: Dedup per window (scan tail rows until a row with the same window is found, or keep a per-(provider,account,window) last-ts map in _record_quota_ledger).

findings.title: default_provider() is never read in production; set_default_provider() writes a 'default_provider' field nothing consumes
findings.scenario: user_actions.py:1059 calls set_default_provider(project, provider) on the 'Lead ใช้ provider' switch, but the only readers of default_provider() are tests (test_user_actions_provider_switch.py:42-79, test_user_profile.py:260-264). The actual routing effect comes from provider_config.save_role_overrides on the next line (user_actions.py:1060), so the per-project 'default_provider' key in user-profile.json is write-only state.
findings.evidence: user_profile.py:479 `def default_provider(project: str) -> str:`; user_actions.py:1059-1060 `user_profile.set_default_provider(project, provider)` / `provider_config.save_role_overrides({"lead": provider}, project, scope=["lead"])`
findings.fix: Remove default_provider/set_default_provider and the call at user_actions.py:1059 (routing.json already carries the Lead provider), or make status_header/provider_config read it if it is meant to be authoritative.

findings.title: bootstrap_default_profile rmtree's an existing prod claude-config that has no marker and no .credentials.json — wipes sessions/todos for API-key users or pre-marker installs
findings.scenario: Installed cockpit whose DATA_HOME/claude-config was created by the older synchronous full-tree copy (no .bootstrap-complete marker) or by a user who authenticates via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / has logged out (no .credentials.json). On the next boot dest.exists() is True, neither guard file exists, and on Windows there is no Keychain check, so shutil.rmtree(dest) deletes projects/, todos/, memory, plugins written by prod panes, then re-clones a bounded subset (10 sessions/project, no credentials) from ~/.claude. app.py:956 swallows every exception so nothing is surfaced.
findings.evidence: user_profile.py:1076-1083 `if (dest / _BOOTSTRAP_MARKER).exists() or (dest / ".credentials.json").exists(): return False` ... `shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)  # torn from an earlier interrupted clone`
findings.fix: Treat a dest that contains any real user data (projects/*.jsonl, todos/, settings.json) as a real profile: write the marker and return False instead of deleting; only rmtree when dest is empty or contains a stale .partial layout.

findings.title: In-process first-line dedup drops the ENTIRE done note (sessions, knowledge base, vault, Lead brief) for any later note with the same first line
findings.scenario: A role whose done notes start with a fixed template line ('## สรุป', 'Done:', 'qa-gate FAIL:' …). After the first report, every later `takkub done` from that (project, role) hashes the same first line → orchestrator._save_decision_note (line 8920) returns None → no runtime/sessions file, no knowledge-base distill, no vault mirror, and the note never reaches Lead's recent-session brief — for the whole cockpit process lifetime. Sampled 55 real notes on this machine (2026-09-11, 2026-08-22): first lines are distinctive, so this is latent here, not observed.
findings.evidence:
vault_mirror.py:232-238 `first_line = scrubbed.splitlines()[0] if scrubbed else ""` … `if key in _DEDUP_HASHES: return True`
orchestrator.py:8920 `if _is_dedup_note(project, role, note): return None`
findings.fix: Hash the whole scrubbed note (or first ~200 chars) and add a time window (e.g. 60s) instead of a process-lifetime set.

findings.title: PROBLEM_DESCRIPTIONS has no reader in src
findings.scenario: The dict is defined and mentioned in a docstring (line 71) but no caller maps a problem key to its description; doctor.py:1715-1722 and orchestrator.py:12044-12060 use the raw key / repair() message instead.
findings.evidence: venv_integrity.py:61 `PROBLEM_DESCRIPTIONS = {`
findings.fix: Remove it, or use it in doctor's finding text for the venv check.

findings.title: `takkub verify` Python branch runs bare `python` (no venv/`python3` resolution) and the command is no longer referenced by any role or Lead doc
findings.scenario: `detect_stack` emits `["python", "-m", "pytest", …]`/`ruff` with a bare `python`; on macOS (no `python` shim) or Windows with the Store stub, `run_checks` (l.429) raises FileNotFoundError → every Python check reports FAIL. The only remaining references to `takkub verify` are docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:105 and a 2026-07-12 qa report; qa-gate.py replaced it (#325) and no `.claude/agents/*.md` or docs/lead mention it — the subcommand (cli.py:6410) plus tests/test_verify.py and tests/test_verify_fail_hint.py keep dead paths alive.
findings.evidence: l.58-62 `Check(\n    name="pytest",\n    cmd=["python", "-m", "pytest", "tests/", "-x", "--tb=short"],` ; grep '*.md' for `takkub verify` → only docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:105 and docs/qa-reports/2026-07-12-full-system-review.md.
findings.fix: Either retire `takkub verify` (delete cmd_verify, the python branch of detect_stack, run_checks/format_summary, and tests/test_verify*.py, keeping node_checks/pm_* used by qa_gate) or make it delegate to `qa_gate.run_gate`.

findings.title: _stuck_git_op assumes `.git` is a directory — silently disabled when the primary checkout is itself a linked worktree
findings.scenario: Lead's project root is a `git worktree add`-created checkout (e.g. the manually named prodtest-taktempmain base checkout from memory). There `.git` is a file, so `Path(git_root)/'.git'/'MERGE_HEAD'` is never a file → merge_isolated/clean_isolated never refuse on a stuck merge (#575 protection off) and the post-abort check at :2021 reports 'abort แล้ว' even when MERGE_HEAD is still present in the real gitdir.
findings.evidence: worktree_manager.py:383-386 `git_dir = Path(git_root) / ".git"` / `if (git_dir / name).is_file():` — no `git rev-parse --git-dir` / `--git-path` resolution.
findings.fix: Resolve the gitdir via `self._run(["-C", git_root, "rev-parse", "--git-path", name])` (or `--absolute-git-dir`) instead of hardcoding `<root>/.git/<marker>`.

findings.title: Dead code: safe_remove / force_remove / _unlink_links / is_dirty / is_dirty_at / uncommitted_count / uncommitted_count_at / _expand_dir_entry / WorktreeConfig.is_empty have no callers outside tests — and safe_remove carries a latent branch-loss bug
findings.scenario: No src caller for any of: safe_remove (:1730), force_remove (:2284), _unlink_links (:1180, only used by those two), is_dirty (:1229) / is_dirty_at (:1233), uncommitted_count (:1377) / uncommitted_count_at (:1372), _expand_dir_entry (:2444, superseded by _expand_dir_entries), WorktreeConfig.is_empty (:182). _finalize_worktree (orchestrator.py:4683) never removes a worktree (#161), so the 2-tier destroy the module docstring advertises is unreachable. Latent bug if ever revived: safe_remove deletes the checkout dir first (:1748) and only then calls `self.commit_count(info)` (:1764), which runs `git -C <deleted path> rev-list` → fails → returns 0 → `branch -D` runs unconditionally, force-deleting a branch that still has unmerged commits. force_remove likewise runs `branch -D` (:2293) before checking `removed` (:2294). Tests exercising these: tests/test_worktree_manager.py (25 refs), tests/test_worktree_assign.py (8 refs).
findings.evidence: worktree_manager.py:1764-1765 `if self.commit_count(info) == 0:` / `self._run(["-C", info.git_root, "branch", "-D", info.branch], None)` after :1748 `removed, disk_msg, leftover = remove_worktree_tree(Path(info.path))`; grep `\.safe_remove\(|\.force_remove\(` in src → only worktree_manager.py docstrings.
findings.fix: Delete safe_remove/force_remove/_unlink_links/is_dirty/is_dirty_at/uncommitted_count/uncommitted_count_at/_expand_dir_entry/is_empty and the tests that only cover them; if a caller is ever added, compute commit_count before the dir delete and delete the branch only when rm.ok.
